background.heading: Entity identification
background.text: UK entity is Abbott Diabetes Care Limited (Companies House 02548046, Witney), formerly MediSense (U.K.) Holding Ltd, renamed 2005 following Abbott's 2004 acquisition of TheraSense/MediSense. Not found on NHS Supply Chain (searched Libre, FreeStyle Libre, Abbott Diabetes — zero results) — confirms FreeStyle Libre is dispensed via NHS prescription (Drug Tariff), not the hospital consumables catalogue. Compatible with third-party closed-loop systems (mylife CamAPS FX/YpsoPump) per Abbott's own technical documentation.

suppliers._specialitiesEvidence: 20/07/2026: added Blood and transfusion for Alinity s-series (donor blood/plasma screening -- HBsAg, anti-HCV, anti-HBc, HTLV I/II, Chagas) -- already bundled into the 'Alinity ci / h / s / m' product line but had no matching speciality tag; this family genuinely sits apart from general pathology, likely procured directly by NHS Blood and Transplant rather than the general NHS Supply Chain catalogue. Added BinaxNOW/Determine/Actim/SureStep -- the former Alere rapid-diagnostics range (Abbott acquired Alere Oct 2017), confirmed live on NHS Supply Chain under a distinct legal entity 'ABBOTT RAPID DIAGNOSTICS LTD' (separate from 'ABBOTT LABORATORIES LIMITED (BERKS)', which covers i-STAT/ARCHITECT/Alinity) -- kept as one combined 'Abbott Diagnostics' record since both are diagnostics-not-diabetes, even though NHS Supply Chain itself treats them as two legal suppliers. CONFIRMED clean separation from Abbott Diabetes Care: FreeStyle Libre is supplied via the NHS Drug Tariff (Part IXR)/community prescribing, an entirely different UK procurement route from the hospital Supply Chain catalogue used by this record -- no overlap or double-counting risk between the two supplier records. ARCHITECT is being gradually migrated to Alinity ci (both still live on NHS Supply Chain today) -- described as a managed transition, not a discontinuation, don't flag ARCHITECT as withdrawn.

background.heading: Product attribution correction
background.text: Removed 'SureStep' — this appears to be a LifeScan brand (originally Johnson & Johnson, now Platinum Equity-owned), not an Abbott product; no evidence found that Abbott ever marketed it. Current NHS point-of-care glucose testing under Abbott runs via FreeStyle Precision Pro/i-STAT instead. Diagnostics products span two UK entities: Abbott Laboratories Limited (00329102, Maidenhead, trades as 'Abbott Diagnostics' — Alinity/Architect/i-STAT) and Abbott Rapid Diagnostics Ltd (01716581, also Maidenhead — Afinion/ID NOW/Determine/Actim distribution). Both confirmed distinct from Abbott Medical U.K. Ltd (cardiac/EP) and Abbott Diabetes Care Ltd (FreeStyle Libre), already recorded separately in this dataset.

background.heading: Acquisition
background.text: Axonics, Inc. was acquired by Boston Scientific, completed 15/11/2024 ($3.7bn equity value) -- no longer an independent NASDAQ company, now 'Axonics, a Boston Scientific company'. Bulkamid came via the Contura Ltd acquisition, which closed 25/02/2021 (not 2022) for up to $235m (SEC filings). Two UK Companies House entities: Axonics Modulation Technologies U.K. Limited (09622653, the SNM business) and Axonics Women's Health Limited (03145216, formerly Contura Limited, the Bulkamid business) -- same registered office, distinct SIC codes. NICE guidance: MTG50/HealthTech 554 (SNM for refractory OAB), MIB259 (SNM for faecal incontinence); IPG138/HealthTech 86 covers urethral bulking procedures generically, not Bulkamid specifically. Do not confuse with an unrelated dissolved 'Axonics Limited' (Swansea, dissolved 2012).
background.source: SEC 8-K / Companies House 09622653 & 03145216 / NICE MTG50 & MIB259

alerts.text: Physidia (home dialysis machine) is manufactured by a French company, Physidia — B. Braun Avitum is its exclusive UK distributor, not the manufacturer; worth noting the distinction. UK entity B. Braun Medical Limited (Companies House 02296559, Sheffield) confirmed family-controlled at UK level; ultimate parent B. Braun Melsungen AG (Germany) remains privately held and family-controlled (CEO Anna Maria Braun, 6th generation), no public listing. B. Braun SE fully acquired True Digital Surgery (Sept 2025, digital 3D robotic surgical microscopy), feeding directly into the already-listed Aesculap Aeos platform. US FDA recalls in 2025-2026 (Lactated Ringer's/Sodium Chloride particulate matter, Microbore Extension Set mislabelling) are US-market actions — no equivalent UK/MHRA recall was found, so these should not be presented as a UK-market issue without separate confirmation.

deepDive.tagline: Family-controlled since 1839, still unlisted · CEO Anna Maria Braun, sixth generation · UK entity B. Braun Medical Limited, Sheffield, incorporated 1988 as Aesculap Limited
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: B. Braun is the biggest supplier on this Hub's framework data and it is privately held by one family, which changes how it behaves. Group sales reached €9.4bn in 2025, growth of 5.1% at constant currency, right inside the 5 to 7 percent corridor the company sets itself, and it put more than €800m back into plant and technology in the same year, including a €145m automated infusion consumables factory at Melsungen. There are no quarterly analysts to satisfy, which is why you hear "long-term" from them and mean it. The UK board is also in the middle of a turnover: Michael Parden, the Sheffield-born UK Managing Director appointed in 2021, resigned as a director on 21 April 2026, Christiane Jandt was appointed the same day, and Simon Topliss was appointed on 3 August 2026, eleven days ago. Ask what the UK leadership is being asked to do differently.

prose: B. Braun publishes a clean five-year sales series, which most of this market does not: €7,859.8m (2021), €8,499.8m (2022), €8,755.0m (2023), €9,136.9m (2024), €9,396.4m (2025). That is steady rather than spectacular, and the company frames it against a self-set corridor of 5 to 7 percent currency-adjusted growth, which it hit in 2025 at 5.1 percent. The 2.8 percent figure quoted in some coverage is the same year measured in group currency, before the currency adjustment; both are B. Braun's own numbers and they are not in conflict.

The 2025 sales split by division was Hospital Care €5,091m, Aesculap €2,374m and Avitum €1,901m, so infusion, nutrition and pain therapy is more than half the business, surgical is a quarter and dialysis and chronic care the rest. By region, Western Europe was €2,021m against North America's €2,397m and Germany's €1,441m. There is no UK-only sales line in the group report, and B. Braun Medical Limited files full accounts at Companies House as a PDF with no tagged profit and loss account, so no UK turnover figure is stated here rather than estimated.

Profitability moved more than sales did. EBITDA margin went from 11.9 to 13.0 percent and gross margin from 39.1 to 40.5 percent, which the company attributes to portfolio management, cost control and plant efficiency. The 2026 guidance is 5 to 7 percent currency-adjusted sales growth, EBITDA margin above 13 percent and return on sales above 5 percent.

ownership: B. Braun has never been sold and has never listed. It was founded in Melsungen, Germany in 1839 and remains controlled by the Braun family; Anna Maria Braun, the sixth generation, has been group CEO since 2019. The group holding is B. Braun SE. That matters commercially: there is no quarterly earnings cycle, no activist shareholder and no separation story of the kind running at several of its listed competitors, and the company's own language, a 5 to 7 percent corridor held over years rather than a growth target for next quarter, follows from that.

The UK operating entity is B. Braun Medical Limited, company number 02296559, incorporated 14 September 1988 and confirmed active at Companies House. It was originally WF 156 Limited, then Aesculap-Skidmore Holdings Limited from February 1989, Aesculap Limited from January 1991, and took the B. Braun Medical name in May 1998, which is why the Aesculap surgical brand and the B. Braun infusion brand sit inside the same UK company. Registered office is Brookdale Road, Thorncliffe Park Estate, Chapeltown, Sheffield S35 2PW. A second UK company, B Braun Sterilog Limited (01472814, incorporated 1980), also exists on the register; this repo records that match as probable rather than confirmed, because no B. Braun-published source read here names it.

press.text: Simon Paul Topliss appointed a director of B. Braun Medical Limited. The fourth change to the UK board inside 28 months, following Craig Cannings (May 2024), Christiane Jandt and Michael Parden's resignation (both 21 April 2026). If you are interviewing into the UK business, the board that hires you is not the board that set this year's plan.

Group sales €9,396m, up 5.1% at constant currency and 2.8% in group currency, with all three divisions and all six business regions growing. EBITDA margin 13.0%, return on sales before tax 4.9%. Guidance for 2026 is 5 to 7 percent currency-adjusted growth, EBITDA margin above 13 percent, return on sales above 5 percent.

B. Braun fully acquired US microsurgery specialist True Digital Surgery, extending the portfolio for robotically assisted 3D microscopy in neurosurgery, spine and ENT. Relevant if the role is anywhere near Aesculap Aeos or digital surgery.

The €145m automated ACTIVE plant for single-use infusion therapy consumables opened at Melsungen, using driverless transport, robotics and intelligent warehousing. Supply resilience is a live NHS procurement question and this is the concrete answer to it.

Foundation laid at Tuttlingen for the Technology Factory, a long-term rebuild of surgical instrument pre-production designed for carbon-neutral operation using geothermal, process waste heat and photovoltaics. Useful if the trust you are selling into has a net-zero supplier requirement.
OMNI plus launched, bringing acute dialysis and apheresis together on one platform for acute kidney failure. Avitum's headline launch of the year.

Health care centre portfolio expanded by acquisition in Romania and Czechia, increasing group dialysis capacity. B. Braun both sells dialysis equipment and runs dialysis clinics, which is unusual and worth understanding before an Avitum interview.

hiring: No rolling count of UK vacancies could be read from a B. Braun-published source in this run, so none is given here rather than estimated. What is checkable on Glassdoor, read 14/08/2026: one live UK listing, a Medical Device Product Specialist (Sales) role covering Central England, and the UK entity is sized at 1,001 to 5,000 employees with a single office location on that profile. Sheffield is both the registered office and, on the company's own Glassdoor photographs, the head office site, so the UK business is a single-site commercial and manufacturing operation rather than a distributed one.

glassdoor.scale: /5 on Glassdoor UK, B. Braun Medical (UK) specifically, not the group (90 ratings)
glassdoor.summary: Unusually, there is a UK-only profile here rather than just a global one, so this is the right number to use. 4.0 is above the 3.4 manufacturing-industry average and above the UK-entity ratings of several direct competitors. 73% would recommend to a friend. Category scores: culture and values 3.8, work/life balance 3.8, diversity and inclusion 3.7, compensation and benefits 3.6, career opportunities 3.5, senior management 3.4. The soft measures beat the hard ones, which fits the family-owned, long-tenure picture, and business outlook is the weak spot at 57% positive. On interviews, 80% of candidates rate the experience positive and average difficulty is 2.6 out of 5.

deepDive.interview: Know which division the role sits in and say the word: Hospital Care (infusion, nutrition, pain), Aesculap (surgical) or Avitum (dialysis, wound, stoma, continence). They are run separately from the executive board down and a candidate who talks about "B. Braun's portfolio" as one thing sounds like they read the website once. Lead on family ownership as a commercial argument, not a nice fact: no listing, no quarterly cycle, a self-set 5 to 7 percent corridor held for years, and more than €800m of capital investment in 2025 including a €145m automated plant. That is a supply-continuity story, and continuity of supply is what NHS procurement has actually been buying since 2022. Be ready on the UK board changes, three director appointments and one resignation since May 2024, with the most recent on 3 August 2026. On the Avitum side, understand that B. Braun runs dialysis clinics as well as selling dialysis machines, so it is a competitor to some of its own customers in that segment. And do not describe Physidia as a B. Braun product: B. Braun Avitum is the UK distributor, not the manufacturer.

news.text: 9 Feb 2026: BD completed the spin-off of its Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business and its combination with Waters Corporation. The business was valued at $18.8bn on Waters' 6 February closing price and BD received $4bn in cash; BD shareholders ended up holding 39.2% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Flow cytometry, single-cell multiomics, microbiology, molecular diagnostics and point-of-care testing now trade as Waters Biosciences and Waters Advanced Diagnostics. Specimen management, including Vacutainer, was retained and sits in BD's Medical Essentials segment.

6 Aug 2026: Q3 FY2026 revenue $5.0bn, up 5.4% as reported and 4.4% currency-neutral; adjusted diluted EPS $3.23; full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $12.62 to $12.72. The first full quarter reported as the four-segment company, with all four segments growing.

31 Jul 2026: BD issued a US nationwide recall of specific lots of the BD Intraosseous Vascular Access System Needle Sets after reports of difficulty removing the obturator; the FDA classified it Class I. Affected lots were distributed 30/09/2024 to 12/06/2026. The BD Intraosseous Powered Driver is not affected. No corresponding UK field safety notice appears in this Hub's gov.uk and NHS Supply Chain alert feed as at 15/08/2026, so UK stock impact is Not verified — check the MHRA alerts page before raising it with a trust.

deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: BD is not the company most reps still describe. On 9 February 2026 it completed the spin-off of its Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business into Waters Corporation, in a Reverse Morris Trust that valued the business at $18.8bn and handed BD $4bn in cash. Flow cytometry, microbiology, molecular and point-of-care diagnostics went with it and now trade as Waters Biosciences and Waters Advanced Diagnostics. What is left, which BD calls New BD, is four segments — Medical Essentials, Connected Care, BioPharma Systems and Interventional — and the company describes itself as one of the world's largest pure-play medtech businesses. It is trading well on that narrower base: revenue of $4,983m in the quarter to 30 June 2026, up 5.4%, with full-year guidance raised on 6 August 2026. Walk in talking about BD's diagnostics portfolio and you will be a year out of date.

prose: No UK-only turnover can be read for this company. Becton, Dickinson U.K. Limited files full accounts at Companies House, but as a PDF with no tagged figures, so identifying the turnover line by position would be a guess rather than a reading, and nothing is taken from it. Its last accounts were made up to 30 September 2025; the next are due by 30 June 2027, and its most recent confirmation statement is dated 14 August 2026. Everything below is therefore group-wide, as reported by BD in its own filings.

Group revenue was $20,178m in FY2024 and $21,840m in FY2025, both years ended 30 September and both as reported before the separation. That basis stops there. After the Waters deal BD restated FY2025 to $18,544m on a continuing-operations basis, and reports the nine months to 30 June 2026 at $14,183m against $13,539m, up 4.8%. Full-year FY2026 guidance, raised on 6 August 2026, is low single-digit revenue growth and adjusted diluted EPS of $12.62 to $12.72.

The number worth asking about is the cost of getting there. The nine months to 30 June 2026 carry $605m of restructuring charges, including $450m of non-cash impairments booked when BD committed to exit activities and projects that no longer fit its Excellence Unleashed strategy. A company simplifying that hard is one where it is fair to ask what the UK commercial structure looks like on the other side.

ownership: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) is a US public company listed on the New York Stock Exchange as BDX, headquartered at 1 Becton Drive, Franklin Lakes, New Jersey. There is no parent above it. Tom Polen is chairman, chief executive and president, and signed both the February 2026 separation release and the August 2026 results release in that capacity.

The group has been deliberately reshaped rather than grown whole: BD's own account of the last several years is three substantial non-core divestments and more than twenty tuck-in acquisitions, ending with the Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions separation on 9 February 2026, which it calls the final milestone of its BD 2025 strategy. The structure was a Reverse Morris Trust: the business was spun into a separate entity that merged with a Waters subsidiary, BD shareholders received about 0.135 Waters shares per BD share and ended up with 39.2% of the combined company, and BD took $4bn in cash, earmarking $2bn for an accelerated share repurchase and $2bn for debt repayment.

The UK operating entity is Becton, Dickinson U.K. Limited, company number 00852702, incorporated 25 June 1965 and active, registered office 1030 Eskdale Road, Winnersh Triangle, Wokingham, Berkshire RG41 5TS, SIC 32500, manufacture of medical and dental instruments and supplies. BD also runs a manufacturing site at Plymouth, which appears in its own careers listings.

press.text: FY2025 results: revenue $21.8bn, up 8.2% as reported and 2.9% organic; adjusted diluted EPS $14.40, up 9.6%. BD states the Waters combination is on track to complete around the end of the first quarter of calendar 2026.

The spin-off of Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions completes and the business combines with Waters Corporation. BD receives $4bn cash, its shareholders take 39.2% of Waters, and the business is valued at $18.8bn on the previous day's Waters closing price. BD calls itself a pure-play medtech company from this point.

Waters names its new divisions the same day: Waters Biosciences is the former BD Biosciences (flow cytometry, single-cell multiomics) and Waters Advanced Diagnostics is the former BD Diagnostic Solutions plus the Waters clinical business (microbiology, molecular, multiplex, automation, point of care). Anything in those categories is no longer a BD conversation.

MHRA Class 2 medicines recall EL(26)A/34 for ChloraPrep 1mL applicators, a potential sterility breach across all lots with expiry to 05/2029. The fourth ChloraPrep recall since May 2025 and the most live UK-facing issue on this account. Full detail and links are in this supplier's alerts.
The Venflon IV cannula with wings, 14G to 22G, completes its NHS Supply Chain delisting, having been progressively withdrawn since January 2025. Any trust still using it has had to convert.

Q3 FY2026 results: revenue $4,983m, up 5.4%, described by BD as its first full quarter as New BD. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $12.62 to $12.72. Highlights named a Vizient Innovative Technology contract for the BD CentroVena One insertion system, the launch of the Elyra thulium fibre laser system in kidney stone care, and a collaboration with Brazilian pharmaceutical company EMS on the Vystra injection pen for semaglutide.

hiring: BD runs its own careers site at jobs.bd.com, which carries UK listings including manufacturing, engineering, field service and sales roles at the Plymouth site. No vacancy count, salary band or UK headcount was verified in this session, so none is stated here.
marketPosition: BD describes itself as one of the world's largest pure-play medical technology companies, with more than 60,000 employees. That is the company's own claim, not an audited market share, and no verified market-share figure was found in this session, so none is given. The strongest UK-specific evidence of scale is procurement footprint: named supplier on 18 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, spanning IV cannulation and vascular access, infusion pumps and administration sets, needle-free connectors, extension sets, blood collection, specimen management, surgical mesh, urology and endoscopy consumables, renal replacement, skin cleansing and pathology services, all confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs.

⚠️ Read this supplier's product list with the separation in mind. The Hub's captured range for BD still includes flow cytometry (FACSLyric, FACSAria, FACSymphony, LSRFortessa), BACTEC, BD MAX, Kiestra, Phoenix and Veritor, all of which transferred to Waters on 09/02/2026. Whether individual UK supply contracts and NHS Supply Chain framework places for those lines have novated to a Waters entity is Not verified: it would be settled by the framework's own supplier list at the next refresh, or by NHS Supply Chain's catalogue. Until that is checked, do not tell a customer BD supplies them.
deepDive.interview: This is a company that has just made itself smaller on purpose, so the interesting questions are about focus rather than growth. Know which of the four segments the role sits in — Medical Essentials, Connected Care, BioPharma Systems or Interventional — because they are separately managed and the diagnostics conversation has left the building. On UK ground, the two live issues are the ChloraPrep recall sequence, four since May 2025, and the Venflon delisting that completed on 31 July 2026: both are switching conversations happening in trusts right now, and being able to talk about continuity of licensed supply is worth more than product knowledge. The $605m of restructuring in the first nine months of FY2026 is a fair, non-hostile thing to raise as a question about what Excellence Unleashed means for the UK team.

alerts.text: IMPORTANT SAFETY FLAG: the ACCOLADE pacemaker/CRT-P family (Accolade, Proponent, Essentio, Altura 2, Visionist, Valitude) is subject to an FDA Class I recall/correction affecting over 1 million devices — a high battery-impedance issue causing an unexpected 'Safety Mode'; as of 18 March 2026 Boston Scientific reported 4 deaths and 2,557 serious injuries. The fix is a software update (SMR6, released March 2026), not device explant — worth surfacing to any rep positioning this pacemaker family. Separately, the Carotid Wallstent Monorail Endoprosthesis was recalled in 2025 for a manufacturing defect (narrow inner lumen risking stroke). UK entity: Boston Scientific Limited (Companies House 02729626, London) — a differently-numbered 'Boston Scientific (UK) Limited' (04949633) is dissolved since Oct 2023, don't use it. Boston Scientific has an active pending $14.5bn acquisition of Penumbra, Inc. (mechanical thrombectomy) announced 2026 but not yet closed — don't add Penumbra products until completion is confirmed. Other recent acquisitions (Cortex cardiac mapping, Bolt Medical, Nalu Medical, SoundCath, Intera Oncology) are agreed/closing through 2025-2026 but not yet reflected as flagship UK-commercial products.

deepDive.tagline: US-parented cardiology, endoscopy and neuromodulation major, on 7 confirmed NHS Supply Chain frameworks -- wholly owned by Boston Scientific Corporation (Delaware) through a UK subsidiary with a single active UK-registered director
deepDive.lede: Boston Scientific Limited is the UK trading entity of a $5bn-a-quarter US medtech group, and its own Companies House record is a reminder that a subsidiary this size can still run on a very small UK board: one active director, Emily Marie Woodworth, appointed 16 August 2024 alongside a corporate nominee secretary, and no other UK-resident officer on the register. Its parent, Boston Scientific Corporation of Delaware, has held 75% or more of the shares and the right to appoint or remove directors since notification on 6 April 2016. Seven NHS Supply Chain frameworks are confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, spanning cardiology, neuromodulation, endoscopy, theatre equipment, radiotherapy, surgical mesh and men's and women's health implants. The group itself is mid-acquisition: a $14.5bn deal to buy Penumbra, Inc., announced 15 January 2026, was still awaiting regulatory clearance as of 29 July 2026 and is not reflected in any UK-commercial product list here until it closes.

A further named entry in this supplier's own frameworks array ("Interventional Cardiology / IR / Neuro / CRM / EP") is a general reference rather than a single confirmed brief and is not counted in the 7.

ownership: Boston Scientific Limited, company number 02729626, was incorporated on 8 July 1992 (originally as Bestdane Limited, renamed 27 July 1992) and is active. Its registered office moved twice in 2023, from 100 New Bridge Street, London EC4V 6JA to Breakspear Park, Breakspear Way, Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, most recently settling at HP2 4TZ on 14 November 2023. This is a wholly controlled subsidiary of a listed US group, not an independent UK company with its own board culture.

A separately numbered entity, Boston Scientific (UK) Limited (04949633), is dissolved (already noted on this supplier's record as dissolved since October 2023) -- do not use that number for the trading company; 02729626 is the live one.

deepDive.interview: Two things are worth knowing before this one. First, the UK company you would be joining is a thin legal shell around a large commercial operation: one active Companies House director, based in Massachusetts, appointed the same day her two predecessors resigned in August 2024, and a UK nominee secretary alongside her -- nobody UK-resident on the statutory register at all. That is normal for a US-parented subsidiary of this size and is not itself a red flag, but it means governance questions get answered in Marlborough, not Hemel Hempstead, and it is worth asking who actually signs off UK commercial decisions day to day. Second, ask where the business is mid-change: the Penumbra acquisition, agreed in January 2026 at $14.5bn, was still not closed as of the company's own late-July 2026 guidance, so anyone joining now is joining before that integration starts, not after it. On the framework side, seven confirmed NHS Supply Chain lines spanning cardiology, neuromodulation, endoscopy and theatre equipment is a genuinely broad NHS footprint for one supplier, and FARAPULSE's continuing UK roll-out (flagged in this record's existing alert) is the live growth story to ask about in an EP or structural heart interview specifically.

deepDive.origin: supplier-deep-capture scheduled run, 18/08/2026. Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (Crest Medical Limited 03876927 and its parent Crest Medical Holdings Limited 06484761: company overview, persons with significant control, officers, charges and filing history), the audited accounts of both companies for the year ended 31 March 2025 read from the tagged (iXBRL) documents filed on 22/12/2025, NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, BSI's own standards development record, Crest Medical's own website and its Cezanne careers board, all read on 18/08/2026.
deepDive.tagline: Warrington first aid, PPE and wound care supplier, named on 17 NHS Supply Chain frameworks and six of them started in 2026 · owner-controlled through Crest Medical Holdings Limited, formerly First Aid Holdings
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Crest Medical is on a great many NHS Supply Chain frameworks and is barely making money. Seventeen frameworks puts it level with Stryker and Mölnlycke and inside the top thirteen of the 1,216 suppliers this Hub holds, counted one way only, by how many of NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name the company. Its own audited accounts for the year to 31 March 2025 record turnover of £24,303,917, down slightly on the £24,683,108 of the year before, and a profit before tax of £829. Not £829,000. Eight hundred and twenty-nine pounds. One rung up, the group that owns it turned over £27,984,811 and lost £824,149 before tax, which is a real improvement on the £2,381,568 it lost the year before, and it is paying £565,973 a year in interest while it builds a new warehouse and invests in the manufacturing arm it bought in 2023. Set that against the framework record and you have the interesting question in the room: six of its seventeen NHS Supply Chain frameworks started during 2026, so this is a business winning NHS category ground faster than it is converting it into margin. Anyone joining a commercial team here is joining the half of that equation the board most needs fixed.

named supplier, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs; three re-read directly on 18/08/2026. Ranking rule, so you can judge it: count the briefs that name the company, one per framework, across the 1,216 suppliers in this Hub's seed. On that count 17 is joint eleventh with Stryker and Mölnlycke; only B. Braun (30), GBUK and Fannin (25), BD (24), GE HealthCare (23), Medtronic (22), Vygon, Praxis and Medline (21) and Banner (18) are named on more. It is a count of frameworks, not of revenue, lots or market share, and nothing here is inferred from product ranges.

Wound Closure (19 January), Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene (16 February), Single Use Theatre Protective Wear (26 May), General Wound Care (24 June), Syringes, Needles and Associated Products (1 July) and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (4 August 2026)

prose: Crest Medical Limited's turnover has sat within a band of about £600,000 for four years: £24,088,369 in the year to 31 March 2022, £24,361,928 in FY2023, £24,683,108 in FY2024 and £24,303,917 in FY2025. The first three of those were read from the tagged (iXBRL) accounts by this Hub's Companies House pipeline. The FY2025 figure is not tagged in the filing, so it is quoted here from the wording of the company's own strategic report, which states it alongside the prior year. Flat is the honest description, and the flatness is what makes the framework record below worth asking about.

The profit line is where the story is. FY2025 profit before tax was £829, following a loss of £229,187 in FY2024. At group level Crest Medical Holdings Limited turned over £27,984,811 (£27,240,891 of it in the United Kingdom and £743,920 overseas) against £26,538,137 the year before, and lost £824,149 before tax against £2,381,568. So the group is growing where the trading subsidiary is not, and the loss has narrowed by about two thirds. Gross margin is the reason: gross profit rose to £9,356,525 on those sales, 33.4% against 29.8% the previous year. Below that line, distribution costs of £5,078,181 and administrative expenses of £4,397,526 still take more than the gross profit, and interest payable of £565,973 does the rest.

The directors describe a deliberate investment phase: a long-term investment in a new warehousing facility, continued investment in Crest Healthcare to strengthen manufacturing capability, and an increased focus on the hospital and retail markets. An exceptional charge of £139,532 for relocation costs sits in the FY2025 group accounts, and the registered office moved from Blue Dot House at Chesford Grange to Unit 5 Farrell Industrial Estate on 30 May 2025. No dividend was paid. The group balance sheet carries one outstanding charge, a fixed and floating debenture in favour of Clydesdale Bank PLC created on 29 March 2010; the other seven charges on the trading company's record are satisfied.

ownership: Crest Medical Limited, company number 03876927, was incorporated on 15 November 1999 and is active. It has traded under earlier names, becoming CREST MEDICAL LIMITED on 19 December 2006, and its registered SIC code is 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. Its registered office moved on 30 May 2025 from Blue Dot House, 3 Chesford Grange, Woolston, Warrington WA1 4RQ to Unit 5 Farrell Industrial Estate, Howley Lane, Warrington WA1 2PB.

Its sole person with significant control is Crest Medical Holdings Limited, company number 06484761, notified on 6 April 2016 and holding 75% or more of the shares. That parent was incorporated on 25 January 2008 as FIRST AID HOLDINGS LIMITED and took its present name on 22 August 2018. It is registered as a non-trading company (SIC 74990) at the same Warrington address, and its own sole person with significant control is Mr Alastair Gerald Lees Maxwell, notified on 1 January 2017, with the nature of control recorded as significant influence or control. This is an owner-controlled British group, not a subsidiary of an overseas manufacturer, which is unusual among suppliers with this many NHS Supply Chain frameworks and is worth knowing: decisions are taken in Warrington.

The group's own strategic report for the year to 31 March 2025 names the wholly owned subsidiaries as Crest Medical Limited, Crest Logistics Limited, Crest Healthcare Limited, Wallace Cameron Training Limited, Scopeguard Limited and Braidlock Limited, alongside other non-trading companies, and describes the group as operating across first aid, pharmaceuticals, PPE and medical consumables. Crest Healthcare Limited (15116309) was incorporated on 5 September 2023, days before the trade press reported Crest's purchase of the assets of Macdonald & Taylor Healthcare, a Cheshire manufacturer established in 1976 that brought the Primeguard brand and UK manufacturing into the group. Crest Logistics Limited (06773990) dates from 16 December 2008. The group's auditor is Wheawill & Sudworth Limited of Huddersfield, its bankers Virgin Money and its solicitors Brabners LLP.

Crest Medical's own newsroom states that BSI published BS 8599-1:2019+A1:2026, the workplace first aid kit standard, on this date. BSI's own standards development record confirms the reference and gives the full title as "Workplace first aid kits – Part 1: Contents of first aid kits and provision of Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) in the workplace – Specification", under committee CH/100. NHS Supply Chain's General Wound Care framework starts, running to 23 June 2028, with Crest Medical Ltd among 28 named suppliers (reference 2025/S 000-028909). Re-verified against the brief on 18/08/2026.

NHS Supply Chain's Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework starts, running to 3 August 2028, with Crest Medical Ltd among 40 named suppliers (reference 2025/S 000-032216). It combines the former Patient Assessment Devices, Blood Pressure Cuffs and Support Products, and Thermometer Device and Support Products frameworks. Re-verified against the brief on 18/08/2026.

NHS Supply Chain posts a contract launch update on the General Wound Care framework: a number of new product NPCs were not orderable at the 24 June launch, with plasters, cotton wool and first aid kit lines being released through August. This is a framework-level notice and NHS Supply Chain does not attribute the affected lines to a named supplier on the brief, so no claim is made here that they are Crest's.

The Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products framework expires. NHS Supply Chain's own brief records it as a Contract Extension that "starts on 3 October 2022, runs for 48 months and ends on 30 September 2026", including a 24 month extension, with Crest Medical Ltd among 27 named suppliers. Verified on the brief on 18/08/2026; six weeks away at the date of this record.

hiring: Crest Medical's own careers board, hosted on Cezanne, carried exactly one live vacancy on 18/08/2026: a Senior Warehouse Operative in Warrington, in Supply Chain. No salary is published. The careers pages describe roles "from apprenticeships to direct roles in our warehouse and manufacturing teams, through sales and customer service, to senior leadership", and list benefits including a birthday day off, the option to buy annual leave and discounted gym membership. Read that as a company recruiting for operations right now rather than proof it is not recruiting commercially: with 82 people in the trading company and 115 in the group, field vacancies here are occasional and are also placed through recruiters this check did not cover.
marketPosition: The verifiable measure of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint: named supplier on 17 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, each confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief. They span wound care at both ends (Advanced Wound Care and General Wound Care), Wound Closure, Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene, Single Use Theatre Protective Wear, Syringes and Needles, Blood Collection Devices, Extension Sets and Lines, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets, Enteral Feeding and Bile Bags, Patient Temperature Management, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, External Defibrillation Devices, Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation, Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy, Maternity, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Sexual Health, and Cleaning Equipment and Supplies. Six of the 17 started during 2026 and one, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets, expires on 30 September 2026.

That breadth is the thing to understand about Crest. It is not a category specialist. It is a wholesaler and own-brand manufacturer whose route into the NHS is being on a great many framework lots with modest volumes on each, and its own site describes it as a wholesale manufacturer of first aid, occupational health products, PPE and consumer health products, and a private label supplier to retail in the UK, Europe and the USA. Its brands are Blue Dot, Wallace Cameron, McKinnon Medical, BioSafe, Irripod, Stericlens and Primeguard, with Microplast, Easyice, Burnkool, Cromessol, Revive-Aid, Advapore, Advacare and Once alongside them. Primeguard is manufactured in the UK by Crest Healthcare.

No market share is given here, and one widely repeated claim is deliberately not repeated: a third-party company directory describes Crest Medical as the largest provider of personal protective equipment to the NHS. No source for that was found in NHS Supply Chain's own material, in the company's filings or on the company's own website, so it is treated as unverified and is not published as a fact. Three Crest products are confirmed in the NHS Supply Chain catalogue by NPC: Stericlens 0.9% sodium chloride aerosol spray in 240ml (ELZ008) and 100ml (ELZ007), and Irripod 20ml sodium chloride irrigation pods in packs of 25 (MRB742). The Hub's own crawl of crestmedical.co.uk on 12/08/2026 read 872 products from the site's XML sitemap; those names come from URL slugs rather than a product record, so treat that as the shape of the catalogue rather than an exact list.

deepDive.interview: Read the accounts before you go in, because they set up the two questions worth asking. The first is margin. Turnover has been flat around £24m for four years and FY2025 profit before tax was £829, while group gross margin improved from 29.8% to 33.4%. Asking what the next point of margin comes from, own-brand mix or the new warehouse, is a serious commercial question and shows you have read the filing rather than the website. The second is conversion. Six NHS Supply Chain frameworks started in 2026, which means live implementation work across trusts right now, and the Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets framework expires on 30 September 2026, so there is a renewal in the diary within weeks of most start dates. Ask how the team is resourced across both. Two pieces of context help you sound like an insider: the standard for workplace first aid kits was amended this year and BSI's own title for BS 8599-1:2019+A1:2026 now runs to the provision of AEDs in the workplace, which touches two Crest categories at once; and this is an owner-controlled business, so the person with significant control sits on the board you are joining rather than in another country. Finally, know which entity you are being hired into. Crest Medical Limited, Crest Healthcare Limited and Crest Logistics Limited are separate companies at the same address doing different jobs.

alerts.text: CRITICAL OWNERSHIP CORRECTION: Current Health is NO LONGER owned by Best Buy. Best Buy acquired it for ~$400m in late 2021, took a $475m non-cash goodwill impairment charge (Q4 2024), launched a $109m restructuring and wound down hospital-at-home partnerships (May 2025), then SOLD Current Health back to co-founder/former CEO Chris McGhee on 24/06/2025 -- it now operates as an independent private company refocused on US home-hospital/high-acuity care. background.heading: Speciality re-tagging
background.text: Re-tagged primary speciality to Anaesthesia and critical care (kept Renal and dialysis as a secondary tag) -- CE-marked indications are cytokine/bilirubin/myoglobin adsorption in critical illness and intraoperative anticoagulant removal during cardiac surgery, not renal replacement itself (it's commonly run in-line with a CRRT circuit, which is a delivery mechanism, not the clinical indication). NICE has published three Medtech Innovation Briefings -- MIB87 (sepsis), MIB217 (COVID-19 respiratory failure), MIB249 (cardiac surgery bleeding reduction) -- all note the evidence base is low-quality/small-sample/mostly observational; current sepsis evidence does not show improved mortality. Any efficacy claims should be qualified as emerging, not established.

background.heading: NHS deployments and funding
background.text: Do NOT list DrugSorb-ATR (ticagrelor removal — FDA De Novo denied April 2025, unclear CE status) or HemoDefend-RBC/-BGA (blood-transfusion safety filters) as available products -- both are investigational/pipeline-stage only, not approved anywhere for the DrugSorb-ATR/HemoDefend line.

background.heading: Regulatory and NICE scope
background.text: IMPORTANT NICE nuance: NICE MTG46 (Dec 2019) is a routine-adoption/cost-saving recommendation SPECIFIC TO CLUSTER HEADACHE, underpinning MedTech Funding Mandate inclusion. Migraine use is covered only by an earlier, lower-status safety clearance (not an MTG) -- do not imply NICE-mandated NHS funding for migraine use to the same degree as cluster headache. NHS Supply Chain catalogue listing was extended to 17/03/2026 with a further-extension option -- current status past that date is unconfirmed, worth re-checking. Parent electroCore, Inc. (Nasdaq: ECOR) remains independent and profitable (FY2025 net sales $32.0m, +27% YoY) -- no acquisition/ownership change. A separate consumer-wellness product, Truvaga (general stress/anxiety/sleep, no headache indication), is sold DTC by the US parent -- UK/NHS clinical channel presence unconfirmed, not added as a UK product.

CORRECTION worth recording: Actico compression bandaging is NOT an Essity/BSN medical product -- it's supplied by L&R MEDICAL UK LTD (Lohmann & Rauscher), a direct competitor; confirmed via both L&R's own site and NHS Supply Chain supplier attribution. Effective 01/01/2026, Essity restructured from three to four business areas -- Medical Solutions now sits inside a new 'Health & Medical' area alongside TENA continence care (previously a separate Consumer Goods line), which is why NHS Supply Chain lists the supplier as 'ESSITY UK TENA HM' -- explains why this record and the separate TENA record now share a commercial parent even though they remain genuinely distinct product lines and are kept as separate supplier records here.

background.heading: Duplicate and record merge
background.text: Confirmed as the SAME legal entity as 'Essity UK Limited (formerly BSN Medical Ltd)' (Companies House 03226403, Dunstable) and 'Essity UK TENA Health & Medical' — Essity's own site genuinely splits its Health & Medical business into distinct category pages (wound-care-vascular, orthopaedics, continence), and NHS Supply Chain lists all three product families under one supplier code, 'ESSITY UK TENA HM'. This is an intentional category split, not a duplicate — kept as three separate records deliberately. Tork (hand hygiene dispensers) is a genuine Essity brand but belongs to Professional Hygiene, not this wound-care line — removed from this record's product list as a different category. The 'formerly BSN Medical Ltd' wording on the sibling Essity UK Limited record is a slight imprecision worth noting: BSN Medical Limited (04085346) still exists as a dormant shell; its trade was legally transferred to Essity UK Limited on 1 Sept 2024, not a company renaming.

suppliers.ownership: BSN medical was acquired in 2017 and has been absorbed into Essity's Health & Medical business area. There is no separate BSN medical company or brand site today; the UK product brands are Leukoplast, Cutimed, JOBST, Actimove and Delta-Cast. Source: Essity's own 'Our Journey' page, https://www.essity.com/company/about-us/our-journey/, read 21/08/2026, which lists under 2017 'Acquisition of BSN medical, a leading medical solutions company' alongside 'Listing of Essity Aktiebolag (publ) on Nasdaq Stockholm'. Corroborated by bsnmedical.com, which redirects (four hops, checked 21/08/2026) to https://www.essity.com/company/essitys-business-areas/health-and-medical/, Essity's Health & Medical page, naming TENA, JOBST, Cutimed, Leukoplast, Actimove and Delta-Cast as the brands. essity.co.uk redirects to https://www.essity.com/company/essity-in-the-world/uk-roi/ (HTTP 200), which states the UK Health & Medical business specialises in Compression Therapy, Wound Care and Orthopaedics.

alerts.text: MAJOR CORPORATE CHANGE: Exactech, Inc. filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2024, driven by ~2,600 patient lawsuits over a packaging/oxidation defect (vacuum bags missing an oxygen barrier layer, causing polyethylene insert oxidation across 140,000+ knee, ~130,000 hip and ~1,500 ankle systems, plus the Equinoxe shoulder system) -- recall ran August 2021 through April 2024. Court confirmed a restructuring plan 15/09/2025; assets sold to a new investor group (Strategic Value Partners, Stellex Capital Management, Greywolf Capital Management). The business relaunched as ADVITA ORTHO, LLC on 03/11/2025, which now owns and distributes the Equinoxe/Vantage/Alteon/Truliant/Novation/Newton/GPS product lines. TPG Capital (the brief's assumed current owner) no longer owns the business -- a litigation trust was set up to pursue claims against TPG. UK legal entity Companies House record shows 'ADVITA ORTHO UK LIMITED' with 'previous name: EXACTECH (UK) LIMITED'. NHS Supply Chain now refers to the supplier as 'Advita Ortho (Exactech) Ltd.' Recall litigation/restructuring fallout is still live as of the most recent sources -- do not present the recall as resolved-and-behind-them without this context.

deepDive.tagline: Companies House 02663514, active since 1991 · registered office Vital Westminster Industrial Estate, Measham, Swadlincote · controlling party changed on 8 September 2025 to Healthco Investment Limited, the vehicle named in Investindustrial's purchase of DCC Healthcare
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Fannin is named on more NHS Supply Chain frameworks than any other supplier in this Hub's framework data — 25, against GE HealthCare's 20 and Medtronic's 19 — and it changed hands less than a year ago. On 8 September 2025 the Companies House PSC register recorded B.M.Browne (UK Holdings) Limited ceasing to control the company and Healthco Investment Limited being notified in its place; two days later DCC plc announced it had completed the sale of its healthcare division, and Healthco Investment Limited is the vehicle named in Investindustrial's own announcement of that deal. The board has turned over completely since: six officers resigned between August 2025 and March 2026, five were appointed between September 2025 and May 2026, and the year end moved from 31 March to 31 December. This is a first-year private-equity carve-out with an unusually wide NHS framework footprint, and that combination is the real subject of any conversation about targets, territory or which ranges get pushed.

ownership: Fannin (UK) Limited is a long-standing UK company under a brand-new owner. It was incorporated on 18 November 1991 as Showissue Limited, traded as B.M. Browne (UK) Limited from February 1992, and took the Fannin name on 28 June 2007. Until last year it sat inside DCC plc's healthcare division — the Vital medical devices platform — with B.M.Browne (UK Holdings) Limited (02872126) recorded as the party with significant control since June 2016.

In November 2024 DCC plc announced, after a strategic review, that it intended to dispose of DCC Healthcare and concentrate on its larger energy business. On 22 April 2025 Investindustrial announced it had signed an agreement to buy the division, naming Healthco Investment Limited as the acquiring entity, at a total enterprise value of £1,050 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis, including £130 million of two-year deferred consideration. Investindustrial's own release describes DCC Healthcare as two platforms — HBI, a supplements and beauty contract manufacturer, and Vital, a supplier of medical devices to acute and primary care — with more than 3,000 employees, 11 manufacturing sites, revenue of £859.4 million and adjusted operating profit of £88.1 million in the year to 31 March 2024, about 13% of DCC group adjusted operating profit. DCC announced completion on 10 September 2025, alongside an £800 million return of capital to its own shareholders.

The register carries the same event from Fannin's side, and this is the part that can be checked rather than taken on trust: on 8 September 2025 the PSC entry for B.M.Browne (UK Holdings) Limited ceased and Healthco Investment Limited (16384404, a holding company incorporated on 14 April 2025) was notified as having significant influence or control. The identical PSC event, on the identical date, appears on Williams Medical Supplies Limited (04240054) and SP Services (UK) Limited (03424705). Both of those are themselves named on NHS Supply Chain frameworks in this repo's data — Williams on 3, SP Services on 2 — so 28 distinct framework positions in this data now sit under one owner. Fannin and SP Services are co-listed on two of them (Electrodes, Ultrasound Gels, Defibrillation and Related Consumables; General Wound Care), and Fannin and Williams share none. Worth knowing before you read an 'also on this framework' list as a list of independent rivals.

Investindustrial's portfolio page presents the business simply as Vital: around 1,500 employees, headquartered in Ireland, operating in France, the UK and Germany and selling into more than 100 countries, through units it names as Vital Healthcare and Vital Healthcare Ireland. That page does not name Fannin, and it dates the investment to August 2025 rather than September; the register date and DCC's own completion announcement are used here in preference. Whether the Fannin trading name survives the group's rebranding is not something any source read here settles, and it is a fair question to ask in an interview rather than a fact to assume.

marketPosition: Fannin is named on 25 NHS Supply Chain frameworks in this repo's data, the highest count of any supplier in it. The counting rule: a supplier is counted on a framework only where NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief for that framework names it, supplier names are normalised to a single key so that 'Fannin Ltd', 'Fannin UK Ltd' and 'Fannin UK Limited' count once per framework, and the count is taken over the 122 briefs parsed into this repo on 12 August 2026. Fifteen further briefs did not parse and are logged as unparsed, so this is a ranking over what has been read, not over every framework NHS Supply Chain runs.

What that number is not: it is not turnover, volume, or share. A framework position is permission to be bought from, not evidence of anything having been bought. No market share percentage is published for this company anywhere in this system, because nobody has that data. What the count does support is a narrower and more useful claim — Fannin's route to the NHS is breadth of distribution across many consumable categories rather than depth in one, which is a different sales job from a single-technology manufacturer's, and is worth reflecting in how you pitch yourself.

On size, Fannin (UK) Limited files full accounts, but the filing at Companies House is a PDF with no tagged figures, so no turnover is read from it and none is estimated here. The £859.4 million quoted above is DCC Healthcare's whole divisional revenue for the year to 31 March 2024 under the previous owner, covering both HBI and Vital across every country, and it must not be read as Fannin's.

deepDive.interview: Lead with the ownership change, because it is recent, checkable and nobody expects a candidate to know it: the company came out of DCC plc into Investindustrial's hands in September 2025, and every current board member was appointed after that date. Fair questions follow naturally — what the first year under the new owner has changed about targets and range focus, whether the Fannin brand stays as the group consolidates on the Vital name, and whether the two sister companies now under the same owner (Williams Medical Supplies, SP Services) change how territories or accounts are split. On the commercial side, know that this is a broad-line distributor: 25 NHS Supply Chain frameworks spanning airway, vascular access, electrosurgery, endoscopy, wound care, theatre wear, orthopaedics and waste, rather than one flagship technology. That means a portfolio-selling conversation with procurement and category managers, not a single-product clinical evangelism pitch, and your examples should be picked to match. Do not walk in describing them as an independent family business; that stopped being true last September.

Stimwave's former CEO, Laura Perryman, was criminally convicted of healthcare fraud and conspiracy (also separately SEC-charged with $41m investor fraud) — the case centred on an internal device component that in some implanted units was reportedly a non-functional piece of plastic rather than the real electronic receiver; roughly 8,000 patients were implanted with these devices between 2017 and 2020. Curonix LLC purchased Stimwave's assets out of bankruptcy in Nov 2022 and now manufactures/sells the Freedom SCS/PNS systems under the Curonix name. Whether Freedom Neuro BV is the current Curonix-era UK distributor or a leftover Stimwave-era relationship is unconfirmed. Confirmed NHS Supply Chain Neuromodulation Devices framework-approved (2024-2028) but no live catalogue SKUs found under this name. Given this is a clinician-facing CPD/training tool, this history should not be omitted if the product is referenced.

deepDive.tagline: Bedford diagnostic imaging and endoscopy business, the former Hitachi Medical Systems UK, named on nine NHS Supply Chain frameworks in its own right and one of only five suppliers on the national Flexible Endoscopes framework · turnover £45.8m in its first full year after Fujifilm UK's diagnostics division transferred in, and it bought Aquilant's endoscopy business on 1 December 2025
deepDive.lede: Three things about this company are not obvious from its name, and all three change how you would sell for it or interview at it. The first is that it is the old Hitachi business: FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED, company number 03218117, was HITACHI MEDICAL SYSTEMS UK LIMITED from 2002 until 1 July 2021, and before that Hitachi Ultrasound and Ecoscan Ultrasound, so the ultrasound and MRI heritage on the NHS frameworks predates the Fujifilm badge by two decades. The second is that it only recently became the trading entity it now is. Fujifilm UK Limited's medical diagnostic division transferred into it on 1 October 2023, and the year to 31 March 2025 was, in the directors' own words, the first full year after that transfer. Turnover was £45,830,000 against £28,810,000, and the honest reading of that 59.1% is that the prior year holds roughly six months of the transferred business, not that the market grew by three fifths. The third is the shape of the headcount. Of 155 average employees, 64 are in sales and sales support and 86 in after-sales and technical, against 4 in administration and distribution. This is a capital-equipment business where the service contract is the annuity: £16,840,000 of the £45.8m, 36.7%, is rendering of services rather than sale of goods. Then on 1 December 2025 it bought the endoscopy trade of Aquilant, a competitor already carried in this Hub, and told its auditors it expects that plus the NHS 10-Year Health Plan to add 10% to sales in the year to 31 March 2026. That is the business you would be joining: mid-forties millions of UK-only revenue, growing by acquisition into a framework it already sits on with only four other suppliers.

stats.n: £45,830,000, against £28,810,000 in the year to 31 March 2024. Read from the Income Statement on page 15 of the full accounts of Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited (03218117) filed at Companies House on 05/12/2025. All of it is United Kingdom revenue: note 3 gives the geographical analysis as £45,830,000 United Kingdom and nothing elsewhere. Treat the 59.1% increase with care, because the prior year is not a like-for-like base: see the growth section.

prose: There is no ten-year turnover series for this company and there should not be, because the entity's revenue base changed twice inside four years. Fujifilm Holdings Corporation was notified as the person with significant control on 31 March 2021, the day Hitachi's holding ceased, and the company was renamed from Hitachi Medical Systems UK Limited on 1 July 2021. Then, on 1 October 2023, the medical diagnostic division of Fujifilm UK Limited transferred into it. The two comparable figures on the face of the FY2025 accounts are turnover of £28,810,000 for the year to 31 March 2024 and £45,830,000 for the year to 31 March 2025, and the strategic report describes FY2025 as the first full year following that transfer. So the year to March 2024 carries only about six months of the transferred business. The 59.1% increase the directors print in their own key performance indicators table is arithmetically correct and is not a like-for-like growth rate. A bar chart of those two years would say something the accounts do not, so none is drawn.

Everything else on the FY2025 face of the accounts moved the same way. Gross profit was £18,535,000 on £45,830,000 of sales, a gross margin of 40.4% against 36.3% the year before. Below that, distribution costs were only £367,000 and administrative expenses £16,031,000, which is what a business with 86 field service and technical staff and 64 in sales looks like when it books almost all of its people cost as administrative. Operating profit was £2,137,000, interest receivable £447,000 against interest payable of £245,000, profit before tax £2,339,000 and profit after tax £1,748,000. Shareholders' funds rose 55.9% to £4,876,000 and cash balances to £9,455,000 from £4,789,000.

Two structural facts sit behind those numbers and are worth knowing before you read the margin as a commercial achievement. The going concern note describes the company as a Limited-Risk Distributor with access to the group's cash pooling arrangement, which is a transfer-pricing structure: a limited-risk distributor is remunerated to earn a modest, stable return, so the operating margin here of 4.7% is substantially set by group policy rather than by UK negotiation. The same note adds that the company is not permitted under group policy to use derivative or hedging techniques, transacts over 95% of purchases and sales in Sterling, holds no fixed debt and does not insure against debtor failure. The directors' forecast for the year to 31 March 2026 assumes growth in sales of 10%, attributed to the acquisition of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited and to strategic alignment with the NHS Fit for the Future 10-Year Health Plan, and assumes a £3m intercompany loan is repaid within the period.

ownership: FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED, company number 03218117, was incorporated on 28 June 1996 and is active, at Fujifilm House, Whitbread Way, Bedford MK42 0ZE, with SIC code 47749, retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods. Its previous names are the whole story of the business: ECOSCAN ULTRASOUND LIMITED from incorporation to 17 January 2000, HITACHI ULTRASOUND LIMITED to 4 April 2002, and HITACHI MEDICAL SYSTEMS UK LIMITED from then until 1 July 2021. Its sole active person with significant control is Fujifilm Holdings Corporation of Tokyo, registration number 010401065370, notified on 31 March 2021 with ownership of 75% or more of shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. Kabushiki Kaisha Hitachi Seisakusho, that is Hitachi Ltd, is recorded as a ceased person with significant control on the same date, 31 March 2021. Note 20 of the accounts names Fujifilm Holdings Corporation as the ultimate parent company and the parent of both the smallest and the largest group for which consolidated statements are drawn up.

The company is not the only Fujifilm entity selling into the NHS, and the distinction matters when you are reading a framework award or addressing a contract. Companies House holds FUJIFILM UK LIMITED (01264514, incorporated 1976) and FUJIFILM SONOSITE LTD (04104159, incorporated 2000) at the same Bedford address, alongside this company. The strategic report records that the medical diagnostic division of Fujifilm UK Limited transferred to Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited with completion on 1 October 2023 and all systems and activities fully integrated during the year to 31 March 2025. Note 21 records the consequence for pensions: as part of that transfer the company became a participating employer of the Fujifilm UK Pension and Life Assurance Scheme, which includes a closed defined benefit section that this company does not contribute to but has guaranteed the obligations of should another participating employer default. That scheme is accounted for in Fujifilm UK Limited's own statements and its funding position at 31 March 2025 was assets £67,579,000, liabilities £60,945,000 and a net surplus of £6,634,000.

On 30 September 2025 the company announced an asset acquisition relating to the endoscopy business of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited. Its own note 22 states the acquisition cost as £13.9m, to take place on 1 December 2025, funded by an intercompany share capital issue, and the register corroborates the funding step: an SH01 filed on 21 November 2025 records a statement of capital of GBP 13,500,000 following an allotment of shares on that date, with the enabling resolution filed on 25 November 2025. The transaction completed. Aquilant Endoscopy Limited (03402556, formerly Endoscopy UK Limited and then Imotech Medical Limited, of Basingstoke) states in its own strategic report for the year ended 30 December 2025, filed on 3 July 2026, that on 1 December 2025 a substantial portion of its trade was sold to a third party for consideration of £12,208,000, that the remaining trade and assets were immediately hived across to another group company, Aquilant Limited, and that from that date the company has ceased to trade and is expected to become dormant. The two consideration figures, £13.9m stated by the buyer as acquisition cost and £12,208,000 stated by the seller as consideration for the trade sold, are not the same number and are not reconciled here; they are quoted as each company filed them.

Four charges have been registered against the company and one is outstanding: a fixed charge in favour of Bank Mendes Gans N.V., created 5 August 2021 and delivered 6 August 2021. Bank Mendes Gans is the cash pooling and netting bank the going concern note refers to. The three satisfied charges are historic Barclays and landlord security from 1996 and 1998, two of them marked satisfied only on 18 October 2024.

press.text: The company's name changes from HITACHI MEDICAL SYSTEMS UK LIMITED to FUJIFILM HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED on the register. Fujifilm Holdings Corporation had been notified as person with significant control on 31 March 2021, the date Hitachi Ltd's holding is recorded as ceased.

Completion of the transfer of Fujifilm UK Limited's medical diagnostic division into Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited, as stated in the strategic report of the FY2025 accounts. The same accounts record that all systems and activities were fully integrated during the year to 31 March 2025, and note 21 records that the company became a participating employer of the Fujifilm UK Pension and Life Assurance Scheme as part of the transfer.

NHS Supply Chain's Digital Diagnostic Solutions framework starts, running to 31 July 2027, reference 2025/S 000-043444, with Fujifilm Healthcare UK Ltd among 54 named suppliers. Re-read on the brief on 20/08/2026. It is the company's only framework outside the 2021 diagnostic equipment tender.

Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited announces an asset acquisition relating to the endoscopy business of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited, stated in note 22 of its own FY2025 accounts at a cost of £13.9m, to complete on 1 December 2025 and to be funded by an intercompany share capital issue.

An SH01 is filed recording a statement of capital of GBP 13,500,000 following an allotment of shares on that date, with the enabling resolution of allotment filed on 25 November 2025. This is the funding step note 22 describes.

The Aquilant endoscopy transaction completes. Aquilant Endoscopy Limited's own strategic report for the year ended 30 December 2025 states that on this date a substantial portion of its trade was sold to a third party for consideration of £12,208,000, that the remaining trade and assets were then hived across to Aquilant Limited, and that from that date the company has ceased to trade and is expected to become dormant.
Full accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 filed at Companies House: turnover £45,830,000, operating profit £2,137,000, profit before tax £2,339,000, 155 average employees.

Nine of the company's twelve NHS Supply Chain frameworks expire on this date. They were all awarded under one reference, 2021/S 000-007768, started on 1 April 2022 and run 72 months including two 24 month extensions: Bladder Scanners, Bone Densitometers, CT Scanners, Flexible Endoscopes, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanners, Mammography Imaging Systems, Mobile Image Intensifiers, Mobile X-Ray Systems, Static X-Ray and Ultrasound Scanners. Verified against the briefs; the Flexible Endoscopes brief was re-read live on 20/08/2026. This is a single renewal event covering most of the company's NHS Supply Chain footprint, not ten separate ones, and it is the most important date in this record.

hiring: No live vacancy list was verified for this company in this session, so nothing is claimed about what it is recruiting for today. What the filed accounts do show is the direction of travel in the workforce, and it is unusually clear. Average employees went from 88 to 155 in one year. Sales and sales support went from 32 to 64 and after-sales and technical from 37 to 86, while management fell from 12 to 1 and administration and distribution from 7 to 4. Some of that is the reclassification you would expect when a division transfers in and job families are mapped onto a new payroll, so do not read the management line as 11 people leaving. The sales and service lines are the ones to take at face value: this company roughly doubled both in the year to 31 March 2025, and directors' remuneration rose from £276,464 to £405,623 across a board that grew over the same period.
marketPosition: This company's NHS position is a narrow and deep one, and the Hub's own framework data shows it plainly. Every one of the twelve NHS Supply Chain frameworks that names a Fujifilm entity sits in a single category, Diagnostic Equipment and Services. There is no wound care, no consumables spread, no facilities line. Nine of the twelve were awarded under one reference, 2021/S 000-007768, all starting 1 April 2022 and all expiring 31 March 2028: Bladder Scanners, Bone Densitometers, CT Scanners, Flexible Endoscopes, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanners, Mammography Imaging Systems, Mobile Image Intensifiers, Mobile X-Ray Systems, Static X-Ray and Ultrasound Scanners. The other three are Digital Diagnostic Solutions (2025/S 000-043444, to 31 July 2027) and Laboratory Diagnostics, Point of Care Testing and Pathology Managed Services (2023/S 000-028831, to 11 March 2028).

The supplier lists on those briefs are short, which is the commercially useful part. Flexible Endoscopes names five suppliers in total: FUJIFILM Healthcare UK Limited, Karl Storz Endoscopy UK Ltd, Olympus KeyMed, Pentax Medical and Richard Wolf UK Limited, re-read live on 20/08/2026. Bone Densitometers names six, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scanners and Mammography Imaging Systems seven each, CT Scanners eight, Mobile Image Intensifiers ten, Bladder Scanners eleven, Static X-Ray thirteen, Mobile X-Ray fourteen and Ultrasound Scanners twenty-one. Against that, Digital Diagnostic Solutions carries 54 named suppliers and Laboratory Diagnostics 122, so those two are a very different kind of framework and being on them says much less about position. No market share figure is given anywhere in this record, because none is verifiable.

⚠ The Hub's single supplier record for Fujifilm covers three separate registered companies, and this record does not merge them. Nine briefs name Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited or Ltd. Three name FUJIFILM UK Ltd or Limited, which is company 01264514: Bladder Scanners, Laboratory Diagnostics Point of Care Testing and Pathology Managed Services, and Ultrasound Scanners. The Ultrasound Scanners brief separately names FUJIFILM Sonosite Ltd, company 04104159, as its own supplier alongside FUJIFILM UK Limited. The timing is consistent with the 1 October 2023 division transfer, since the 2021 tender was awarded while the diagnostics business still sat inside Fujifilm UK Limited, but NHS Supply Chain's briefs are not evidence that the contracting entity on those three has been novated to Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited, and this record does not claim that it has. If the contracting entity matters to you, ask NHS Supply Chain or the company; do not infer it from the brief.

The Aquilant purchase is the one competitive move a rep should be able to talk about. Aquilant is already a supplier in this Hub, named on fifteen NHS Supply Chain briefs across its group entities, and two of those briefs name Aquilant Endoscopy Limited specifically: Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) Endoscopes and Associated Options and Related Services, and Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products. That company sold its trade on 1 December 2025, has ceased to trade and expects to become dormant, per its own filed accounts. Whether those two framework positions moved to Fujifilm Healthcare UK Limited, to Aquilant Limited (which received the residual trade), or to neither, is not stated on the briefs and was not verified in this session. It is an open question, not a finding, and it is a very good question to ask in an interview.

deepDive.interview: Read the FY2025 accounts before you go in, because three lines in them set up better questions than anything on the website. First, do not walk in praising 59% growth. The directors themselves say the year to 31 March 2025 was the first full year after Fujifilm UK's diagnostics division transferred in on 1 October 2023, so the comparative holds about six months of that business. Saying so, and then asking what underlying growth was on a like-for-like basis, will land better than the headline. Second, ask about the service annuity. £16.84m of £45.83m is rendering of services, 86 of 155 staff are after-sales and technical, and on capital imaging that mix is the whole commercial model: you are selling a scanner once and a maintenance contract for a decade. Ask how the sales team is measured across the two. Third, ask about 31 March 2028. Nine of the twelve NHS Supply Chain frameworks the Hub holds against Fujifilm expire on that single date, all awarded under one 2021 reference, so this is one renewal event covering nearly the whole NHS footprint rather than a rolling series of them. Anyone in a commercial role here will be working towards it. Two further pieces of context make you sound like an insider. This is the old Hitachi Medical Systems UK, renamed on 1 July 2021, so a candidate who knows the MRI and ultrasound heritage is not starting from Fujifilm cameras. And the going concern note calls the company a Limited-Risk Distributor with access to group cash pooling, which tells you the UK operating margin is largely a transfer-pricing outcome: pushing hard on price in the interview as though UK margin is locally controlled will read as naive. Finally, know the Aquilant story. Fujifilm Healthcare UK bought the endoscopy trade of Aquilant Endoscopy Limited on 1 December 2025, and the company itself has ceased to trade. Fujifilm is one of only five suppliers on the national Flexible Endoscopes framework. Asking how that acquisition is being integrated into the endoscopy field team is a question only someone who has read the filings can ask.

background.heading: Ownership and parent
background.text: MAJOR OWNERSHIP FLAG — not publicly announced anywhere, but strongly evidenced via Companies House primary filings: on 18-20 November 2025, founders Guy Braverman and Allen Hanouka ceased as persons with significant control of Gama Healthcare Corporation Limited (the holding entity above GAMA Healthcare Ltd), replaced by Deb Holdings Limited (04113118, registered at Deb Group's long-standing Denby, Derbyshire HQ) with 75%+ shares/voting rights; Al Schretter (CEO of SC Johnson Global Professional, which owns Deb Group) was appointed a director the same day. This is strong documentary evidence that GAMA Healthcare passed majority control to SC Johnson via its Deb Group/Professional entity in November 2025 — the 'private, founder-led, no PE' framing is now out of date. GAMA's own news page makes no mention of this — treat as Companies House-verified but not yet publicly confirmed, and phrase cautiously rather than as a settled fact until it surfaces publicly. Vascular access tag clarification: GAMA makes no vascular access devices itself, but its HEXI brand (HEXI PREP skin antisepsis before cannulation, HEXI HUB for catheter-hub/access-port disinfection) genuinely supports vascular access procedures — the tag reflects skin/site antisepsis, not device manufacture.

deepDive.tagline: Private, majority owned by A&M Capital Europe since Dec 2023 · HQ Selby, North Yorkshire
deepDive.lede: The story to know here: GBUK spent nearly a decade under one private equity owner (H2 Equity Partners, from 2016), then changed hands again in December 2023 when A&M Capital Europe took majority control. Since then it's bought three companies in under 18 months and been through a genuine changing of the guard at board level, with two long-serving directors and the company secretary all departing within the last year. This is a business mid-transformation, not a steady state, and that's exactly the kind of thing worth asking about in an interview.

prose: Filed accounts at Companies House show turnover climbing from £44m in the year to June 2019 to £74.8m in the year to June 2024, alongside £30.6m in net assets and £14.3m cash. Employee headcount in those same FY2024 accounts was 147, though that figure predates the three acquisitions made since, so the group is materially larger today than the last filed numbers show. Full accounts for the year to June 2025 were filed on 11 July 2026; the FY2025 figures have not yet been extracted from that document.

The real growth story since December 2023 has been acquisitive rather than organic: Care & Independence (patient handling, the first deal under new ownership), Severn Healthcare Technologies (added two new therapeutic areas), and GS Medical Limited (an Irish single-use device distributor spanning endoscopy, announced January 2025). GBUK also launched a new international arm, GBUK Global, alongside a dedicated global website, signalling an explicit push beyond the UK and Ireland.

ownership: Ultimate control sits with Enhancing Patient Care Limited, the UK holding vehicle A&M Capital Europe (AMCE) used to buy 75%+ of GBUK Group Limited in December 2023, from previous owner H2 Equity Partners. AMCE is a London-headquartered, middle-market private equity firm with around €650m under management; GBUK was its seventeenth transaction, advised by Weil Gotshal & Manges, Houlihan Lokey, Boston Consulting Group and EY among others, which tells you this deal had serious institutional backing behind it.

Underneath the holding company sits the original operating business, GBUK Ltd (trading since 2004), plus a cluster of subsidiaries built up over the years including GBUK Enteral, Intervene, R&J Medical and Blue Box Medical, alongside brands like It's Interventional and Frontier Medical Group. The three post-2023 acquisitions sit alongside these, with endoscopy added via GS Medical.

press.text: A&M Capital Europe announces its majority investment in GBUK Group, buying out H2 Equity Partners. GBUK continues under Mike Geering's leadership, with AMCE backing a stated strategy of bolt-on acquisitions in the UK, Europe and North America.
Three bolt-on acquisitions in quick succession: Care & Independence, Severn Healthcare Technologies, and GS Medical Limited, each announced as strengthening a specific therapeutic area or geography.

Notable board turnover: long-serving director Peter Spiller resigns (November 2025), followed by another director (February 2026), continuing a reshuffle that began with the company secretary's departure in January 2025.

hiring: GBUK doesn't publish a rolling count of roles filled, and its own careers page shows no live vacancies at the time of this check, so treat hiring as something that moves in bursts, likely tied to the acquisition integrations, rather than a steady drip. Recent live postings tracked via Indeed have skewed operational: warehouse, quality and supply chain roles based at Selby, rather than field sales.
marketPosition: On market share, GBUK doesn't publish an independent figure and neither does any market research source we could verify, so none is invented here. The closest verifiable proxy is its own claim to be a top 20 supplier to the NHS and its stated position as a market leader in specific clinical niches, which is a company claim rather than an independently audited number.

deepDive.interview: This isn't a household name, it's a mid-size, PE-backed specialist mid-integration of three recent acquisitions, so ask about how those are bedding in. Know which of the group's therapeutic areas the role sits in. It's fair game to ask about the board changes and what AMCE's growth plans look like from here.
