deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: on 29 July 2026 GE HealthCare told the market it is "reviewing strategic options" for Patient Care Solutions — the segment that holds anaesthesia machines, ventilators, patient monitoring and maternal-infant care. That is not a side business as far as the NHS is concerned. It is the half of GE that sits on most of the 20 NHS Supply Chain frameworks this supplier is named on, including Anaesthesia Machines and Ventilators, Patient Monitoring, Pulse Oximetry and Capnography, and Respiratory Solutions. In the same quarter the company merged Imaging and Advanced Visualization Solutions into one segment, Advanced Imaging Solutions, and its CFO announced he was leaving. So you are walking into a company posting record orders and backlog that is simultaneously redrawing its own org chart, and if the role sits in PCS rather than imaging, ask about it. "Reviewing strategic options" is the company's own phrase, and it does not commit them to selling anything.

prose: No UK-only turnover figure is published here. GE Medical Systems Limited files full accounts at Companies House and its most recent set covers the year ended 31 December 2025, filed on 12 July 2026 and running to 175 pages, following a 176-page set for 2024 filed on 20 August 2025. Those accounts have not been read: this run had no Companies House API key, and picking a turnover line off a filing by position is a guess about which number is turnover. Whether the filing carries a machine-readable profit and loss account is therefore unknown rather than ruled out, and the accounts-figures step of the Monday company-intelligence workflow is what settles it. Every figure below is group-wide and as filed by GE HealthCare Technologies Inc., not derived and not UK-specific.

The group trajectory is steady rather than dramatic: $19.6bn in FY2023 (up 7%), $19.7bn in FY2024 (up 1%, a flat year the company attributed largely to China), then $20.6bn in FY2025, up 4.8% reported and 3.5% organic, with growth in Imaging, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Advanced Visualization Solutions and strength specifically called out in the US and EMEA. Q2 2026 continued that: $5.3bn, up 5.7%, book-to-bill above 1 and record backlog. FY2026 guidance is 3.0% to 4.0% organic revenue growth and adjusted EPS of $4.80 to $5.00, reaffirmed with the Q2 2026 results on 29 July 2026.

For a UK conversation the useful framing is that this is a mid-single-digit grower buying its way into software: $2.3bn on Intelerad in March 2026 for cloud-first enterprise imaging, aimed at specialist clinics and ambulatory care rather than the big hospital installed base it already holds. That is directly relevant to any NHS diagnostic-hub or community-diagnostics conversation.

ownership: GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. was spun out of General Electric on 3 January 2023 and listed on Nasdaq as GEHC. GE retained a minority stake at spin-off and sold it down in stages; GE — by then renamed GE Aerospace — completed its exit of the entire remaining holding in November 2024. There is no residual GE ownership. The GE brand is used under a trademark licence, which is why the company's own UK pages still carry the line "GE is a trademark of General Electric Company. Used under trademark license." A rep who describes GE HealthCare as part of GE is three years out of date, and it is the sort of thing an interviewer notices.

The UK operating entity is GE Medical Systems Limited, company number 00252567, incorporated 8 December 1930, registered office Pollards Wood, Nightingales Lane, Chalfont St. Giles, Buckinghamshire HP8 4SP — the same address the company gives as its UK head office. Its person with significant control is recorded at Companies House as GE UK Holdings, per a PSC05 filed 1 November 2023 for a change of details dated 28 April 2023. The full current PSC entry could not be read in this session: the Companies House PSC page returned empty on three attempts. Treat the intermediate UK holding layer as Not verified until that page is read; the operating entity, its number and its officers are confirmed.

Several other GE-named UK companies exist on the register and are easy to confuse with this one, including GE HEALTHCARE LIMITED (01002610, the former Amersham plc line), GE HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED (03337033) and GE HEALTHCARE CLINICAL SYSTEMS (UK) LIMITED (01334654). NHS Supply Chain's briefs name "GE Medical Systems Ltd" or "GE Medical Systems Limited" on 17 of the 20 frameworks, "GE Healthcare" on two and "GE" on one, so 00252567 is the entity that matters for framework work.

press.text: Completes the acquisition of Intelerad for a base price of $2.3bn in cash. Cloud-first enterprise imaging and workflow, aimed at specialist clinics and ambulatory care alongside the existing hospital installed base. Expected c.$270m revenue in the first full year, c.90% recurring, adjusted EBITDA margin above 30%.

Nuffield Health and GE HealthCare open an AI-enabled diagnostic imaging hub in Oxford serving both NHS and private patients, under the £200m collaboration the two announced in January 2024 to install close to 800 pieces of imaging, ultrasound, surgical and x-ray equipment across the Nuffield network. The clearest current example of GE's UK route to market outside trust capital tenders.

Q2 2026 results. Revenue $5.3bn, up 5.7% (3.5% organic), record orders and backlog with organic order growth in every segment. Imaging and Advanced Visualization Solutions merged into a new segment, Advanced Imaging Solutions, taking the company to three reportable segments. The company states it is reviewing strategic options for Patient Care Solutions while working to return it to growth and profitability.

CFO Jay Saccaro notified the company he was resigning, for a role outside the medical technology industry. His last day was 14 August 2026, so he has already gone. On 23 July the company named George Newcomb, its Controller and Chief Accounting Officer, as interim CFO effective 14 August 2026, and began a search for a permanent successor. Recorded in the Form 8-K filed 23 July 2026, not in the Q2 results release.

marketPosition: GE HealthCare's UK position is best evidenced by its framework footprint rather than by any market-share figure, and no verified market-share percentage was found in this session, so none is stated. It is a named supplier on 20 NHS Supply Chain frameworks confirmed against the briefs, spanning CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography, fluoroscopy, nuclear medicine, mobile and static x-ray, bone densitometry, mobile image intensifiers, angiography and hybrid theatres, anaesthesia and neonatal equipment, patient monitoring, pulse oximetry and capnography, cardiac and pulmonary diagnostics, respiratory solutions, bladder scanners, electrodes and consumables, digital diagnostic solutions and total patient assessment. That is a genuinely unusual spread: most of the suppliers with comparable framework counts are consumables distributors, not capital-equipment manufacturers.

A practical caveat carried from this Hub's earlier catalogue work: an NHS Supply Chain check found no direct GE capital-equipment listings for CT, MRI, ultrasound or anaesthesia. That class of equipment is bought through trust tender and negotiation, not off the public catalogue. Framework presence means eligibility to be bought, not availability to order — worth being precise about in an interview, because getting it wrong signals someone who has read a list rather than sold anything.

place.caption: Pollards Wood, Nightingales Lane, Chalfont St Giles, Buckinghamshire HP8 4SP: the UK head office and the registered office of GE Medical Systems Limited, housing Diagnostic Imaging, Life Care Solutions, Ultrasound, Diagnostic Imaging Services and Healthcare Digital, per the company's own UK offices page. Three other UK sites: Hatfield (learning centre and repair centre for Life Care Solutions and Ultrasound, 61 Great North Road AL9 5EN), Amersham (Pharmaceutical Diagnostics), and Lisburn, Lissue Industrial Estate BT28 2RF, covering sales and service in Northern Ireland.

glassdoor.scale: /5 on Glassdoor: 4.3 worldwide; 4.2 from 87 reviews at the London location specifically
glassdoor.summary: 84% of London reviewers would recommend the company to a friend. London sub-scores: work-life balance 4.2, diversity and inclusion 4.3, culture and values 4.2, career opportunities 4.0, compensation and benefits 4.0. Career opportunities and pay are the two lowest of the six, which is a fair thing to probe on: this is a large matrixed organisation currently reorganising its segments, and progression inside one is a reasonable question to ask.

deepDive.interview: Three things will make you sound like you have done the work. First, know that GE HealthCare is a standalone Nasdaq company and has been since January 2023, with GE fully out since November 2024 — it is not a division of GE. Second, know which segment the role sits in: Advanced Imaging Solutions is the newly merged, growing half; Patient Care Solutions is the half under a stated strategic review, and it is also the half that carries most of the NHS Supply Chain framework presence. Asking a calm, non-loaded question about what the review means for UK customers is fair game and shows you read the results, not the careers page. Third, be precise about route to market: capital imaging goes through trust tender and negotiation, the frameworks establish eligibility, and the Nuffield Health collaboration shows the private and diagnostic-hub route running alongside. If the role touches diagnostic hubs or community diagnostics, the Intelerad acquisition is the thing to bring up, because it is exactly a bet on imaging outside the acute hospital.

alerts.text: FDA Letter to Health Care Providers, 'Safety and Quality Concerns with Getinge Cardiovascular Devices' (08/05/2024): names Cardiosave (IABP), Cardiohelp (ECMO) and the HLS Set. FDA states 246 MDRs relating to Cardiohelp/HLS Set in the prior 12 months, including 33 reports of serious injury or death, and recommended facilities transition away from the devices where possible. Verify directly at fda.gov before quoting MDR/injury figures client-facing.

Class I FDA recall (most serious tier) of the Flow-c/Flow-e anaesthesia machine on/off suction switch, correction notices sent ~02/05/2022 (devices distributed 02/06/2020-15/02/2022, 64 US units, 21 complaints, no injuries/deaths reported). Closure status NOT independently confirmed -- do not describe as resolved without checking the FDA record directly (IDs 193879/193880).

Earlier FDA letter (~01/03/2023) re: potential insufficient packaging sterility of the HLS Set Advanced disposable used with Cardiohelp; Getinge/Maquet issued an Urgent Medical Device Correction ~13/02/2023.

Extended a further 6 months as of the most recent update (28/05/2026), now applying to 12 specific product codes (KFK228, KFK1298, KFK1294, KFK1302, KFK1299, KFK1295, KFK1301, FNG85008, FNG85013, FNG85007, FNG85018, FNG85019). KFK593 (Blood Collection Set Safety 23G) is being sold through remaining stock and will delist once depleted.

suppliers.note: Genuine dual player, unusually for this speciality: Preanalytics business unit carries BOTH VACUETTE blood collection AND the CLiP peripheral IV cannula range (14G-26G, ported/winged) plus a SWiTCH arterial catheter — one of only two suppliers in the system tagged both Vascular access and Blood collection. Two Greiner Bio-One business units overall (Preanalytics, BioScience); BioScience is research/industry-facing, not relevant to NHS ward sales. Verified 20/07/2026 against greiner.com and the live gbo.com catalogue. Companies House 02734565 — the NHS Supply Chain catalogue names the supplying legal entity as "GREINER BIO-ONE LTD", and the register holds exactly one active company of that name (GREINER BIO-ONE LIMITED). background.text: IMPORTANT: NHS Supply Chain's catalogue still lists Magseed/Magtrace under supplier 'SYSMEX UK LTD', not Hologic — this is a stale catalogue entry. background.heading: Ownership change
background.text: Smiths Medical International Limited was officially renamed to ICU Medical International Limited on 2 October 2024 (Companies House 00362847) — also historically traded as Portex Limited (1940-2004), which is why 'Portex' persists as a live brand under this entity. Separately, ICU Medical completed a 60% divestiture of its IV Solutions (large-volume parenteral fluids) manufacturing business to Otsuka Pharmaceutical Factory, forming 'Otsuka ICU Medical LLC' (1 May 2025) — this is North America manufacturing-focused (Austin, TX + Otsuka's Asian plants) and does not appear to affect any UK-relevant device brand currently listed (Plum, Medfusion, CADD, Clave, Portex, Level 1, Jelco, Pneupac, ChemoLock/ChemoClave, Plum 360, Transpac).

background.heading: Ownership change
background.text: Major corporate change: Rhône (US private equity) completed acquisition of Invacare Holdings S.a.r.l. (Invacare Europe & APAC -- covers this UK entity) and Direct Healthcare Group (DHG) on 30/01/2026, merging them into a new combined company 'DHCare'; ARCHIMED (DHG's former backer) retains a minority stake. This is separate from, and post-dates, Invacare Corporation's 2023 US Chapter 11 -- the US lineage kept only North America, which was itself sold on again (to MIGA Holdings, Nov 2024). Invacare UK (Pencoed, Wales) is now part of DHCare, not the original US Invacare Corporation. No visible rebrand on invacare.co.uk as of this check -- still 'Invacare GB' branding, likely mid-transition. DHG's brands (Dyna-Form, System RoMedic, Raizer) are now sister brands under the same DHCare parent, no longer independent competitors.

Bariatric/plus-size patient handling: equipment, evacuation/relocation services and a training arm built around its own WISH framework (Workforce Development, Integrated Care Planning, Safe Systems of Work, Hands-On Training) and a 443 sqm Centre for Excellence simulation facility at the Wetherby site. Sells to NHS trusts, ambulance services and local authorities, and its Liftie flat lift is marketed as exclusively available through Arjo. Flagged as one to watch on two conditions, both sourced in the alerts below: a founder with a verifiable prior senior product and marketing role at an established supplier in the same category (GBUK Group), and its own branded range rather than resale only. The flag is an editorial judgement about who to keep an eye on — it is not a revenue, growth or performance claim, and no figure supports it. Products from jeenie.uk.

watch: It competes on pathway, not price — conversations lead with the WISH training framework and the 443 sqm Centre for Excellence, not the product list. Pitching equipment features answers a question it is not asking.

The founder is likely already known to your customers: 15+ years in patient handling and a National Back Exchange award mean manual-handling leads may know him by name. Treat recognition as a given, not an advantage to win.
GBUK adjacency — he ran GBUK's Banana division, so where a trust already buys GBUK patient-handling lines Jeenie is credible in the same conversation.

The same claim appears on Arjo-branded exhibition collateral: a pull-up banner reading "Liftie(R) Flat Lift System — Now exclusively available from Arjo", carrying the Jeenie.uk logo and Liftie's specification, displayed beside Arjo's own Maxi Move 5 launch banner. CHECKED 19/08/2026 AND PRESENT ON NEITHER SITE: jeenie.uk/flatlifting names no partner or distributor at all, and Arjo UK's patient-handling range lists no Liftie and no flat-lift product — so the arrangement is going to market through events and social posts ahead of either website, and a rep checking only the two sites will not see it. Both strands are the parties' own claims about themselves, which is enough to report that the claim is being made and by whom. Neither is a contract, and no value, term or lot is evidenced beyond "UK & Ireland". frameworkTiming.framework: Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling
frameworkTiming.note: Jeenie is named on none of the 122 NHS Supply Chain contract launch briefs captured to date, and the dates explain it. That tender ran through 2025, when this company was under a year old and had filed no accounts — a stage at which financial-standing and track-record requirements routinely exclude a bidder. So the absence is a function of incorporation date, not of product, capability or standing, and "not on a framework" should not be read to a customer as a quality signal. LIMITS: this record makes NO claim about whether Jeenie intends to bid, has bid, or would qualify, and 8 March 2028 is the term's stated end date, not a published tender timetable. Places on that framework are held by Arjo UK Ltd (Jeenie's own Liftie distributor), GBUK Healthcare, Etac, Direct Healthcare Group, Prism UK Medical, Select Health Care (UK), Winncare PAC, Lisclare, Invacare UK, Medstrom and Stryker UK. Three of those — Select Health Care, Prism and Direct Healthcare Group — own product lines Jeenie currently resells, so they are supplier and competitor at once.
frameworkTiming.source: NHS Supply Chain contract launch brief, count-verified at 53 suppliers

background.heading: Ownership and stage
background.text: Genuinely UK-owned: Companies House confirms 100% ownership by sole director Mr Lee James Quickmire (British, UK-resident), not a subsidiary. Incorporated 09/09/2024, first accounts filed 26/03/2026 as a micro-entity — genuinely early-stage. Zero results on NHS Supply Chain: not on the national framework, consistent with selling direct to trusts, ambulance services and local authorities.

background.heading: The catalogue is wider than the store front page
background.text: The jeenie.uk store landing page and the Jeenie Products menu both show a curated subset; the full store-products sitemap lists 32 products, including a seated transfer slide board, a handling belt and two turning aids that appear nowhere in the site navigation. Read the sitemap, not the store page. RESOLD THIRD-PARTY LINES, resale not confirmed with Jeenie: the LOCO- prefixed board, belt and turners share their SKU scheme and product names with Select Healthcare's Locomotor range (LOCO-501/LOCO-600 turners, S.U.P.A Slide, Uni Slides); "Oxford" is Prism Healthcare Group's sling brand; "Rota Stand" is a Direct Healthcare Group product name. Same pattern as the Bariquin training mannequin, which is a resold third-party brand and not a Jeenie-owned product — it is made by Bariatric Training Mannequins Ltd, trading as "Bariquins", a separate UK company.

background.heading: How the company describes itself
background.text: Mission stated as "empowering caregivers, preserving dignity and fostering collaboration"; the company reads its own name as an acronym — "Jeenie Enables Empowered Nursing, Inclusivity and Excellence". Products are built to an internal "LAMP" design framework (Limit Risk, Act With Ease, Move Safely, Promote Better Care); training is delivered through "WISH" (Workforce Development, Integrated Care Planning, Safe Systems of Work, Hands-On Training), aimed at NHS manual handling teams, falls leads, tissue viability specialists, link assessors, ward staff and procurement teams, with travel and meals covered for NHS attendees and quarterly on-site support visits. UNCONFIRMED, check before repeating to a customer: jeenie.uk states "20 years of frontline experience" while the company's LinkedIn About states "over 18 years' experience"; the Leadership panel resolves this as rounding on one career, but neither page itself names whose experience it is. LinkedIn states company size as 2–10 employees, which is a self-reported band, not the accounts figure — Companies House recorded an average headcount below one for the year to 30/09/2025.

background.heading: Centre for Excellence
background.text: A 443 sqm simulated training facility at the same Wetherby address as the registered office (Unit 416B, Street 7, Birch Park, Thorp Arch Estate, Wetherby LS23 7FG): a replica hospital ward (gantry and mobile hoists, specialist beds and chairs), a confined bedroom set, a stairwell rig and bathroom/bathtub rescue scenarios. Hired out to independent trainers and organisations, or run as bespoke courses for hospitals, councils and larger organisations. Training on offer: a "Free the Jeenie" escape-room challenge, a CPD-badged "Comprehensive Care for Plus-Size and Bariatric Patients" course (accrediting body not named on the site), an Advanced Manual Handling Workshop using weighted mannequins, and bespoke sessions. Four case studies are listed by title only (complex evacuation, evacuation from upstairs, complex care evacuation, complex care relocation), with no trust name, outcome or date on the public pages, so none is usable as a reference.

alerts.text: IMPORTANT SAFETY FLAG: the Impella heart pump range (via the Abiomed acquisition) has had a serious run of FDA Class I recalls through 2025 — Automated Impella Controller connectivity issues (linked to 3 patient deaths, corrective actions in July/Sept/Oct x2/Dec 2025), purge cassette leaks, differential pressure sensor malfunctions, and an introducer kit thrombosis risk alert. The device isn't withdrawn from market (corrections are software-update/corrective-action in nature), but this is material and currently unflagged — worth surfacing before positioning Impella with a clinician. UK entity confirmed: Johnson & Johnson Medical Limited (Companies House SC132162, Scotland, formerly Ethicon Limited). No overlap or conflict found with DePuy Synthes (J&J MedTech) or Johnson & Johnson Surgical Vision, both separate records in this dataset — the DePuy Synthes 18-24 month spin-off (announced Oct 2025) remains on track and unchanged. The reported Cerenovus (neurovascular) sale exploration (~$1-1.5bn, FT/Reuters) remains just that — no completed sale found; treat Cerenovus as still J&J-owned but under a cautious flag.

deepDive.tagline: MedTech segment of Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) · UK & Ireland HQ: Wokingham · UK orthopaedics base: Leeds
deepDive.lede: The single most important thing to know before this interview: J&J announced in October 2025 that it's spinning off its Orthopaedics business, DePuy Synthes, into a standalone company within 18 to 24 months, putting completion at roughly April to October 2027. If the role touches orthopaedics or sits at the Leeds site, that separation will very likely come up, and you should have a view on it.

prose: MedTech is J&J's smaller segment by revenue (it sits alongside Innovative Medicine, the pharma side) but it's currently the faster-growing one. Segment sales went from $30.4bn in FY2023 to $31.86bn in FY2024 (up 4.8%) to $33.79bn in FY2025 (up 6.1%). Those are the three years verifiable on a clean, consistent basis from J&J's own filings; the segment's product scope shifted around the 2023 Consumer Health spin-off (Kenvue), so the comparison is deliberately not stretched further to avoid mixing different segment definitions.

Within FY2024, Surgery and Orthopaedics were the two biggest franchises, together worth around $19bn, more than half of segment revenue. Surgery brought in $9.84bn (down 1.9%) and Orthopaedics $9.16bn. Cardiovascular, which covers electrophysiology, Abiomed and the newer Shockwave business, is the fastest mover: up 12.6% to $2.21bn in a single quarter (Q3 2025), and it's explicitly where J&J says future MedTech investment is being weighted.

ownership: J&J runs two segments: Innovative Medicine (pharma, about 64% of group revenue) and MedTech (about 36%). MedTech is organised into four franchises: Orthopaedics (DePuy Synthes), Surgery (Ethicon, Mentor, Acclarent), Cardiovascular (Biosense Webster, Cerenovus, Abiomed, Shockwave) and Vision. In September 2023 the MedTech and pharma brands were folded under the single Johnson & Johnson name, retiring some of the old standalone product-line branding.

The live structural story is the Orthopaedics separation. J&J is carving DePuy Synthes out as its own standalone, investment-grade company, targeting a $50bn+ global orthopaedics market and roughly seven million patients a year. J&J's own framing is that it would be the largest, most comprehensive orthopaedics-focused company in the sector on completion. For scale, DePuy Synthes generated around $9.2bn in 2024, over 10% of J&J's total revenue and about 29% of MedTech segment sales. Its named competitors post-separation are Stryker ($22.6bn total revenue in 2024, including $9bn from orthopaedics) and Zimmer Biomet ($7.7bn total revenue).

press.text: J&J announces intent to separate its Orthopaedics business into a standalone company, DePuy Synthes, within 18 to 24 months. Namal Nawana named Worldwide President to lead it through and beyond the separation. This is still in progress and is the single biggest structural fact about this employer right now.

Johnson & Johnson MedTech signs a Memorandum of Understanding with Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, tied to the government's New Hospital Programme and the Leeds General Infirmary rebuild, to collaborate on MedTech innovation, R&D and skills in the city where DePuy Synthes has its UK manufacturing and R&D base.
J&J unifies its MedTech and pharmaceutical businesses under a single Johnson & Johnson brand, retiring separate product-line branding in external communications.
J&J MedTech UK opens an Innovation Suite at its Wokingham Pinewood Campus: a replica operating room and surgical skills zone used to train healthcare professionals.

hiring: J&J doesn't publish a rolling count of UK roles filled over the last 12 months, so no verified historical figure is given here. What's checkable: their own UK careers page currently lists around 40 open roles, spanning functions from Customer Management and HR (both Leeds) to Finance (Wokingham), which gives a live snapshot of where hiring is concentrated right now rather than a full year's history.

place.caption: DePuy Synthes, St Anthony's Road, Beeston, Leeds LS11 8DT. Street level imagery isn't available here, so this is the satellite view. The UK HQ and Innovation Suite sit at Pinewood Campus, Nine Mile Ride, Wokingham RG40 3EW.

glassdoor.summary: MedTech doesn't have its own Glassdoor listing, its reviews sit inside the main Johnson & Johnson page tagged by business segment, so treat this as directional rather than MedTech-specific. The recurring pattern: people value the compliance discipline and the genuine global scale, and push back on a layered, hierarchical structure that can slow things down.

deepDive.interview: Have a view on the DePuy Synthes separation, expect it to come up if the role is anywhere near orthopaedics. Be clear whether the role sits in MedTech or Innovative Medicine. Expect a formal, competency-based process built around Our Credo, J&J's founding values statement. Know Hugo Breda's name if you're interviewing into the UK & Ireland business.

background.text: Ownership/governance note: Sybill Storz — daughter of founder Karl Storz, long-standing managing director then supervisory board chair — died 28 November 2025, aged 88, reflected in a recent Companies House PSC filing change. suppliers.ownership: Not an acquisition. Kimberly-Clark Corporation spun off its health care division to its own shareholders on 31 October 2014 as Halyard Health, Inc.; Halyard Health, Inc. was renamed Avanos Medical, Inc. on 28 June 2018. Separately, on 30 April 2018 the Surgical and Infection Prevention business, including the 'Halyard Health' name itself, was sold to Owens & Minor, Inc. So the old Kimberly-Clark surgical consumables sit with Owens & Minor under the Halyard brand, while Avanos holds only pain management and specialty nutrition. Effective 31/10/2014. Source: Halyard Health, Inc. Form 10-K for 2014, filed with the SEC 13/03/2015, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1606498/000160649815000009/halyardhealth_10k2014.htm, read 21/08/2026: 'On October 31, 2014, Kimberly-Clark distributed all of our capital stock to its shareholders and completed the previously announced spin-off of its healthcare division'. Avanos Medical, Inc. Form 10-K for 2018, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1606498/000160649819000018/avns2018form10k.htm, read 21/08/2026: 'On April 30, 2018, we closed the sale of our Surgical and Infection Prevention (S&IP) business, which included the name Halyard Health ... to Owens & Minor, Inc.' SEC EDGAR company record CIK 0001606498, read 21/08/2026: name AVANOS MEDICAL, INC., former name Halyard Health, Inc. from 2014-05-06 to 2018-06-28. Cross-checked against avanos.com (read 21/08/2026), whose portfolio is MIC-KEY, CORTRAK, NEOMED, GAME READY, COOLIEF and ON-Q only, and kimberly-clark.com/en-us/company/about (read 21/08/2026), whose brand navigation lists only Adult Care, Baby and Child Care, Family Care, Feminine Care and Kimberly-Clark Professional, with no healthcare or medical device category.

Companies House 00062537 — the NHS Supply Chain catalogue names the supplying legal entity as "MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED", and the register holds exactly one active company of that name (MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED). Merged 21/08/2026 by merge_duplicates.py: one company was showing as 2 suppliers. Folded in: "Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Ltd". Company number 00062537. Companies House shows MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED (00062537) with BUNZL RETAIL & HEALTHCARE SUPPLIES LIMITED as a previous name, ceased 12/06/2023; the only other register hit for that name is NF004224, an oversea-company registration that is converted-closed and never traded as a separate business. deepDive.tagline: Castle Donington multi-speciality distributor of surgical, wound care, clinical care and infection control consumables, owned by the Dutch Mediq group since December 2022, and the buyer of the old Bunzl healthcare business, H & R Healthcare and C&P Medical.

deepDive.lede: Two things to get straight before you walk in. First, do not quote a growth number at Mediq: its last three filed periods are nine months, fifteen months and twelve months long, so any year-on-year comparison you build from the headline figures is wrong. The company's own like-for-like figure is 3.7% underlying sales growth in 2024. Second, this is a business spending money, not making it: turnover of 155.1m in the year to 31 December 2024, an operating loss of 4.5m after 6.2m of one-off costs for consolidating four sites into one national distribution centre, a loss before tax of 6.6m, and then 14m of fresh cash equity from the parent on 27 August 2025. The commercial shape that follows from that is the useful part. Sixty-one people in selling against 155m of sales, and the selling headcount fell by ten in the year while the warehouse grew by eleven. Both the sales director and the commercial director are named on the company's own site. And two live things are worth a diary note: the Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets framework it sits on ends on 30 September 2026, and Mediq is in the middle of pulling its own-brand ranges under a single Mediq Select identity.

stats.n: £155,094,000. Read from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its profit and loss account, page 16, and repeated in the strategic report on page 3 and in note 2 on page 24, in the full accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 filed at Companies House on 14 March 2025 (00062537). By destination: UK £151,472,000, Europe £3,501,000, Rest of World £121,000. The filing is a scanned PDF with no iXBRL tagging at all — ?format=xhtml returns HTTP 500 — which is why company-financials.json in this Hub still shows no turnover for the company while this record does.

£4,481,000 operating loss, from the same profit and loss account on page 16. The strategic report on page 3 states that this includes £6,202,000 of one-off costs associated with business restructure and site consolidation during the year. Loss before taxation was £6,645,000 and the loss for the financial year after a £1,514,000 tax credit was £5,131,000. Gross profit was £34,360,000 on £155,094,000 of sales.

The SH01 return of allotment filed at Companies House on 27 August 2025 records 14,000,000 ordinary shares of £1 allotted on 27 August 2025, amount paid £14,000,000, amount unpaid £0, and states "No shares allotted other than for cash". Note 17 of the 2024 accounts had put called-up share capital at £1,010,537 (1,010,537 £1 ordinary shares) at 31 December 2024, so the statement of capital on the same filing reads GBP 15,010,537. This is eight months after a £6.6m pre-tax loss and it is cash, not a book entry.

Note 7 of the 2024 accounts, page 26: Selling 61 (2023 period: 71), Distribution and warehouse 227 (216), General and administration 64 (64), total 352 (351). Aggregate payroll cost £16,249,000, of which wages and salaries £14,411,000. The company's own About page separately says the Mediq group has more than 2,500 employees across 14 countries; that is the international group, not this UK company.

Note 7 of the 2024 accounts, page 26. It fell from 71 in the previous period while Distribution and warehouse rose from 216 to 227, which is consistent with the four-into-one distribution consolidation described in the same accounts. Sixty-one selling heads against £155.1m of turnover is roughly £2.5m of revenue per person in selling — that ratio is arithmetic on two figures from the same filing, and it is a measure of how the company is organised, not of how good its salespeople are.

Named supplier on ten NHS Supply Chain contract launch briefs: Advanced Wound Care, Enteral Feeding Bile Bags and Associated Products, Examination Gloves, General Wound Care, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products, Respiratory Solutions, Skin Cleansing Disinfection and Hygiene, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, Urology and Bowel Management, and Wound Closure. Ranking rule, so you can judge it: count the briefs that name the company, one per framework, across the 1,199 suppliers in this Hub's seed. On that count 1,076 suppliers are named on at least one brief, 21 are named on more than ten, and Mediq is joint twenty-second with GenX MediCare, Hospital Services Limited and Rocialle Healthcare. It is a count of frameworks, not of revenue, lots or market share, and nothing here is inferred from product ranges.

Companies House company 00062537, read 22/08/2026, status Active, SIC 46900 non-specialised wholesale trade. The number is old because the entity is: the register records it as BRIERLEY-ALMOND LIMITED from 13 June 1899 to 28 January 2000, BUNZL RETAIL SUPPLIES LIMITED to 28 September 2007, BUNZL RETAIL & HEALTHCARE SUPPLIES LIMITED to 12 June 2023, and MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED since. The company's own website footer publishes the same number as "Registered No. 0062537".

series.axisNote: Only one of this company's three filed periods is a normal twelve months, so only one is charted. The period ended 2 October 2022 was NINE months and the period ended 31 December 2023 was FIFTEEN months, both stated as such in the company's own strategic reports, and putting bars of different lengths side by side would manufacture a growth story that is not in the filings. Those two figures are given in full in the prose below instead. prose: The three filed periods, with their lengths, are: nine months to 2 October 2022, turnover for continuing operations £144,358,000 and for discontinued operations £247,896,000, a total of £392,254,000; fifteen months to 31 December 2023, £187,176,000, all continuing; and twelve months to 31 December 2024, £155,094,000. The £247.9m of discontinued turnover in the first of those is the Bunzl retail business that did not come with the healthcare business, and the year end moved from Bunzl's early-October date to 31 December because the owner changed. Any comparison drawn straight across those three headline numbers is meaningless, and that is why only 2024 is charted.

The loss is a programme, not a collapse, and the accounts say so. The strategic report for 2024 records that operations underwent significant restructure with four sites consolidated into one national distribution centre, together with new systems, and that the £4,481,000 operating loss includes £6,202,000 of one-off costs for exactly that. Strip those and the year is around £1.7m of operating profit on the same figures — that subtraction is arithmetic on two numbers from page 3 of the filing, offered so a reader can judge it, and it is not a figure the company itself publishes. The fifteen-month period to 31 December 2023 also ran an operating loss, of £5,527,000, so 2024 is the second loss-making period in a row on the face of the accounts.

Two balance-sheet moves are worth carrying into a commercial conversation. Bank loans and overdrafts in creditors due within one year went from £226,000 at 31 December 2023 to £9,674,000 at 31 December 2024 (note 15, page 32), and interest payable rose from £295,000 to £2,217,000 (note 4, page 24); the accounts record that bank loans and overdrafts are guaranteed under a cross guarantee structure by certain group companies in a bank account pooling arrangement. Net assets fell from £20,354,000 to £16,223,000. No dividend was paid in 2024; £68,400,000 was paid in the previous period (note 18, page 33), when the business was still leaving Bunzl. Then £14,000,000 of cash equity went in on 27 August 2025. Read together, that is an owner funding a rebuild rather than taking money out.

The directors' own list of pressures, from the strategic report, is worth knowing because it is the conversation they are already having internally: UK government policy influencing NHS spending, failure to secure new sales contracts or renegotiate existing ones, competitive pressure forcing price reductions, cyber-attack, supply chain risk including freight, product cost, tariffs and the effect of international conflict on trade routes, and regulation targeting certain plastic products. On inflation they say they have used selective product price increases and developing own-brand product sales at lower cost — which is the commercial logic behind Mediq Select.

ownership: MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED, company number 00062537, registered office Mediq House, Arundel Avenue, Castle Donington, Derby, DE74 2HJ, is a private limited company incorporated on 13 June 1899 and currently Active. Its Companies House persons with significant control register, read 22/08/2026, holds one active entry: Mediq Holding Uk Limited, company 12477997, of 3 Redcliff Road, Melton Park, Melton, Hull HU14 3RS, notified 19 December 2022, holding 75% or more of the shares and of the voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. The only other entry is a ceased one, Bunzl Holding Gtl Limited of York House, 45 Seymour Street, London, notified 6 April 2016 and ceased 19 December 2022. That ceased date is the change of control.

Above the UK holding company, note 1 of the 2024 accounts states plainly on page 19 that the ultimate controlling company is Mediq Top Holding BV, and the directors' report on page 9 records that Mediq Top Holding B.V. as ultimate parent has confirmed its intention and ability to provide continued financial support to the company for at least 12 months from the date of approval of the financial statements, which is the basis on which the accounts are prepared as a going concern. The company reports under FRS 101 and takes the reduced-disclosure exemptions, so there is no cash flow statement and no key management remuneration in the filing.

The 2023 filing explains where the money went on the way out of Bunzl. Net assets fell from £93,673,000 at 2 October 2022 to £20,354,000 at 31 December 2023, and the strategic report attributes that mainly to the company assigning an intra-group loan of £57,654,000 with Bunzl UK Ltd, which had arisen from the transfer of the Retail division, to Bunzl Holdings GTL. Read alongside the £68,400,000 of dividends in the same period, the entity that Mediq bought was stripped of the retail business and its associated balances first.

Two UK businesses have been folded into this company since the 2024 year end, and both still exist as separate names in NHS Supply Chain's own supplier lists. Note 19 of the 2024 accounts (page 33) records that on 1 January 2025, as part of a group reorganisation, the trade, assets and liabilities of H & R Healthcare Limited were transferred to the Company at a book value of £3,258,000, made up of debtors £4,467,000 and cash £392,000 against creditors £1,551,000, deferred tax £45,000 and provisions £5,000. H & R Healthcare Limited, company 05817827 of Melton, Hull, is still an active company at 22/08/2026, but its recorded nature of business is now SIC 82990, other business support service activities, and its confirmation statement was due on 23 May 2026 and had not been filed when the register was read.

C&P Medical is the second, and the register is unusually clear about it. C & P MEDICAL TRADING LIMITED, company 03613589, incorporated 11 August 1998, now has its registered office at Mediq House, Castle Donington, and its one active person with significant control is C&P MEDICAL HOLDINGS LIMITED, company 16282719, notified 30 August 2025. That holding company was incorporated on 28 February 2025 and its own active person with significant control is MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED, company 00062537, notified 2 September 2025 at 75% or more of the shares; its ceased entries are Mr Peter John Shaw and Mrs Julia Lauren Shaw, both notified 28 February 2025 and ceased 2 September 2025. So C&P sits directly under this company, not merely under the wider group, and the date on the register matches the company's own announcement of 03.09.25.

press.text: Mediq announced the acquisition of Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Limited in the UK, including what it called its flagship brand, 365 Healthcare. The Companies House PSC register dates the change of control to 19 December 2022.

The registered company name changed from Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Limited to Mediq Healthcare UK Limited, recorded both on the Companies House register and in the company's own strategic report for the period ended 31 December 2023.
Mediq announced Arjen Linders as Chief Executive Officer of the group, effective 1 March 2024.

The company said its new 280,000 sq ft base at Castle Donington, with 30 loading bays, would be fully operational by the end of 2024, and published drone footage of the new racking system as the centre for its UK operations.
Mediq UK published its first Carbon Reduction Plan and an ambition to be Net Zero by 2045.
Mediq UK announced it had relocated its head office to a new purpose-built facility at Castle Donington and expanded with a new North London office at Cheshunt, Hertfordshire.
Mediq UK announced Rory Batt as Managing Director of Mediq UK alongside his role as Group Chief Digital Officer.

Mediq announced that C&P Medical, which it described as having more than 25 years in the sector, had become part of Mediq, and told customers to continue trading with either or both organisations as before. The Companies House PSC register dates Mediq Healthcare UK Limited's control of C&P Medical Holdings Limited to 2 September 2025.
Mediq UK announced the appointment of Stephanie Chomyn as Finance Director.
Mediq announced its intention to acquire Medguard Healthcare, an Irish supplier of medical products and services to acute and private hospitals, clinics and nursing homes.
Mediq announced that Medguard Healthcare had joined Mediq. Medguard's Ashbourne, Co. Meath address now appears on Mediq UK's own locations page as its Republic of Ireland site.

Mediq announced the launch of Mediq Select, bringing its own-brand ranges — it names 365 Healthcare, Klinion, Absorin and Curion — together under a single name, with products, specifications and product codes unchanged. It says the rollout is phased across its European markets including the UK, starting with the 365 Healthcare range of surgical gowns, and quotes group CEO Arjen Linders, UK Managing Director Rory Batt and group Chief Procurement Officer Guido Mouws. The item carries no date on the company's news page.

hiring: No vacancy count is published here. Mediq UK routes careers to a group-wide site, careersatmediq.com, which renders its vacancy list client-side; the list could not be read from the page source in this session, and a number guessed from a partial read would be worse than none. What the site does show is the shape of the group's hiring, in six categories: Supply Chain and Logistics, Customer Service, Commercial, Business Support, Digital and Innovation, and Homecare and Nursing.

The filed accounts are the reliable headcount signal, and they point one way. Note 7 of the 2024 accounts shows Selling down from 71 to 61 and Distribution and warehouse up from 216 to 227 across a year in which four distribution sites became one. Total average monthly headcount barely moved, 351 to 352, so this is a business that reshaped rather than grew: ten fewer people carrying the bag, eleven more in the warehouse.
marketPosition: What is independently checkable is the framework footprint, and the spread matters more than the count. NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name this company on ten frameworks: Advanced Wound Care (1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027, 56 suppliers), Enteral Feeding, Bile Bags and Associated Products (5 September 2025 to 13 July 2027, 19), Examination Gloves (27 November 2023 to 25 April 2027, 19), General Wound Care (24 June 2026 to 23 June 2028, 28), Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products (3 October 2022 to 30 September 2026, 27), Respiratory Solutions (1 August 2022 to 15 June 2027, 37), Skin Cleansing, Disinfection and Hygiene (16 February 2026 to 15 February 2028, 29), Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (4 August 2026 to 3 August 2028, 40), Urology and Bowel Management (21 February 2024 to 20 February 2027, 57) and Wound Closure (19 January 2026 to 18 January 2030, 39). Four of the ten started in 2026.

One of those ten has a date on it. NHS Supply Chain's own brief page for Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products, read at source on 22/08/2026, states that the framework "starts on 3 October 2022, runs for 48 months and ends on 30 September 2026", that this includes a 24 month extension, and that its type is Contract Extension, reference Project_12 ITT_382. That is a live end date about five and a half weeks from this record being written. The same page still lists the supplier as "Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Ltd", a company name the register retired on 12 June 2023, which is worth knowing if you are searching NHS Supply Chain for this company and finding nothing.

The commercial footprint is wider than those ten rows suggest, because two other names in this Hub are now the same operation. H & R Healthcare Ltd is named on three briefs (Examination Gloves, Negative Pressure Wound Therapy, Procedure Packs) and its trade moved into this company on 1 January 2025; C&P Medical Trading Ltd is named on two (Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation, Urology and Bowel Management) and has sat under this company since 2 September 2025. Counting distinct framework names across the three supplier records — that is the rule, one count per framework name, duplicates dropped — gives thirteen frameworks under one commercial roof, the ten above plus Negative Pressure Wound Therapy, Procedure Packs and Orthotics, Podiatry and Immobilisation. The three records are deliberately not merged in this Hub: they are three live registered companies and NHS Supply Chain still names them separately.

The range, as the company itself groups it on its site read 22/08/2026, is four categories. Surgical Supplies: face protection, haemostats, headwear, patient wear, scrub and warming apparel, specialist surgical drapes, drape sets, drapes, gowns and theatre consumables. Clinical Care: bedding, colour lancets, diagnostics, injection and infusion, oxygen and aerosol therapy, patient care essentials, procedure packs, suction consumables, underpads and urology. Infection Control: cleaning and disinfection, hand hygiene and skin care, instrument sterilisation, medical gloves and gauntlets, PPE, sharps management and waste disposal. Wound Care: bandages and medical tapes, bio compression, Hidrawear, dressings, swabs, closure strips and wound management. The brands it lists are 365 Healthcare, Bio Compression Systems, Cardinal Health, Chemviron, Curion, Hartmann, Healthgard, HidraMed Solutions, Klinion and Kliniderm, NOSA, Premier, PolyMem, Safecare, Sorbaderm and Universal.

It can wholesale medicines, and most device-and-consumables distributors cannot. The MHRA register entry for UK WDA(H) 34759, read 22/08/2026, names MEDIQ HEALTHCARE UK LIMITED as authorisation holder at Mediq House, Castle Donington, under Regulation 18 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012, with a document date of 14 August 2026. The authorised operations are procurement, holding, supply, products imported from countries on a list, and products certified under Article 51 of Directive 2001/83/EC; the categories of product handled at the site are Prescription Only Medicines, General Sales List and Pharmacy, and the annex also carries site details for homeopathic products. If you are competing on a tender that mixes devices with medicines, that licence is a real difference and not a marketing claim.

This Hub holds no own-site product range for Mediq, and that is a reading outcome rather than a thin catalogue. The crawler recorded a refusal against www.mediq.co.uk on 12/08/2026 with the reason "robots.txt disallows automated reading of this site", and recorded the same reason against mediq.co.uk on 22/08/2026 under the H & R Healthcare record. Read by hand on 22/08/2026, neither host serves a robots.txt at all: both return the site's own HTML with HTTP 200 for that path, which is how a single-page-application site answers any unknown URL. The four-category range above was read from the company's own pages in this session. Do not read an absent product list for this company as an absent product range.

deepDive.interview: Match the period before you quote a number, because this is the company where that goes wrong: nine months to October 2022, fifteen months to December 2023, twelve months to December 2024. The only like-for-like figure in the filings is the directors' own 3.7% underlying sales growth in 2024. On the commercial position, the honest read is a business mid-rebuild: a £4.5m operating loss carrying £6.2m of restructure and site-consolidation costs, bank borrowing up from £0.2m to £9.7m, interest up from £0.3m to £2.2m, and then £14m of cash equity from the parent on 27 August 2025 — an owner funding it rather than harvesting it. Ask what the new Castle Donington centre has actually changed on lead times, because that is what the money bought and it is the claim they will want to make. Ask about Mediq Select: they are consolidating own-brand ranges under one identity, starting with 365 Healthcare surgical gowns, and their own strategic report names growing own-brand sales at lower cost as an inflation response — so on any line where you compete with an own-brand equivalent, you are competing with a strategy, not a product. Put 30 September 2026 in the diary: NHS Supply Chain's own brief says the Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets framework ends that day, and the brief still names the supplier as Bunzl Retail & Healthcare Supplies Ltd. And know who you are dealing with — the company publishes its own leadership team, so Nick Heys is Commercial Director, Dougie Payne is Sales Director and Helen Twigg is UKI Sourcing Director, while only Rory Batt and Stephanie Chomyn are on the register. With 61 people in selling against £155m of sales, and ten fewer of them than the year before, coverage on the ground is thin: that is where a specialist wins, and it is why Mediq will sell breadth of range through one account instead.

deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Medline stopped being a private family-and-private-equity business eight months ago. It listed on Nasdaq on 17 December 2025 as MDLN, raising $6.27bn in the largest US IPO of 2025, and it now reports quarterly. The most recent set, published 5 August 2026, is a genuinely mixed picture. Sales rose 11.6% in the quarter and the company raised its full-year organic sales outlook, but net income fell 58.3%, mostly because of a $336m loss from a fire at its Tracy, California distribution centre, and it cut full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance from $3.5bn to $3.6bn down to $3.3bn to $3.4bn. In the UK the direction is much less ambiguous: seven of the eighteen NHS Supply Chain frameworks Medline is named on started during 2026, the most recent of them on 10 August. That is a company taking NHS ground while its US parent absorbs a bad quarter, and the gap between those two stories is the interesting question in the room.

prose: No UK turnover figure can be read for this company. Medline Industries Limited (Companies House 03238147) files full accounts, most recently for the year ended 31 December 2024, but the tagged accounts carry no turnover, and its registered SIC code is 82990, other business support service activities, rather than a distribution code. The UK holding company above it, Medline Stellar UK Limited (07567112, activities of distribution holding companies), sits at the same Warrington address. So the figures below are the listed US parent's, as reported in its own filings, and they are not a proxy for UK trading.

Medline Inc.'s audited consolidated net sales were $23,231m in FY2023, $25,507m in FY2024 and $28,432m in FY2025, all three read from the consolidated statements of comprehensive income in the Form 10-K filed 25 February 2026. FY2025 net income was $1.2bn, a 4.1% margin, and Adjusted EBITDA $3.5bn, a 12.2% margin. The business splits almost evenly between its two segments by sales and not at all by profit: Medline Brand took $13.7bn of FY2025 sales (48.3%) but $3.3bn of segment Adjusted EBITDA (80.6%), while Supply Chain Solutions took $14.7bn of sales (51.7%) and $0.8bn of segment Adjusted EBITDA (19.4%). If the role you are interviewing for sells Medline-branded product, it sits in the half of the business that carries the margin, and that is worth knowing.

The first half of 2026 continued the top line and broke the bottom line. Six-month net sales were $15.0bn, up 11.1%, while net income fell 42.3% to $378m. Two one-off items sit inside that: a $336m loss from the fire at the Tracy, California distribution centre, before expected insurance recoveries, and a $243m net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds recognised after the US Supreme Court ruled in February 2026 that those tariffs were unauthorised ($332m of refunds less $89m of accrued customer repayments). The guidance cut announced on 5 August 2026 was attributed to higher than expected inflationary pressure from the Middle East conflict, increased operational investment to support customer demand, quality remediation efforts and retail channel softness.

ownership: Medline was founded in 1966 and is headquartered at 3 Lakes Drive, Northfield, Illinois. It was owned by the Mills family until June 2021, when investment funds associated with Blackstone, The Carlyle Group and Hellman & Friedman took a majority stake in one of the largest leveraged buyouts on record. The company went public on 17 December 2025: it priced 216,034,482 shares of Class A common stock at $29.00 on 16 December, raising approximately $6.27bn, and began trading the following day on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker MDLN. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities and J.P. Morgan were global coordinators and lead bookrunners.

The pre-IPO owners have not left. The 10-K filed 25 February 2026 records that the Designating Stockholders, defined in that filing as investment funds associated with Blackstone Inc., The Carlyle Group Inc. and Hellman & Friedman LLC together with members of the Mills family, beneficially owned or controlled approximately 67.0% of the combined voting power, and hold contractual rights to nominate directors. A secondary offering on 26 May 2026 sold a further 72,554,594 shares at $37.00, raising about $2.68bn entirely for the selling stockholders (the company received no proceeds), and took that figure to approximately 55.4%. The practical read for a rep is that this is still a sponsor-influenced business that now also has quarterly public reporting discipline on top of it.

The UK entity is Medline Industries Limited, company number 03238147, incorporated 15 August 1996 and confirmed active at Companies House on 17/08/2026, registered at 3rd Floor, Quayside, Wilderspool Business Park, Greenalls Avenue, Warrington WA4 6HL. Its sole person with significant control is Medline Stellar UK Limited (07567112, a distribution holding company at the same address), notified 6 April 2016, holding 75% or more of the shares.

hiring: Medline's European careers board carried 40 open roles on 17/08/2026, and exactly one of them was in the UK: a QA Specialist W&D at Bicester. The company's separate US-facing Workday board carried 611 roles the same day and returned none for the United Kingdom or Warrington. No salary figures are published on either board. Read this as a company whose European hiring is concentrated in the Netherlands, Germany, France and Slovakia rather than in Britain, not as proof there is no UK field-sales recruitment: UK commercial roles are also advertised through recruiters and job boards this check did not cover.
marketPosition: Medline describes itself as "the largest provider of medical-surgical (med-surg) products and supply chain solutions serving all points of care", and, unusually, it publishes the basis: the claim rests on its own 2025 net sales measured against the publicly reported med-surg net sales of companies that are both med-surg manufacturers and distributors. That is the company's own derivation, disclosed in its 10-K, not an independently audited market share, and no market-share percentage is stated here because none was found in a verifiable source.

The verifiable measure of UK scale is the NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 18 separate frameworks, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs on 17/08/2026, spanning examination and surgical gloves, procedure packs, single-use theatre protective wear, wound closure, advanced wound care, airway management, respiratory solutions, electrosurgical consumables, syringes and needles, minimally invasive surgery, urology and bowel management, pressure area care and patient handling, physiotherapy and occupational therapy, textiles, tray wrap and sterilisation, skin cleansing, and clinical and sharps waste management. Seven of the 18 started during 2026, which is a supplier gaining category ground rather than holding it.

Scale in Britain is commercial rather than industrial. The 10-K lists Medline's largest non-US employee populations as Mexico, the Dominican Republic, India, Canada, Slovakia, France, China, Japan, Germany and Australia; the UK is not among them. Globally the company runs 30 manufacturing facilities, 24 of them in North America, and 70 distribution centres, warehouses, cross-docks and transship facilities, and manufactures roughly a third of its own-brand products.

deepDive.interview: This is a newly public company, so for the first time you can read what it tells its investors. Two things are fair game. First, the 5 August 2026 guidance split: sales outlook raised, profit outlook cut, with quality remediation named as one of the reasons. Asking how that lands on the UK business is a serious question, not a gotcha. Second, the framework run: seven NHS Supply Chain frameworks started in 2026 alone, which means implementation work across trusts right now, and a question about how the UK team is resourcing that shows you have read the actual award record. Know which segment the role sits in, because Medline Brand and Supply Chain Solutions are close to equal on sales and nowhere near equal on margin. And check who your interviewer reports to: the UK entity has only two statutory directors and no company secretary, so UK commercial leadership is not visible from the register.

deepDive.tagline: Medtronic plc (NYSE: MDT), Irish-incorporated · UK entity Medtronic Limited, Croxley Park, Watford · Centre of Digital Excellence, Old Street, London
deepDive.lede: The single most important thing to know before this interview: Medtronic is halfway through separating its Diabetes business, and halfway is the operative word. MiniMed listed on Nasdaq as MMED on 6 March 2026, but Medtronic still held about 90% of it when the offering closed three days later, and the split-off that actually completes the separation is expected around six months after the listing, with the whole thing targeted for the end of calendar 2026. If the role touches insulin pumps or CGM you are interviewing at a business on its way out of the group, and you need a view on that. Everywhere else the story runs the other way: FY2026 revenue of $36.4bn was the company's fastest annual growth in ten years, and Cardiovascular is where it came from.

prose: Medtronic's fiscal year ends in late April, so FY2026 closed on 24 April 2026 and "this year" means something different here than it does at a calendar-year employer. Group revenue ran $31.686bn in FY2022, $31.227bn in FY2023, $32.364bn in FY2024, $33.537bn in FY2025 and $36.364bn in FY2026. The shape matters more than the total: revenue actually fell in FY2023, ground back up over the two years after it, then rose 8.4% in FY2026, which the company itself calls its highest annual revenue growth in ten years. If you are asked why now, that turn is the honest answer.

The growth is not evenly spread, and knowing which segment your role sits in is most of the interview. In FY2026 Cardiovascular was $13.976bn (up 12.0%), Neuroscience $10.287bn (up 4.5%), Medical Surgical $8.815bn (up 4.9%) and Diabetes $3.112bn (up 12.9%). Inside Cardiovascular, Cardiac Ablation Solutions revenue rose 78% globally on pulsed-field ablation, which is the growth story the company leads with. Diabetes grew fast and is being separated anyway, so its numbers describe MiniMed's prospects rather than Medtronic's. Guidance for FY2027 is 6.75% to 7.25% organic growth.

ownership: "Where is Medtronic based" has no single answer, and getting it right is free credibility. Medtronic plc is Irish-incorporated. Its own locations page names the principal executive office as Building 2, Parkmore Business Park West, Co. Galway, and the operational headquarters as 710 Medtronic Parkway, Minneapolis. Ireland is the legal domicile, dating from the 2015 Covidien acquisition and redomiciliation; Minneapolis is where the business is run from.

The group reports in four segments: Cardiovascular, Neuroscience, Medical Surgical and Diabetes. Diabetes is the one that is leaving. Medtronic announced its intent to separate the business in May 2025, the unit was renamed MiniMed, and it listed 28,000,000 shares on Nasdaq at $20 on 6 March 2026, raising $560m, with the offering closing on 9 March 2026. Medtronic held approximately 90.03% of MiniMed at that close. The company's stated preferred route to finish the job is a split-off, an exchange of Medtronic shares for MiniMed shares, and its own FY2026 results release still says a final decision on structure has not been reached. So MiniMed today is a separately listed subsidiary, not an independent company.

The UK entity is Medtronic Limited, company number 01070807, incorporated 8 September 1972, active, registered at Building 9 Croxley Park, Hatters Lane, Watford WD18 8WW. It files full accounts, last made up to 25 April 2025, next due 31 January 2027. Those accounts are filed as a PDF carrying no tagged figures, so no UK turnover and no UK headcount is published here. That is a filing-format fact rather than a gap: picking the turnover line off a PDF by position would be a guess about which number is turnover, and this file does not guess.

Two separate UK operations sit behind that one company number. The commercial business runs from Croxley Park in Watford. Engineering runs from London, where Medtronic doubled its site in September 2025 to 25,000 sq ft and more than 200 staff, branding it the Centre of Digital Excellence and calling it the company's largest global digital centre for AI and robotics in surgery. It sits at Old Street. If you are interviewing into surgical robotics, that is a UK asset worth naming.

press.text: MiniMed, Medtronic's Diabetes business, began trading on Nasdaq as MMED. The IPO of 28,000,000 shares at $20 closed on 9 March 2026 raising $560m, leaving Medtronic with approximately 90.03%. The split-off that completes the separation is expected roughly six months after the listing, with the whole separation targeted for the end of calendar 2026. This is the single biggest structural fact about this employer right now, and it is not finished.

FY2026 results: revenue $36.364bn, up 8.4% as reported and 5.8% organic, which the company describes as its highest annual revenue growth in ten years. Cardiac Ablation Solutions revenue rose 78% globally. FY2027 guidance is 6.75% to 7.25% organic growth.

Medtronic disclosed unauthorised access to certain corporate IT systems in April 2026. The company says it has identified no impact to product security or patient safety, to manufacturing and distribution, or to financial reporting, and that hospital customer networks are separate from Medtronic IT networks. It reported 3,834,294 individuals affected and began notifying them with 24 months of credit and dark-web monitoring. Expect a trust IT or procurement contact to raise this, and know what Medtronic has actually said rather than what the headlines said.

Medtronic doubled its London site to 25,000 sq ft and more than 200 staff, naming it the Centre of Digital Excellence and calling it its largest global digital centre for AI and robotics in surgery. Part of a stated multi-million-dollar, five-year UK investment.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust and Medtronic signed a UK-first Research, Development and Innovation collaboration agreement covering cardiovascular, neuroscience, medical surgery and diabetes, building on a decade of existing work together.

Medtronic appointed John Groetelaars and Bill Jellison to the board and created a Growth Committee and an Operating Committee, both chaired by Geoff Martha, alongside continuing the Diabetes separation. An investor day was set for mid-calendar 2026.

hiring: Medtronic publishes no rolling count of UK roles filled, and its jobs site could not be read from this run on 13/08/2026, so no open-roles number is given here rather than an estimate. What is checkable: the London Centre of Digital Excellence passed 200 staff in September 2025 and is the company's largest global digital centre for AI and robotics in surgery, and the UK commercial entity is registered at Croxley Park, Watford. Those are the two ends of the UK organisation, engineering in London and commercial in Watford, and they hire for very different things.

glassdoor.summary: This is Medtronic worldwide, not the UK business and not the sales organisation, so treat it as directional. 67% would recommend the company to a friend, but only 53% approve of the CEO, and senior management scores 3.0, the lowest of the six category ratings; career opportunities is 3.4. The recurring pattern is a strong mission and a brand that travels well on a CV, set against large-company bureaucracy and a lot of variation by manager and business unit.

deepDive.interview: Have a view on the MiniMed separation, and know it is not finished: Medtronic still held about 90% of MiniMed after the March 2026 IPO. Be clear which segment the role sits in, because Cardiovascular is where the growth and the investment are and Diabetes is leaving. Know that FY2026 was the fastest growth in ten years and that the fiscal year ends in late April, so their "this year" is not your calendar year. If the role is surgical or robotic, name the London Centre of Digital Excellence. If it is NHS-facing, expect the April 2026 IT incident to come up from a trust IT or procurement contact, and be able to say what Medtronic itself has stated about product safety and hospital networks.

alerts.text: IMPORTANT CLINICAL SAFETY FLAG: the Diabetes Technology Network (DTN) committee of the Association of British Clinical Diabetologists (ABCD) issued a formal statement that Medtrum could not provide published safety/efficacy evidence when requested; a small number of NHS England pilot users experienced adverse events including increased hypoglycaemia risk. DTN recommends Medtrum's HCL system should NOT be provided to people with type 1 diabetes in the UK as a hybrid closed loop until published safety/efficacy evidence is provided. BSPED and ACDC separately do not recommend Medtrum HCL use in children. Source: abcd.care/announcement/dtn-statement-regarding-use-medtrum-hcl-systems (publication date on the ABCD page itself unconfirmed). Medtrum's HCL system appeared on an NHS Supply Chain HCL procurement framework per a 2024 Find a Tender notice, but is NOT named in NICE TA943's own guidance text (unlike Medtronic/Tandem/mylife YpsoPump) — a rep must be aware of the DTN caution before positioning this product with an NHS team.

Earlier generations (A6, A7+ TouchCare) are superseded by the current A8 Nano — not a routine product-cycle change: Insulet won European patent-infringement rulings against Medtrum (Higher Regional Court Düsseldorf; Judicial Court of Paris, which separately ordered a French-market recall over patent EP 2 438 957). Direct UK-market impact of these rulings is unconfirmed.

deepDive.tagline: Owned by Investor AB (via Patricia Industries) since 2007 · UK legal entity Molnlycke Health Care Limited, commercial office Milton Keynes, wound care manufacturing at Oldham
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Mölnlycke's global CEO, Zlatko Rihter, told the board he was resigning on 24 March 2026, and the group is currently being run by an interim CEO (CFO Guillaume Joucla) while the board recruits a permanent replacement. That leadership gap sits alongside a genuinely strong trading year, group sales passed €2bn for the first time in 2024 and grew again in 2025, and a fresh €40m investment in UK wound care manufacturing at Oldham announced in June 2026. A company doing well commercially while looking for its next CEO is exactly the kind of tension worth asking a good question about.

prose: Mölnlycke doesn't file a UK-only turnover figure that can be read: Molnlycke Health Care Limited's UK accounts are filed as a PDF at Companies House with no tagged P&L, so the group's own reported numbers are what's usable here. Group net sales passed €2bn for the first time in 2024, at €2,064m (up 7.4%, with 8% organic growth in constant currency and Wound Care, the largest business area, growing 10% and passing €1.2bn on its own). 2025 continued that trajectory: €2,104m in net sales, a further 4% increase, alongside an EBITDA of €596m (28% margin). Both figures are as directly reported by the company, not derived.

The investment pattern backs the growth story up: alongside the €40m Oldham/Mikkeli wound care manufacturing investment (June 2026), Mölnlycke has also opened its first China manufacturing facility (completed July 2026) and formed a majority-owned wound care joint venture with Zhende Medical in China (announced May 2025), both aimed at expanding capacity in fast-growing markets rather than just the UK/Europe base.

ownership: Mölnlycke Health Care Group has changed hands twice since its creation. Nordic Capital merged SCA's Clinical products division with Kolmi-Set in 1997 to form the original Mölnlycke Health Care AB; Apax Partners bought it from Nordic Capital in 2005 and merged in Medlock Medical and Regent Medical to create the current group. Apax sold to Investor AB and Morgan Stanley Principal Investments jointly in January 2007, and Investor AB bought out Morgan Stanley's stake in August 2010, taking Investor AB to a 96% holding, with the remaining 4% held by management.

Mölnlycke is now held via Patricia Industries, Investor AB's wholly owned operating investment arm, and is described by Investor AB as the largest wholly owned subsidiary within that portfolio. Investor AB itself is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. The UK operating entity is Molnlycke Health Care Limited (company number 03493645, incorporated 12 January 1998), confirmed active at Companies House.

hiring: Live UK vacancies tracked via Glassdoor in this session skew commercial and are concentrated at the Milton Keynes office: Inside Sales Manager (c.£50k), Key Account Manager Central West and Central East (c.£60k each), and Marketing Product Manager: Incision Care (c.£65k), plus a Manufacturing Application Specialist role (c.£60k) based at Oldham. Salaries shown are employer-provided figures on the job listing, not independently verified. This is a company actively hiring into UK field sales at the point of this check, not a quiet period.
marketPosition: Mölnlycke describes itself as a 'global leader in MedTech' and 'world-leading' in wound care and surgical solutions; these are the company's own words, not an independently audited market-share figure, and no verified market-share percentage was found in this session, so none is stated. The clearest UK-specific evidence of scale is its own NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 13 separate live frameworks spanning wound care, surgical gloves, orthopaedics, ophthalmology, electrosurgical consumables, procedure packs, patient temperature management, patient handling and skin cleansing, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs on 12/08/2026, which is a genuinely broad spread across NHS procurement categories.

Wound care manufacturing sits separately at Oldham, Greater Manchester (site of the June 2026 €40m-equivalent investment); the group's global HQ is at GoCo Innovation City, Mölndal, Sweden.

glassdoor.summary: 73% would recommend the company to a friend company-wide, rising to 99% at Oldham specifically, though the Oldham sample is small (15 reviews). Company-wide pros cluster around people, culture and work-life balance; cons cluster around inconsistent management quality and change fatigue. Approval of the outgoing CEO (Zlatko Rihter, named on Glassdoor at the time of this check) sits at 82% company-wide.

deepDive.interview: This is a PE-and-family-investor-owned (Investor AB) global MedTech business currently without a permanent CEO, so it's fair game to ask how the leadership search is going and what continuity looks like at UK level. Know whether the role sits in the Milton Keynes commercial team or touches the Oldham manufacturing site, they're different operations. The NHS glove-change study and the Steriwave win in Scotland are both recent, specific, UK-facing talking points if the role touches infection prevention or theatre.

background.text: Corporate restructuring: Nikkiso's CRRT business (Aquarius, Aqualine/Aquaset/Citraset) has united with NorrDia -- the old 'Nikkiso UK Co Ltd' legal entity was renamed 'NorrDia UK Co Ltd' on Companies House 22/09/2025. background.heading: Divestment and spin-off
background.text: IMPORTANT: the Nikkiso business genuinely split in 2025. Chronic haemodialysis (DBB-series, above) remains with Nikkiso — current UK entity Nikkiso Medical UK Limited (15806878), PSC Nikkiso Co., Ltd (Tokyo). CRRT (continuous renal replacement therapy — acute/ICU dialysis, e.g. Accusol fluids, AquaStream/AquaMax/Aqualine filter sets) was sold to Swedish renal-care group NorrDia in Feb 2025 (alongside Bellco); the long-established UK trading entity (08785171) was renamed from Nikkiso UK Co., Ltd to Norrdia UK Co., Ltd on 22/09/2025. If the Hub content covers CRRT products, they should now be attributed to NorrDia/Norrdia UK, not Nikkiso — treating this as one undivided dialysis range is out of date as of Sept 2025.

alerts.text: Cleaned up duplicate product-list entries (EVIS X1 and Thunderbeat each appeared twice). IMPORTANT — the duodenoscope reprocessing/infection-control issue affecting this product family is LIVE and current, not historic: in October 2025 Olympus issued a worldwide Urgent Field Safety Notice on its current-generation duodenoscopes (TJF-Q190V, Q290V, Q170V), citing two deaths and five serious injuries linked to infections/positive cultures since 2024, and introducing a new mandatory requirement to visually inspect the scope tip under 10x magnification (naked-eye inspection deemed unreliable). The US FDA separately ran a Class II recall (June 2025, TJF duodenoscope contamination risk), a Class II recall (March 2026, OER-Pro reprocessor valve cleaning-incompatibility fault), and a Class 2 recall of the Single Use Distal Cover MAJ-2315 (unexpected detachment). A September 2025 field correction also covered laser-compatible bronchoscopes over endobronchial combustion risk. A UK-specific MHRA Field Safety Notice or GOV.UK Drug Device Alert naming Olympus in 2025-2026 could not be independently confirmed in this pass — Olympus's notices are issued worldwide so UK trusts almost certainly received them via MHRA/Olympus channels, but this should be verified directly (e.g. with an NHS decontamination lead) before stating a UK-specific status as settled fact. UK entity confirmed: Olympus KeyMed Group Limited (Companies House 01210694, Southend-on-Sea), PSC Olympus Europa Holding SE.

deepDive.origin: supplier-deep-capture scheduled run, 18/08/2026. Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (company overview, officers, persons with significant control, filing history) and OscarTech UK's own website (about us, home, frameworks, contact, insights pages), all read in this session.
deepDive.tagline: NHS Supply Chain approved supplier of surgical instruments, wound care, defibrillators and cardiovascular devices to NHS Trusts and private healthcare.
deepDive.lede: OscarTech UK Ltd, company number 09196814, was incorporated on 30 August 2014 under the name Oscar Corporation Ltd, and only became OscarTech UK on 31 December 2018, a rename filed at Companies House days after sole director and PSC Adnan Shabbir took full control of the company on 27 November 2018 from the previous director, Shazia Rafiq. Worth knowing before a meeting: the current site claims fifteen-plus years in operation, but the Companies House incorporation date puts the entity at just under twelve years old as of August 2026, so that figure is worth asking about rather than repeating as fact.
