prose: No turnover figure is available for OscarTech UK Ltd. The company's Companies House filing history, read directly in this session, shows only micro-entity and unaudited abridged accounts, most recently micro company accounts made up to 28 February 2025, filed 30 November 2025, and micro-entity and abridged filings are exempt from disclosing turnover or a full profit and loss account. There is no machine-readable turnover or employee-count figure on the public record, and the company's own website does not publish a turnover figure either, so none is given here rather than estimated from the PDF accounts.

ownership: OscarTech UK Ltd is a UK private limited company, registered office 27 Old Gloucester Street, London, WC1N 3AX, a Monomark House registered-office and company-formation address rather than an operational site, per the Companies House overview read this session. It is not part of a wider group structure on the public record: Companies House shows a single active person with significant control, Adnan Shabbir, holding 75% or more of shares and voting rights since 27 November 2018, with no parent company or corporate PSC listed. No holding company, private equity ownership, or listing status was found; on the evidence read this session it appears to be a wholly individually owned private company.

people.name: Adnan Shabbir
people.role: Director and sole person with significant control
people.note: Companies House officers and PSC pages, read 18/08/2026: appointed director 27 November 2018, PSC notified same date, British, resident in England. Previously an officer and PSC of the company under its earlier name, Oscar Corporation Ltd, from 30 August 2014, per filing history.

deepDive.peopleNote: Companies House shows only one current officer, Adnan Shabbir, director, and no company secretary currently in post; four prior appointments, a resigned secretary and two spells for a second director, Shazia Rafiq, who left the board and PSC register on 22 December 2020, are all historic. No other current directors, no finance or commercial contact, and no named managing director or CEO title could be verified from Companies House or the company website in this session; job titles beyond director are not disclosed on the public record.

press.text: Company changed its registered name from Oscar Corporation Ltd to OscarTech UK Ltd, filed at Companies House.

No 2025 or 2026 press releases, news coverage or formal announcements from OscarTech UK could be found via web search or on the company's own site in this session; the Insights blog contains only three general procurement and compliance guidance articles, UKCA vs CE marking, an NHS Supply Chain framework buyer's guide, and choosing a defibrillator, none of which is a company announcement.

hiring: No careers or vacancies page was found on oscartech-uk.com in this session, and no current job listings for OscarTech UK Ltd, the medical supplier, turned up in search; results under similar names returned an unrelated IT recruitment firm trading as Oscar Technology. Hiring activity could not be verified and should be treated as unknown rather than assumed absent.
marketPosition: OscarTech UK positions itself as an NHS Supply Chain approved partner supplying surgical instruments, sterile single-use and reusable, including ophthalmology and specialist retractor sets, general and advanced wound care, emergency equipment including AEDs, PPE, pharmacy consumables, electrosurgical units, and cardiovascular devices spanning cardiology, radiology and neuro-interventional lines, per its own site read this session. Its Frameworks page states it holds NHS Supply Chain framework listings across surgical instruments, wound care and emergency equipment categories specifically, and offers to confirm framework or lot status on request, rather than listing lot numbers publicly.

This supplier is already captured in this Hub's frameworks array; framework-by-framework verification against supplychain.nhs.uk was out of scope for this deepDive and was not independently repeated here beyond noting what the company's own frameworks page claims.
deepDive.interview: Ask directly about the 2018 name change and change of control: the company traded for over four years as Oscar Corporation Ltd before becoming OscarTech UK, and sole control passed to Adnan Shabbir at the same moment, which is worth understanding as company history rather than treating OscarTech as a business built from scratch in 2018. Also worth a polite challenge on the fifteen-plus years in operation claim on the website against a 30 August 2014 incorporation date, under twelve years as of August 2026, and worth asking which specific NHS Supply Chain framework lots and reference numbers currently cover their product range, since the company's own site does not publish lot numbers and only offers to confirm them on request.
deepDive.sources: Company identity: confirmed. The Companies House entry for OSCARTECH UK LTD, company number 09196814, registered office 27 Old Gloucester Street, London, WC1N 3AX, matches exactly the registered office address and company number printed in the footer of the company's own website, oscartech-uk.com, read in this session; this is treated as a positive cross-check confirming the same entity. Sources read directly in this session: Companies House officers page, persons with significant control page, filing history page, and the more information page, which did not surface additional detail; OscarTech UK's own website homepage, about-us, contact-us, tenders and frameworks, and insights and blog listing pages. The Companies House company overview page itself returned no readable content across three attempts in this session and so status, SIC codes and active flag as shown on that specific page were not independently confirmed from it; company-active status is instead inferred from the filing history read directly, which shows a confirmation statement filed 27 October 2025 and accounts filed 30 November 2025, both current. SIC classification codes seen in aggregator search snippets were not used as a source because that page also failed to load when fetched directly in this session and is not one of the four permitted source types; SIC codes are therefore omitted rather than guessed. Turnover and employee counts: not verified and deliberately omitted, per the filing history showing only micro-entity and abridged accounts, which are exempt from disclosing those figures. A LinkedIn company page was found via search but returned no content when fetched in this session, so it is not cited or linked here. No 2025 or 2026 press releases or news coverage were found. NHS Supply Chain framework specifics were not independently re-verified against supplychain.nhs.uk in this session, per instruction that this supplier's frameworks are already captured elsewhere in the Hub; only the company's own general framework-category claims are cited above.

background.heading: Company description
background.text: PKB does NOT sell condition-specific products under separate names -- it is one Single Patient Record platform with configured deployments per clinical use-case. First PHR fully integrated into the NHS App (launched 14/07/2020); all hospital test results in the NHS App arrive via PKB, 20m+ results/month, live on the NHS Wales App since 2025. June 2025: nationwide GP data integration launched. Over one-third of England's Mental Health Trusts use PKB. £6m funding Jan 2025; strategic investment from DNV (Norwegian assurance/risk group) Sept 2025, amount undisclosed. alerts.text: Historical context worth knowing: Pentax was one of three manufacturers (with Olympus and Fujifilm) named in the 2015-2019 US CRE/'superbug' duodenoscope scandal — the US DOJ reached a $43m settlement over historic failures to report infections and maintain FDA-cleared cleaning instructions. This is public record, not new. The DEC (Disposable Elevator Cap) duodenoscope, launched 2019, was Pentax's direct design response and remains their current standard (precise model: ED34-i10T2, also marketed as 'i-DEC'). A newer Slim DEC Duodenoscope (ED32-i10) for narrower anatomy was described in Pentax's own materials as forthcoming — its UK launch-live status is unconfirmed. No current (2024-2026) UK MHRA field safety notice was found naming Pentax duodenoscopes in the periods checked, though this was not an exhaustive search.

voice.line: Established third scope vendor — competitive challenger to Olympus/Fujifilm on GI and ENT fleets.

suppliers._specialitiesEvidence: Gastroenterology: Confirmed dedicated GI range: named gastroscopes (HD+ EG34-i10, MagniView EG-2990Zi), colonoscopes (RetroView, SCOPEPILOT 3D), duodenoscopes (Slim DEC ED34-i10T2/T).20/07/2026: added ENT (VNL/FNL scopes, confirmed live NHS Supply Chain accessory naming these exact models) and Continence & urology (cystoscopes/ureteroscopes, ECY-1575K confirmed live NHS Supply Chain accessory). CORRECTED: Pentax's duodenoscope differentiator (DEC, ED34-i10T2/Slim DEC ED32-i10) is a REUSABLE scope body with a single-use disposable elevator cap only -- SAGES' own technology assessment labels it explicitly 'Partially Disposable', NOT a fully single-use duodenoscope as an earlier brief assumed (competitors Boston Scientific EXALT Model D and Ambu aScope Duodeno ARE fully single-use -- important distinction for a rep not to misstate). Pentax's genuinely fully single-use product is the ONE Pulmo bronchoscope system (pulmonology), confirmed live on NHS Supply Chain (EB11-S01, box of 5). Confirmed HOYA Corporation ownership, with a live corporate change to note: HOYA is spinning the endoscope business out into a new wholly-owned subsidiary 'PENTAX Medical Corporation', effective 01/05/2026 -- ownership stays 100% within HOYA Group, doesn't change who owns Pentax Medical for sales purposes.

background.heading: Regulatory and NICE scope
background.text: NICE HTG709 (formerly IPG781, Jan 2024) is CONDITIONAL, not a blanket approval: post-stroke patients WITH a tracheostomy may use it under special arrangements (governance notification, consent covering uncertainty, mandatory outcome audit); all other populations (non-tracheostomy, non-stroke) are restricted to formal research studies only. Do not present as a general NICE approval. Ownership history: Nestlé Health Science-backed 2016-2025 (PSC filings show Nestlé S.A. control until ceased 29/08/2025); now independent, backed by EQT Life Sciences/Sectoral Asset Management following a $42m Series D (March 2024). NHS deployment scale unverified beyond the company's own claim of 3,000+ commercial treatments.
background.source: NICE HTG709 / Companies House 06308699 PSC filings / PRNewswire Series D announcement

alerts.text: Confirmed genuinely single-product (EASEE only). CE-marked since 2023, genuinely available on the NHS in the UK since 28/04/2025 (first implant at Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle Hospitals NHS FT; also UCLH) -- but only at SELECT centres, not nationally commissioned; no NICE technology appraisal or formal NHS England national commissioning policy found. No UK Companies House entity exists -- Precisis GmbH (Heidelberg, Germany) sells/supports the UK market directly via its own field sales function, not a UK subsidiary or distributor. US status remains investigational (FDA Breakthrough Device Designation 2022, pivotal IDE trial authorised Nov 2025) -- do not conflate with the CE-marked/NHS-available European status.

voice.line: Nucleic-acid extraction automation plus QuantiFERON (NHS TB screening standard) and QIAstat-Dx.

suppliers._specialitiesEvidence: 20/07/2026: removed NeuMoDx -- QIAGEN confirmed discontinuation of NeuMoDx and Dialunox, cited as a ~$20m revenue headwind in 2025 and ~$10m expected in 2026, being wound down. Added therascreen (EGFR/KRAS) companion-diagnostic PCR kits under a new Oncology and infusion tag -- these are genuinely high-stakes: a positive/negative therascreen result gates NHS prescribing eligibility for specific licensed targeted cancer drugs (EGFR-TKIs, KRAS G12C inhibitors, anti-EGFR antibodies in colorectal cancer), sitting at the pathology-oncology interface rather than routine diagnostics. NOTE: exhaustively tested the NHS Supply Chain catalogue for every QIAGEN family (Qiagen, QuantiFERON, therascreen, QIAstat, QIAamp, EZ1, digene) -- zero results for all of them, though the search tool itself was confirmed working (nitrile gloves returned 453 results, 'PCR kit' surfaced Roche/Illumina reagents). This means QIAGEN's entire range should be treated as company-site-confirmed only, NOT NHS-Supply-Chain-catalogue-confirmed -- doesn't mean these aren't used in the NHS (QuantiFERON is a well-known NHS TB-screening standard in practice), just that procurement likely runs through a separate pathology/trust-direct route not indexed in this catalogue.

deepDive.origin: supplier-deep-capture scheduled run, 18/08/2026. Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (company overview, officers and persons with significant control filings for RELIANCE MEDICAL LTD, company number 05701697, and RELIANCE MEDICAL HOLDINGS LTD, company number 11911024) and Reliance Medical's own website (about, brands and latest news pages), all read in this session.
deepDive.tagline: Staffordshire-based, family-owned manufacturer and trade-only supplier of first aid and medical equipment, with its own vertically integrated factory in Shanghai and long-standing NHS and Ambulance Service supply relationships.
deepDive.lede: This is a genuinely vertically integrated supplier, not just a trade distributor: Reliance Medical Ltd owns and runs its own 77,000 sq ft, TUV Rheinland certified medical device factory in Shanghai, which the company says made over 80 million plasters for the UK market in a recent year alone. Reliance Medical Shanghai is a wholly owned subsidiary manufacturing exclusively for the UK parent, which is unusual for a company this size and worth knowing before any conversation about supply resilience or own label capability. The UK company remains a private, family controlled business: it was formed in 2006 by four directors and is majority owned via a holding company, Reliance Medical Holdings Ltd, controlled by the Pear family.

prose: The turnover figure of £20,989,946 for the year to 31 December 2024 comes from this Hub's own Companies House pipeline and has not been independently re-verified against the full accounts in this session; it should be read as company level UK turnover for Reliance Medical Ltd, not group turnover including the Shanghai manufacturing subsidiary.

The filed employee figure of 1 sits oddly against a company that describes itself as running warehousing, a UK sales team and a fifty plus person Shanghai factory, and against Companies House confirming seven current officers. This is very likely an artefact of how the figure was tagged in the accounts, for example a headcount convention counting only a specific class of employee, or a data extraction quirk in the source pipeline, rather than a true reflection of staff numbers. This has not been independently resolved in this session: treat the workforce size as not verified and do not repeat 1 employee as a real headcount without checking the full statutory accounts.

ownership: Reliance Medical Ltd, company number 05701697, is a private limited company incorporated on 8 February 2006, registered office West Avenue, Talke, Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire, ST7 1TL. Company status is Active. SIC codes are 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods, and 46900, non-specialised wholesale trade, per Companies House, read 18/08/2026.

Its sole person with significant control is Reliance Medical Holdings Ltd, company number 11911024, notified 18 July 2019, holding 75% or more of shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. Reliance Medical Holdings Ltd is itself a private limited company, incorporated 28 March 2019, same registered office, SIC code 64209, activities of other holding companies. Before the holding company structure was put in place, Mr Andrew Mark Pear held the equivalent 75%-plus control personally from 6 April 2016 until it ceased on 18 July 2019, per Companies House PSC filings read 18/08/2026.

This confirms the company is privately, family controlled (the holding company's registered PSC address and the surname Pear recurring among current directors point to continued family ownership) rather than private equity backed or listed. No further ownership layer above Reliance Medical Holdings Ltd was checked in this session.

deepDive.peopleNote: Companies House lists officer appointments and roles but not job titles such as Managing Director or Sales Director, so nothing here should be read as confirming who runs day to day commercial or NHS-facing activity; that would need the company's own leadership page or LinkedIn profiles, neither of which was available to check in this session. Two directors share the Pear surname, Andrew Mark Pear and Thomas Andrew James Pear, consistent with continued family involvement, but the family relationship itself is not independently verified here.

press.text: The company's own Careers page states there are no vacancies available at the moment, checked this date; no dated 2025 to 2026 press releases, leadership changes or acquisition announcements naming Reliance Medical Ltd were found in this session.

hiring: The company's own Careers page states plainly there are no vacancies available at the moment, checked 18/08/2026. This cannot be taken as a permanent state, only as the position on the day it was read; a rep should check the live careers page again close to any meeting rather than rely on this note.
marketPosition: Reliance Medical describes itself as the UK's leading manufacturer and trade-only supplier of first aid and medical equipment to the industrial sector, supported by what it calls the UK's largest distributor network for first aid, and as a trusted supplier to the NHS and Ambulance services for nearly fifteen years, per its own About Us page, read 18/08/2026. These are the company's own claims and have not been independently benchmarked against competitors in this session; treat UK's leading and largest distributor network as marketing positioning, not verified market share facts.

The company states it is trade-only, it sells through distributors, not direct to end consumers, and does own-brand and private-label manufacturing for other UK brands and major retailers, which is a distinct commercial model from suppliers who sell direct.

This supplier's NHS Supply Chain framework presence is already captured elsewhere in this Hub's frameworks array for Reliance Medical; no independent NHS Supply Chain contract launch brief naming this exact company was found or read in this session, so nothing further is added here beyond that existing record.
deepDive.interview: Before any meeting, ask about the split between the UK trade-distribution business and the wholly owned Shanghai manufacturing operation, since that vertical integration, own factory, own quality control, TUV Rheinland certification, is the company's stated point of difference from agents and distributors who rely on third parties, and is worth probing on lead times and control of specification changes. Given the filed employee count of 1 looks inconsistent with the scale the company describes, do not quote workforce size from the accounts without first asking the company directly or checking the full statutory accounts, and be ready to ask plainly who currently leads commercial and NHS-facing sales, since Companies House does not give job titles and the public site does not name a leadership team.
deepDive.sources: Sources read in this session, all 18/08/2026 unless stated: Companies House company overview for RELIANCE MEDICAL LTD, 05701697; Companies House officers list for the same company; Companies House persons with significant control for the same company; Companies House company overview for RELIANCE MEDICAL HOLDINGS LTD, 11911024; Reliance Medical's own About Us page; Our Brands page; Latest News page; Careers page. The turnover, £20,989,946, and employee, 1, figures were supplied as already read from this Hub's Companies House pipeline for the accounts made up to 31 December 2024 and were not independently re-pulled from the raw accounts filing in this session. Could not verify: any 2025 to 2026 dated UK press release, leadership change, acquisition or product launch announcement specifically naming Reliance Medical Ltd, a web search for 2025 to 2026 press coverage returned no relevant results, only unrelated Reliance companies; the true current headcount, given the filed figure of 1 looks inconsistent with the company's own description of its operations; named job titles for any officer, Companies House gives appointment roles only, director or secretary, not functional titles; any NHS Supply Chain contract launch brief specifically naming this company, not searched independently, per instruction to rely on the existing frameworks array for this supplier; ultimate ownership above Reliance Medical Holdings Ltd, that is whether the Pear family surname connection between directors is a formally confirmed family relationship. These gaps are left as Not verified rather than filled.

deepDive.origin: supplier-deep-capture scheduled run, 21/08/2026. Editorial deepDive built from Companies House (company overview, officers, persons with significant control and filing history for ROCIALLE HEALTHCARE LIMITED, 11965323, and the overview and PSC pages for MULTIGATE MEDICAL PRODUCTS UK LIMITED, 11937332), from four sets of the company's own filed accounts read at source as tagged iXBRL documents (years ended 31 December 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024), and from Rocialle Healthcare's own corporate website and its four divisional websites, all read in this session.
deepDive.tagline: Mountain Ash manufacturer of custom procedure packs, single-use surgical instruments and drapes and gowns, 55% owned by Shanghai-listed Zhende Medical through a Hong Kong holding company and 45% by Australia's Multigate Medical Products.
deepDive.lede: Check which year's turnover figure you are carrying into the room, because Rocialle's looks like three different companies. Its filed accounts put turnover at 371.4m in the year to December 2020 and 72.3m in 2021, then 30.3m in 2022 once, in the directors' own words, the business had no PPE activities at all. It has climbed back to 53.9m in the year to December 2024, and that climb is acquisitions rather than recovery: MidMeds in late 2022, Dene Healthcare at the start of 2023 and the trade and assets of Ward Mobility on 3 January 2024. Worth knowing before a meeting: profit has not followed sales back up, with profit before tax down to 2.0m from 3.0m, and the products a rep would actually be quoting against are not on the corporate website at all, they are spread across four separate divisional sites.

Read from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its group statement of comprehensive income, page 12, and repeated in note 3, in the audited group accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 filed at Companies House on 14 July 2025 (11965323). The figure is printed but not iXBRL-tagged in that document, which is why company-financials.json in this Hub still shows no turnover for the company.

stats.n: £2,025,037, against £3,049,523 in 2023. Same filing, group statement of comprehensive income, page 12. Profit for the financial year after tax was £362,692 (2023: £1,656,556).
The directors' own key performance indicator, stated in their strategic report in the same filing: £5.5 million against £5.9 million in 2023. It is the company's own measure, not one calculated here.

Note 6 of the same filing: group 307 (2023: 341), parent company 257 (2023: 286). Rocialle's own About Us page separately says the group employs over 450 staff, undated copy read 21/08/2026. The two are on different bases and both are the company's own figures; the accounts number is an average across the year, and neither is reconciled here.

Named supplier on ten NHS Supply Chain contract launch briefs: Advanced Wound Care, Extension Sets and Lines, General Wound Care, Intravenous Cannula and Associated Products, Maternity Obstetrics Gynaecology and Sexual Health Products, Procedure Packs, Surgical Instruments, Syringes Needles and Associated Products, Urology and Bowel Management, and Vascular Therapy and Associated Products. Ranking rule, so you can judge it: count the briefs that name the company, one per framework, across the 1,203 suppliers in this Hub's seed. On that count, 1,081 suppliers are named on at least one brief, 21 are named on more than ten, and Rocialle is joint twenty-second with GenX MediCare and Hospital Services Limited. It is a count of frameworks, not of revenue, lots or market share, and nothing here is inferred from product ranges.

Companies House company 11965323, read 21/08/2026. Status Active. The trading business is much older than the entity: the company's own About Us page says over 45 years and that it relocated to South Wales in 1995.

Note 27 of the audited accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024: New Beginnings Investment (Hong Kong) Co Ltd owns 55% of the issued share capital and Multigate Medical Products UK Ltd owns 45%. Zhende Medical Co. Ltd is the 100% owner of the Hong Kong company.

prose: The shape of that chart is PPE, and the company says so itself. Its accounts for the year ended 31 December 2022 state that in contrast with 2021, where PPE was the dominant activity in relation to both turnover and profitability, the business had no PPE activities in 2022, and that this is the reason for the decreased turnover and profitability. The 2021 strategic report had already warned that 2022 would significantly reduce as the business reverted to its core business and PPE demand fell away completely. So £371.4m in 2020 and £72.3m in 2021 are not a baseline for anything, and a figure lifted from either year will be wrong by an order of magnitude.

The recovery from £30.3m in 2022 to £53.9m in 2024 is bought rather than grown. The strategic report names the two purchases that did it, MidMeds Limited in late 2022 and Dene Healthcare Ltd at the beginning of 2023, the latter described as giving a strong presence in the primary care sector. Both are now 100% owned subsidiaries registered at the same Mountain Ash address. A third deal, the trade and trading assets of Ward Mobility, completed on 3 January 2024 for £2,448,204 in cash, of which £1,745,750 was attributed to an NHS licence, and contributed £1,209,485 of turnover and £192,839 of profit after tax in its first part-year.

Margin is where the pressure shows. Gross profit fell to £15,520,868 in 2024 from £16,090,775 in 2023 on higher sales, so gross margin went from 31.1% to 28.8%, and profit before tax fell from £3,049,523 to £2,025,037. The directors' own list of causes, in the strategic report, is high energy cost, increased component cost, an employee cost uplift and disruption from continuous NHS strikes, and they say they expect those pressures to continue through 2025 and the 2025 result to be stable. No ordinary dividends were paid in the year.

ownership: ROCIALLE HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company number 11965323, registered office Ty Mynydd, Cwm Cynon Business Park, Mountain Ash, Wales, CF45 4ER, is a private limited company incorporated on 26 April 2019 and currently Active. Note 27 of its audited accounts for the year ended 31 December 2024 sets out the shareholding directly: New Beginnings Investment (Hong Kong) Co Ltd owns 55% of the issued share capital and Multigate Medical Products UK Ltd owns 45%, and Zhende Medical Co. Ltd is the 100% owner of the Hong Kong company. Note 28 names New Beginning Investment (Hong Kong) Co. Ltd as the immediate parent undertaking and Zhende Medical Co. Ltd, of Gaobei Industrial Zone, Gaobu Town, Shaoxing, 312035, China, as the ultimate parent that draws up the consolidated financial statements.

The Companies House PSC register for 11965323 does not carry the 55% holder. It records one active person with significant control, Multigate Medical Products Uk Limited, company number 11937332, notified on 22 August 2019, at ownership of shares and of voting rights of more than 25% but not more than 50%, which is consistent with the 45% in the accounts. The only other entry is a ceased one: Berendsen Healthcare Limited, company number 10174957, of Basingstoke, notified 26 April 2019 and ceased 22 August 2019, which had held 75% or more of shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. That ceased date is the change of control, and it matches the company's own account of it: its About Us page says that in August 2019 Rocialle Healthcare Ltd, comprising Rocialle and Guardian, was purchased by a wholly owned subsidiary of Zhende Medical Co. Ltd and Multigate Medical Products Ltd.

Multigate itself is family-held. Companies House shows one active person with significant control for MULTIGATE MEDICAL PRODUCTS UK LIMITED, 11937332: Mr Bounchong Chaisumdet, Australian, born June 1955, notified 10 April 2019, holding more than 50% but less than 75% of shares and voting rights. Rocialle's own register records a Boun Chong Chaisumdet as a director from 22 August 2019 to 5 July 2022, and a Julius Chaisumdet, Australian, born June 1991, appointed a director on 5 July 2022 and still in post. Those are two dated register events and nothing here asserts a succession between them, because succession is not a register fact.

The group buys from its owners, and at a scale worth knowing. Note 27 records purchases from Zhende Medical Co. Ltd of £3,728,756 in 2024 (2023: £4,849,004), with £404,405 still payable at the year end, and purchases from Shaoxing Fuqing Health Products Co Ltd, described as a joint venture of Multigate Medical Products UK Ltd, of £1,664,125 (2023: £1,026,226). Both shareholders have also lent to the company: £6,050,000 was advanced by Zhende Medical and £4,950,000 by Multigate Medical Products UK in 2022 to fund the future purchase of a trading entity, interest free and repayable within one year, with balances at 31 December 2024 of £4,400,000 and £3,600,000 respectively.

Two 100% owned subsidiaries sit under the company, both registered at the Mountain Ash address: Midmeds Limited, 05440524, principal activity medical supplies to primary care trusts, and Dene Healthcare Limited, 05427785, medical supplies and general surgery consumables. The accounting policies note, under Subsidiary audit exemption on page 19, records that the parent has guaranteed the liabilities of both subsidiaries outstanding at the balance sheet date, so they are exempt from audit under s479A Companies Act 2006.

The dated changes on the register since 2022 are: Boun Chong Chaisumdet resigned and Julius Chaisumdet was appointed, both 5 July 2022; Zhendong Shen resigned and Yanjun Yang was appointed, both 27 April 2022; Simon David Loose resigned and Andrew John Stonehouse was appointed, both 21 May 2025; Yanjun Yang resigned and Wolfgang Suessle was appointed, both 1 January 2026. press.text: Rocialle Healthcare announced it had acquired MidMeds, which would join its primary care division.
Rocialle Healthcare announced the acquisition of Dene Healthcare, which would sit alongside MidMeds Limited in the group.

Rocialle Healthcare announced the launch of Rocialle Direct, a new trading division joining Rocialle AcuteCare and the rest of the group. The division's own website separately describes itself as established in 2022.
Rocialle Healthcare announced that Dene Healthcare had won Medical Supplier of the Year at the General Practice Awards 2023.
The company announced it was on track to generate an estimated 386,000 kWh of solar electricity output that year, having activated solar panels in April 2023.

Rocialle Healthcare announced that the trade and assets of Ward Mobility Limited had been acquired and would operate as a prescription home delivery service. The audited accounts date the acquisition to 3 January 2024 and put the consideration at £2,448,204 in cash.

The most recent item on the company's own news page at the date of this check is a Mental Health Awareness Week team post. Nothing later than 15 May 2025 was published there, so the corporate news feed has been quiet for about fifteen months.

hiring: One vacancy was listed on the company's own Current Opportunities page when it was read on 21/08/2026: a Hygiene Operator, 35.75 hours a week, in the Hygiene department, with a closing date of 07/08/2026 that had already passed. The advert places the role at postcode CF44 6DA, in Aberaman near Aberdare, which is not the CF45 4ER registered office and head office at Mountain Ash, and describes it as a regulated medical device manufacturing environment working to Good Manufacturing and Distribution Practice. One stale advert is not a hiring signal in either direction, and no conclusion is drawn here from a single listing.

On its own careers and About Us pages the company says it employs over 450 staff across the group, that 51% of its people have been in the business ten years or more, and that it runs a graduate programme. Those are undated claims in the company's own copy, read 21/08/2026, and they sit above the 307 average monthly group headcount in the 2024 accounts.
marketPosition: The company's own claim, in its directors' report and repeated on its About Us page, is that with over 35 years' experience in acute care the group serves almost every NHS trust in the UK as well as many private hospital groups, and has gained a market leading position in the supply of Procedure Packs, Medical Packs, Single Use Instruments, Single Use Drapes and Gowns and other PPE products. That is Rocialle's own wording, published in a filed document and on its own site, and it is reported here as its claim, not as a finding: nothing in this Hub measures market share, and no share figure exists anywhere in this system.

What is independently checkable is the framework footprint. NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name Rocialle on ten frameworks, and the spread of them is the interesting part for a rep: it runs from Procedure Packs and Surgical Instruments, which is the core manufactured business, out into Intravenous Cannula, Extension Sets and Lines, Vascular Therapy, Syringes and Needles, Urology and Bowel Management, Maternity, and both Advanced and General Wound Care. Only two of the ten, Procedure Packs and Surgical Instruments, are the core theatre business; the other eight run through wound care, vascular access, syringes and needles, maternity and urology, which is wider than the Hub's current single speciality tag of Theatres / surgical suggests.

Manufacturing is genuinely in-house and in Wales. The About Us page states the business relocated to South Wales in 1995 and that head office, warehouse operations, clean room production and sterilisation facilities are all at Mountain Ash, and the directors' report records certification to ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 alongside compliance with the EU Medical Device Directive. Set against that, note 27 shows £5.4m of the year's purchases coming from the Chinese shareholder and its joint venture, so the group both manufactures and imports, and which of the two applies to a given line is a fair question to ask.

Four divisions, on four separate websites, and this matters for anyone reading this Hub's product data. Rocialle AcuteCare (rocialleacutecare.com) carries the hospital catalogue: procedure packs, surgical instruments, IV cannulae, administration and extension sets, and wound care. Rocialle PracticeCare (rociallepracticecare.com) is the primary care business and trades under the MidMeds name in its own page title, with GP consumables, diagnostics, gloves and gynaecology. Rocialle Direct (rocialledirect.com) is direct to patient, in stoma, wound and continence prescription products. Rocialle Mobility (rociallemobility.com) is the former Ward Mobility, a mobility store serving Canvey Island and South Essex and, on its own description, a Dispensing Appliance Contractor serving the United Kingdom more broadly. All four were read on 21/08/2026.

That last point is a data caveat, not just background. The corporate site recorded for this supplier carries no product catalogue at all, and this Hub currently holds no own-site product range for Rocialle. That is a reading gap, not an absence of products: the catalogue is on the four divisional hosts named above. Do not read a thin product list for this company as a thin company.

deepDive.interview: Ask which division you are actually being sold by, because the answer changes the conversation: AcuteCare is the manufactured hospital range, PracticeCare is the MidMeds primary care business, Direct is prescription supply to patients and Mobility is the former Ward Mobility. On the numbers, the useful question is margin rather than growth: sales are up to £53.9m but gross margin fell from 31.1% to 28.8% and profit before tax from £3.0m to £2.0m, and the directors blame energy, components, wage costs and NHS strikes, so a discussion about price is a discussion they are already having internally. On supply, note 27 of the accounts shows £5.4m of purchases from the Chinese shareholder Zhende Medical and from Shaoxing Fuqing Health Products, so it is fair to ask which lines are made at Mountain Ash and which are imported from the parent, particularly on anything you would compete with on lead time or on UK content. And be aware that five of the seven registered directors are resident in Australia or China: whoever you meet will not be on the Companies House list, so establish early who actually owns the NHS account relationship and who signs off pricing.

alerts.text: Field safety notice on the Universal Blood Culture Adapter (NPC KCM176) -- a production-related membrane misalignment causing possible leaks/false-negative blood cultures, affecting lot 4074321 ONLY. Not a recall/discontinuation -- future stock confirmed unaffected; action is inspect-and-replace for the affected lot.

suppliers.note: Specimen-collection and laboratory company, NOT a vascular access player — no IV cannula found anywhere in the current published catalogue (verified against the live site 20/07/2026, with the caveat that the site is mid-migration and some legacy pages are unreachable, so 'none found' rather than a flat denial). Four business areas: Preanalytics, Life Science, Laboratory automation, Sample transport. S-Monovette's differentiator is that the same device supports EITHER aspiration (gentler, adjusts to vein condition) OR a fresh user-generated vacuum — not a factory pre-set vacuum that decays.

voice.line: Aspiration technique reduces haemolysis and repeat draws — lead with patient experience and sample quality, not price.

One academic study (J Clin Microbiology 2020, COVID-era) found Sarstedt dry swabs in saline achieved lower SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR detection than a CDC-recipe VTM -- a single study caveat, not a recall, noted for completeness only. Recorded the Universal Blood Culture Adapter field safety notice in alerts[].

deepDive.tagline: Frankfurt-listed (SHL), FY2025 group revenue €23,375m · UK entity Siemens Healthcare Limited, Park View, Watchmoor Park, Camberley · two structural changes running at once: Siemens AG is spinning off its majority stake, and Diagnostics is being moved to its own independent structure

links.label: Siemens AG on the spin-off timetable

deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: the company is being taken apart and rebuilt at the same time, in two separate ways, and which half of it your role sits in changes the story completely. First, Siemens AG is letting go. On 12 November 2025 it announced it would deconsolidate its roughly 67% stake, and on 17 April 2026 it confirmed the mechanism and the date: a direct spin-off under the German Transformation Act, put to a shareholder vote at the Siemens AGM in February 2027, with Siemens AG shareholders receiving Siemens Healthineers shares directly. Second, and more directly relevant to anybody selling into an NHS pathology lab, Bernd Montag told the annual shareholders' meeting on 5 February 2026 that "Imaging and Precision Therapy … form the highly synergetic core of our company. Diagnostics, on the other hand, has few synergies with the other segments. The next step is now for Diagnostics to consistently pursue its own strategy – and derived from that, its own independent structure." That is the CEO, on the record, saying the Diagnostics business is going its own way. The numbers behind it are not flattering: Diagnostics revenue fell 5.5% in Q3 FY2026 on an adjusted EBIT margin of 4.1%, against 26.5% in Imaging, and it was the sole reason the company cut its full-year revenue growth guidance on 31 July 2026. If the role you are interviewing for is Atellica, IMMULITE or point-of-care, you are interviewing for a business being separated from its parent. If it is MAGNETOM, NAEOTOM or Varian, you are interviewing for the part being kept.

prose: There is no readable UK turnover for Siemens Healthineers. Siemens Healthcare Limited (company number 09567186) files full accounts, most recently made up to 30 September 2025, but this pipeline records them as PDF-only with no tagged figures, so nothing is read from them: picking the turnover line off a PDF by position would be a guess, not a reading. The company does publish a UK & Ireland revenue figure of about £1.4bn for FY2024 on its own fact sheet, but that is a management figure covering two countries and several legal entities, and it is not the same thing as a filed statutory turnover. Both numbers are given here for what they are.

Group FY2025 was a good year. Revenue was €23,375m, up 4.5% reported and 5.9% comparable, adjusted EBIT rose to just under €3.9bn on a margin of 16.5%, adjusted basic EPS was €2.39, free cash flow was around €2.7bn and the proposed dividend rose to €1.00 a share. Imaging did the heavy lifting at €13,182m of adjusted revenue, up 8.5% comparable; Varian was €4,081m and Advanced Therapies €2,128m; Diagnostics was €4,347m, essentially flat at +0.4% comparable, on a 7.7% margin.

FY2026 has split in two. From 1 October 2025 Varian and Advanced Therapies report as a single Precision Therapy segment, so prior-year segment figures are restated and old comparisons will not line up. In Q3 FY2026, to 30 June 2026, group revenue was €5,764m, up 2.8% comparable, with an equipment book-to-bill ratio of 1.27, adjusted EBIT margin of 19.1% and adjusted EPS of €0.70. Precision Therapy grew 9.2% and Imaging 2.3%, while Diagnostics fell 5.5%. On 31 July 2026 the company cut FY2026 comparable revenue growth guidance to 3.5% to 4.0%, from 4.5% to 5.0%, citing Diagnostics, and simultaneously raised adjusted EPS guidance to €2.35 to €2.45 on refunds of tariffs imposed under the U.S. IEEPA. Order intake, note, is strong: a book-to-bill of 1.27 is a company selling well into a soft revenue quarter.

ownership: Siemens Healthineers AG is listed in Frankfurt as SHL and headquartered at Siemensstr. 3, 91301 Forchheim, Germany. Siemens AG has held the majority since the 2018 IPO, and is now getting out. Siemens announced on 12 November 2025 that it would deconsolidate its stake of around 67%, and confirmed on 17 April 2026 that it is preparing a direct spin-off under the German Transformation Act, under which Siemens AG shareholders receive Siemens Healthineers AG shares directly, to be voted on at the ordinary Siemens AGM in February 2027. Siemens has said it intends to reduce the holding to a financial stake in the medium term. Final regulatory confirmation was still outstanding at the date of that release.

The second ownership question is internal. At the annual shareholders' meeting on 5 February 2026 CEO Bernd Montag said Imaging and Precision Therapy form the company's "highly synergetic core", that Diagnostics "has few synergies with the other segments", and that the next step is for Diagnostics to pursue its own strategy "and derived from that, its own independent structure". Those are the company's own words. What the eventual structure is, whether a sale, a separate listing or an internal carve-out, and on what timetable, was not stated in any source read in this session: **Not verified**, and worth asking about rather than assuming.

The UK trading entity is Siemens Healthcare Limited, company number 09567186, incorporated 29 April 2015, active at Companies House, registered office Park View, Watchmoor Park, Camberley, Surrey GU15 3YL, accounts made up to 30 September 2025. Siemens Healthcare Diagnostics Limited (company number 03050664) is a separate registered entity at the same address, which is worth knowing when a contract or an NHS purchase order names one and not the other. Varian Medical Systems UK Limited (company number 00558526) is a further separate entity and NHS Supply Chain lists Varian as a distinct supplier.

press.text: Siemens AG announces it plans to deconsolidate its stake of around 67% in Siemens Healthineers, with a transfer of about 30% of the shares to Siemens shareholders by way of a direct spin-off as the preferred option, and a medium-term intention to reduce the holding to a financial asset.

Siemens Healthineers Magnet Technology in Oxford hosts the President of the Federal Republic of Germany, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, and the First Lady, on their official UK visit. The company's own release names Ghada Trotabas as Managing Director of Siemens Healthineers Great Britain and Ireland.
NHS Fife reports MRI scan times reduced by over 20% using Deep Resolve AI from Siemens Healthineers.
A €10m Centre of Excellence for Immunoassay Instrument Research & Development opens at Swords, Ireland.

At the annual shareholders' meeting, CEO Bernd Montag states that Imaging and Precision Therapy form the "highly synergetic core" of the company, that Diagnostics "has few synergies with the other segments", and that the next step is for Diagnostics to pursue its own strategy "and derived from that, its own independent structure". The meeting also approves a dividend of €1.00 a share for FY2025 and marks the start of the "Elevating Health Globally" strategy phase.
The University of Edinburgh installs Scotland's first photon-counting CT scanner (NAEOTOM Alpha).
The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre becomes the first in the UK to install the Biograph Trinion PET-CT, reporting scan times cut by over 70%.

Siemens AG confirms the spin-off mechanism and timetable: a direct spin-off under the German Transformation Act, with Siemens AG shareholders receiving Siemens Healthineers AG shares directly, to be voted on at the ordinary Siemens AGM in February 2027. Final regulatory confirmation outstanding.
A new 8X radiopharmacy is announced for Dunstable, described by the company as the UK's first, at eight times the output of a single Radiopharma facility today.

Q3 FY2026 results: revenue €5,764m, up 2.8% comparable, equipment book-to-bill 1.27, adjusted EBIT margin 19.1%, adjusted EPS €0.70, free cash flow €1.0bn. FY2026 comparable revenue growth guidance cut to 3.5% to 4.0% on Diagnostics, adjusted EPS guidance raised to €2.35 to €2.45 on U.S. IEEPA tariff refunds.
St. Vincent's Private Hospital becomes the first in Ireland to install the LUMINOS Q.namix R fluoroscopy system.

hiring: Siemens Healthineers recruits UK field roles through its own careers site rather than through a job board feed this pipeline can read, so a live UK vacancy count was not captured in this session and is not asserted. What the company does publish about its UK workforce is substantial: about 3,000 employees across the UK and Ireland, around 60 early-careers roles hired a year across graduate, intern and apprentice programmes, about £2.8m spent on training and development in FY2024, and more than 45,000 training hours a year. It has been named by Great Place To Work as one of the UK's Best Workplaces and Best Workplaces for Development. All of those are the company's own figures from its own UK & Ireland fact sheet.

The UK operation is not just a sales office, which matters for how a commercial role is scoped: eight manufacturing sites are operational or under construction across the UK and Ireland with a combined footprint over 110,000 m², including superconducting magnet manufacture at Oxford, IMMULITE reagent manufacture at Llanberis (the sole global manufacturer, per the company), instrument design and assembly at Sudbury, and haematology and immunoassay analysers at Swords. A 56,000 m² magnet facility in North Oxfordshire is under development, part of about £380m of investment in new production facilities and machinery between 2024 and 2027.
marketPosition: No verified market-share percentage is stated here for the group. The company describes itself as a global provider active in more than 180 countries with direct representation in more than 70, and at the February 2026 shareholders' meeting it did claim that Varian has increased its market share by 10 percentage points since 2021 to above 60 percent. That is the company's own claim about its own segment, made at its own shareholders' meeting, and it is repeated here as such rather than as an independently verified figure.

The UK-specific evidence of position is the NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 14 live frameworks confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, and the shape of that list is the point. Eleven of the fourteen sit in the Diagnostic Equipment and Services category, covering CT, MRI, mammography, static and mobile X-ray, fluoroscopy, mobile image intensifiers, nuclear medicine, ultrasound, angiography and hybrid theatres, digital diagnostic solutions, and laboratory diagnostics, point-of-care testing and pathology managed services. Very few suppliers hold that many imaging modality frameworks at once. The company also reports around 1,000 UK and Ireland customers across NHS and private healthcare and around 30 Value Partnerships with NHS trusts and private providers.

The commercially interesting tension for a rep is that the strongest part of the NHS-facing franchise, imaging capital and managed services, sits in the segment being kept, while pathology and point-of-care sit in the segment being separated. Whoever ends up owning Diagnostics inherits an installed base of Atellica, IMMULITE and Aptio in NHS labs and the managed-service contracts wrapped around it.

glassdoor.summary: 82% of reviewers would recommend Siemens Healthineers to a friend. Sub-scores: work-life balance 4.1, culture and values 4.1, compensation and benefits 3.8, career opportunities 3.6 — career opportunities being the clear weak spot. This is the company-wide review base, not a UK sample, so treat it as indicative of the group rather than of the Camberley commercial team. The UK manufacturing sites score higher where a local sample exists: Oxford 4.5 from 39 reviews, Sudbury 4.4 from 16.

deepDive.interview: Lead with the structure question, because it is the live one and it shows you have read something more recent than the corporate boilerplate. Ask which segment the role sits in and what the Diagnostics separation means for it: the CEO said on 5 February 2026 that Diagnostics will pursue its own strategy and its own independent structure, and the form and timing of that are not public, so it is a fair and informed question rather than a gotcha. Do not confuse the two changes — Siemens AG spinning off its stake, voted February 2027, is about who owns the shares, while the Diagnostics separation is about the shape of the business — and do not describe either as done. Know the segment structure changed on 1 October 2025: Varian and Advanced Therapies are now one Precision Therapy segment, so anybody quoting a "Varian segment" number is quoting something historic. Know the momentum split, because it drives the whole conversation: Precision Therapy +9.2% and Imaging +2.3% in Q3 FY2026 against Diagnostics −5.5%, with a group equipment book-to-bill of 1.27 that says orders are strong even where revenue is soft. On the NHS side, be specific: MAGNETOM, NAEOTOM Alpha photon-counting CT, Biograph PET-CT, MAMMOMAT, ARTIS and syngo are the imaging names clinicians will recognise; Atellica, IMMULITE, Aptio and epoc are the lab and point-of-care names. And know that the UK is a manufacturing country for this company, not just a market — Oxford magnets, Llanberis reagents, Sudbury instruments — because that lands well with a UK hiring manager and is a genuine differentiator against most of the imaging competition.

background.heading: Speciality re-tagging
background.text: SIRT (selective internal radiation therapy) is a percutaneous, catheter-based procedure performed by interventional radiologists within a hepatobiliary/liver MDT -- IR is the operating speciality, oncology the referring/MDT context. NHS England routinely commissions SIRT specifically for chemotherapy-refractory/intolerant, unresectable colorectal cancer liver metastases (per the 2014-2017 Commissioning through Evaluation review with NICE, Oct 2017); SIRT for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is explicitly NOT routinely commissioned. Routine-commissioning status for primary HCC specifically could not be confirmed either way.
background.source: NHS England specialised commissioning policy library / British Liver Trust

background.heading: Product attribution correction
background.text: Owned since 2018 by a consortium of CDH Genetech (CDH Investments) and China Grand Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Holdings (Grand Pharma 51% / CDH 49%), delisted from the ASX 24/09/2018 -- no ownership change found since. Main competing product is TheraSphere Y-90 glass microspheres, which belongs to Boston Scientific (via its 2019 BTG acquisition), NOT Sirtex -- do not conflate the two companies' Y-90 products or their respective dosimetry software (Sirtex/MIM's SurePlan LiverY90 vs Boston Scientific/Mirada Medical's Simplicit90Y).
background.source: Wikipedia / PR Newswire / Boston Scientific product pages

deepDive.tagline: The UK and Ireland trading company of the STERIS group: sterilisation and decontamination equipment, endoscope reprocessing, theatre equipment and GI/endoscopy consumables, on ten NHS Supply Chain frameworks, with a Republic of Ireland branch that is roughly a quarter of its turnover.
deepDive.lede: Three things, and the first one will keep you out of trouble. STERIS Solutions Limited has grown turnover from £77.5m to £98.5m to £110.6m across the three years to 31 March 2025, and its own directors attribute the rise in both of the last two years to trade and assets moved in from fellow group companies rather than to business won: the 2024 strategic report says increases "were driven by the acquisition of certain trade and assets from fellow group companies during the prior year", and the 2025 one says the increase was "predominantly driven" by the same thing, contributing an estimated £12m. Turnover rose £12.0m that year. So the underlying number is close to flat, and a growth line quoted off the headline is a line the directors themselves do not make. Second, this is not a UK-only company: of £110.6m in FY2025, £77.9m was United Kingdom and £29.9m was Republic of Ireland, from a branch the accounts say it continues to run. Ireland has sat between £29.4m and £29.9m for three straight years while the UK went from £46.8m to £77.9m, so every pound of growth in this company is a UK pound. Third, the commercial shape: 126 people in Sales out of 258 employees, three fewer than the year before while turnover rose 12%, and £7,000,000 of dividends paid out of a £4,025,978 profit — the strategic report says in terms that shareholder's funds fell because the dividend exceeded the year's profit. The registered office moved from Syston, Leicester to Basingstoke on 31 July 2026.

stats.n: £110,563,286. Read from the line the company itself labels Turnover on the face of its statement of comprehensive income, page 11, and repeated in the key performance indicator table on page 1 and in note 3 on page 20, in the full accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 filed at Companies House on 20 December 2025 (02767165, 32 pages, audited by Ernst & Young LLP). Prior year £98,543,685. The filing IS tagged iXBRL, but it carries no turnover tag among the tags it does carry, which is why company-financials.json in this Hub shows no turnover for the company while this record does.

£29,885,017 of £110,563,286, or 27.0%, from the turnover-by-geographical-market table in note 3, page 20 of the 2025 accounts. United Kingdom £77,949,106, Rest of the world £2,729,163. The comparatives in the same note and in note 3 of the 2024 accounts give Republic of Ireland £29,435,050 (FY2024) and £29,732,856 (FY2023) against United Kingdom £67,948,380 and £46,795,014. The strategic report states the company "continues to have a branch in the Republic of Ireland".

stats.l: Estimated turnover contributed by the Diagmed transfer, FY2025
stats.n: Note 21 of the 2025 accounts, page 27: "On 1 April 2024 the company acquired the business of Diagmed Healthcare Limited", total identifiable net assets £1,256,210 (inventories £1,359,677, trade and other receivables £1,200, trade and other payables £(104,667)), consideration £1,256,210 satisfied in cash, and "Since the acquisition, it is estimated that the contribution to turnover has been £12m and the contribution to Profit after tax has been £1.4m." Turnover rose £12,019,601 that year. The company's own section 172 statement describes the same transfer, calling the entity "Diagmed Healthcare UK Limited", and says several of its employees continued with STERIS Solutions.

Note 6 of the 2025 accounts, page 21: Sales 126 (2024: 129), Technical support 85 (83), Administration 47 (43), total average monthly number of persons including directors 258 (255). Note 6 of the 2024 accounts gives the FY2023 split as Sales 103, Technical support 61, Administration 40, total 204. So the sales force grew by 26 in FY2024 and fell by 3 in FY2025. Aggregate remuneration FY2025 £21,111,026 — wages and salaries £17,307,388, social security £2,109,790, pension £1,693,848.

£4,726,223, down from £5,359,996, from the statement of comprehensive income on page 11. Gross profit was £36,302,611 against £36,343,616 — flat on £12.0m more sales, so the gross margin fell from 36.9% to 32.8% (percentages computed here from the two figures on that page). The strategic report on page 1 gives the directors' own explanation: "rising costs of raw materials only saw gross profit rise by £2m", distribution expenses rose, and "salaries rising by ~£1m was the main driver in the increase in administrative expenses". Profit before taxation £5,163,053, tax £1,137,075, profit for the financial year £4,025,978.

£7,000,000, from the statement of changes in equity in the 2025 accounts and repeated in the section 172 statement ("The company paid dividends of £7,000,000 during the year to 31 March 2025"). FY2024 £5,000,000 (note 10 of the 2024 accounts, "Final paid"), FY2023 nil. So £12,000,000 has left the company over two years against profits for those financial years of £4,918,863 and £4,025,978. Shareholder's funds fell from £8,536,152 to £5,878,504, and the strategic report says so directly: "The shareholder's funds dropped due to the declaration of a dividend during the year in excess of profit in the year." Current assets as a percentage of current liabilities fell from 119.5% to 107.5% (both figures from the company's own KPI table, page 1).

prose: The split of turnover by class of business, from note 3 of each filing, is worth carrying into a meeting because a third of this company is not product sales. FY2025: sale of goods £86,813,059, sale of services £17,267,465, provision of services to group companies £6,482,762. FY2024: £75,992,736, £15,146,834 and £7,404,115. So services to other STERIS companies were 5.9% of turnover in FY2025 and 7.5% in FY2024 — revenue that has nothing to do with any NHS customer, and which the strategic report reflects when it describes the principal activities as including "the provision of management services to group operations throughout Europe".

Directors' remuneration appears in this company for the first time in FY2025: note 7 gives remuneration for qualifying services £119,325 and company pension contributions £7,432, a total of £126,757, against nil in FY2024. Note 7 of the 2024 accounts explains the nil: "Directors' remuneration for all the directors have been borne by another group company." The audit fee for the audit of the company's own financial statements was £52,347 (FY2024 £51,070).

ownership: STERIS SOLUTIONS LIMITED, company number 02767165, registered office 2200 Renaissance Basing View, Basingstoke, Hampshire, England, RG21 4EQ, is a private limited company incorporated on 24 November 1992 and currently Active, SIC 46460 wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. Its previous registered names, from the register's own table read 23/08/2026, are STERIS LIMITED (2 March 1998 to 20 October 2015), AMSCO (U.K.) LTD. (19 January 1993 to 2 March 1998) and WEIGHTVIEW PROJECTS LIMITED (24 November 1992 to 19 January 1993) — which is why AMSCO, still a live product name in this Hub's range for the company, is also the name this legal entity traded under thirty years ago.

The persons with significant control register, read 23/08/2026, holds one active entry: Steris Dover Limited, company 11241200, incorporated in England, of 2200 Renaissance, Basing View, Basingstoke RG21 4EQ, notified 26 March 2018, holding 75% or more of the shares and 75% or more of the voting rights. The only other entry is a ceased one, Steris Plc, company 09257343, incorporated in England, of Chancery House, 190 Waterside Road, Hamilton Industrial Park, Leicester LE5 1QZ, notified 6 April 2016 and ceased 26 March 2018.

The accounts describe the chain differently from the PSC register, and both are recorded here rather than reconciled, because reconciling them would be a guess. Note 24 of the 2025 accounts states: "The company's immediate parent undertaking is STERIS Holdings BV, a company incorporated in the Netherlands. The ultimate parent undertaking and controlling party is STERIS plc a company incorporated and domiciled in Ireland. The largest and smallest group for which consolidated financial statements are prepared is STERIS plc", with copies available from its registered office at 70 Sir John Rogerson's Quay, Dublin 2, D02 R296, Ireland. So the register names an English company as the controller and the accounts name a Dutch immediate parent and an Irish ultimate parent. What is not in doubt is that the UK trading company is a subsidiary several layers below a listed group, and that its dividend policy is set above it.

The registered office moved on 31 July 2026. The AD01 filed that day records the change "from Chancery House Rayns Way, Watermead Business Park Syston Leicester LE7 1PF United Kingdom to 2200 Renaissance Basing View Basingstoke Hampshire RG21 4EQ on 31 July 2026". The accounts filed in December 2025 still print the Leicester address. DIAGMED HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company 04707660, whose business this company acquired on 1 April 2024, is registered at the same Basingstoke address, remains Active on the register with accounts last made up to 31 March 2025, and is a separate legal entity from this one. There is no company on the register called Diagmed Healthcare UK Limited, the name the section 172 statement uses.

deepDive.peopleNote: Companies House records 28 officers and 24 resignations for 02767165, leaving three people in four active appointments, all listed above. No commercial leadership is published for the UK company: steris.com is a group site and names no UK managing director, sales director or commercial director, so unlike several other records in this Hub there is no company-published leadership list to set beside the register, and none is invented here. The dated board events on the register since 2016 are: Dennis Patrick Patton resigned as director and as secretary on 30 June 2016, and Julia Kipnis was appointed director and Ronald E Snyder secretary the same day; John Patrick Ubbing was appointed director on 6 September 2022 and Julia Kipnis resigned the same day; Ronald E Snyder resigned as director and as secretary on 30 August 2024; Allan John Rowley was appointed director and John Patrick Ubbing secretary on 16 September 2024; Michael Joseph Tokich resigned as director on 14 November 2025 and Karen Louise Burton was appointed the same day. Those are dated register events only. Nothing here says any person replaced any other, because succession is not a register fact and several of these dates coincide for reasons the register does not give. Two of the three directors are resident in the United States; the practical read for a rep is that UK commercial decisions are unlikely to sit with the statutory board.
marketPosition: The framework footprint is the independently checkable part, and it is broad rather than deep. NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs name this company on ten frameworks, captured for this Hub on 20/08/2026 and listed with their dates, references and supplier counts on the framework panel of this record rather than restated here: Decontamination Capital Equipment, Digital Diagnostic Solutions, Electrosurgical Consumables, Endoscopy Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables, Instrument Decontamination and Accessories, Operating Theatres Equipment, Patient Temperature Management, Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling, and Tray Wrap and Sterilisation Equipment. The briefs name it variously as "Steris Solutions Limited", "STERIS Solutions Limited" and "Steris Solutions Ltd", which independently ties the Hub record to company 02767165.

Where the field is small, that place is worth more. On the briefs captured, this company is one of 8 suppliers on Tray Wrap and Sterilisation Equipment, one of 18 on Patient Temperature Management, and one of 20 on each of Instrument Decontamination and Accessories and Decontamination Capital Equipment. On the wider ones it is one of 58 (Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables), one of 54 (Digital Diagnostic Solutions) and one of 53 (Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling). Those counts are the briefs' own and are recorded per framework on this record.

On the product range: this Hub holds 733 items for Steris, read on 07/08/2026 from the steris.com XML sitemap. That is the GROUP's global catalogue, not a UK availability list, and its own division names are American-spelled ("Sterilizers"). The largest divisions are Surgical Table Accessories (245), Endoscopy Devices (119), Sterility Assurance and Monitoring (57), Endoscope Reprocessing (51) and Washing and Decontamination Systems (39). Treat it as the shape of what the group makes, and check NHS Supply Chain or the company before telling a customer any single line is available to them here.

One derived observation, with its rule stated so it can be judged: adding the FY2025 turnover-by-class figures to the FY2025 employee split shows £110,563,286 of turnover against 126 people in Sales, or roughly £0.88m of turnover per sales head, and 85 in Technical support against a business whose principal activities include servicing installed capital equipment. This is a ratio computed here from two figures in the same filing, not a figure the company publishes, and it says nothing about individual quota. What it does suggest is a capital-equipment-and-service model rather than a consumables-volume one, which is consistent with the frameworks it sits on.

deepDive.interview: Do not quote the growth. Turnover went £77.5m, £98.5m, £110.6m across the three years to March 2025, and the directors attribute both rises to trade moved in from fellow group companies — in FY2025, an estimated £12m of a £12.0m increase, from the Diagmed Healthcare business acquired on 1 April 2024 for £1,256,210 in cash. Saying "you've grown 12%" to someone who signed those accounts will land badly; asking what the Diagmed integration has actually done to their endoscopy coverage will not. Know that Ireland is roughly a quarter of the company — £29.9m of £110.6m — and that it has not moved in three years while the UK has, so if you are being told a UK growth story, the Irish branch is the flat part of it. On margin, the honest read is a business absorbing cost it cannot pass on: gross profit was flat at £36.3m on £12m more sales, the directors name raw material costs, and operating profit fell to £4.73m. And the money leaves: £5m of dividends in FY2024 and £7m in FY2025 against a £4.03m profit, with the strategic report saying plainly that shareholder's funds dropped because the dividend exceeded the profit. That is an owner taking cash out, not reinvesting, which is the opposite of the Mediq picture in this Hub and tells you what a capital business case here has to clear. On people: 126 in Sales, down three while turnover rose, and 85 in Technical support — this is a service-and-capital business, so the service contract is often the real conversation and the installed base is the real barrier. Do not expect the board to be your route in: three directors, two of them resident in the United States, one company secretary who is also a director, and no UK commercial leadership published anywhere. Finally, if you are searching for this company, search all of "Steris Solutions", "STERIS Limited" and "AMSCO" — the register shows all three as names of company 02767165 — and note the registered office moved to Basingstoke on 31 July 2026, so anything filed under Leicester is out of date.

alerts.text: Urgent recall of TMJ (temporomandibular joint) patient-fitted implants, issued 30/09/2025 and expanded 04/12/2025 and 25/02/2026: a design discrepancy could place a 6mm screw into ~2.6mm-thick bone, risking cranial vault penetration (dural damage, CSF leak, meningitis). One serious injury reported as of Dec 2025, no deaths. UK/MHRA-specific status not independently verified (FDA/US source only).

Voluntary recall (June 2026, single US unit) of the Neptune Smart Docking Station after FDA flagged unverifiable safety testing and potential electrical shock risk. Neptune 2 (the related waste-management product) is confirmed live on NHS Supply Chain -- worth knowing even though this specific recall record appears US-scoped; UK/MHRA status not verified.

news.text: Apr 2026: NHS England and NHS Supply Chain coordinated response to Stryker cyber-attack supply disruption; manufacturing expected back to normal levels by 10 April 2026.

deepDive.tagline: NYSE-listed (SYK), FY2025 group net sales $25.1bn · UK entity Stryker UK Limited, Stryker House, Hambridge Road, Newbury · recovering from a global cyber attack that forced NHS England to run a national stock SitRep in March 2026

links.label: NHS England letter on the disruption

deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: on 11 March 2026 Stryker was hit by a cyber attack that took down its internal Microsoft environment worldwide, halted production and stopped electronic ordering. It was serious enough that NHS England wrote to every acute, community, mental health and ambulance trust, ran a national stock SitRep with a 4pm deadline, cancelled every Stryker order placed between 11 and 16 March, and stood up an interim ordering route through NHS Supply Chain and Stryker's logistics partner DHL. Some patient-specific implant cases were rescheduled. Then the company recovered: Q2 2026 sales were $6.6bn, up 9.4%, and the full-year guidance held. That arc, a supplier that failed its customers badly for a fortnight and then earned its way back, is the single most useful thing to have a view on in this interview.

prose: There is no readable UK turnover for Stryker. Stryker UK Limited (company number 03669454) files full accounts, most recently made up to 31 December 2025, but they are filed as a PDF with no tagged figures, so nothing is read from them: picking the turnover line off a PDF by position would be a guess, not a reading. Every financial figure here is therefore group-wide and comes from Stryker's own published releases.

FY2025 was a strong year on any measure. Group net sales reached $25,116m, up 11.2% reported and 10.3% organic, with MedSurg and Neurotechnology up 15.7% to $15,647m and Orthopaedics up 4.3% to $9,469m. The Orthopaedics number understates the underlying business, because Spinal Implants fell 73.9% to $185m after the US spinal implants sale completed on 1 April 2025; strip that out and the rest of Orthopaedics grew 10.9%. Vascular grew 50.6% to $1,968m on the Inari Medical acquisition. Reported operating margin was 19.5%, adjusted 26.3%.

2026 has been the cyber year. Q1 2026 net sales were $6.020bn, up just 2.6%, with reported gross margin pressed to 63.3% by idle production time, and the company missed consensus. Kevin Lobo told investors the incident 'meaningfully' affected growth and hit each business differently depending on its route to market. Q2 2026 then came in at $6.6bn, up 9.4% reported and 9.0% organic, with reported net earnings up 44.3%, and Stryker held its full-year organic growth guidance of 8.0% to 9.5% and adjusted EPS of $14.90 to $15.10.

ownership: Stryker Corporation is a publicly listed US company, NYSE ticker SYK, headquartered at 1941 Stryker Way, Portage, Michigan. There is no private-equity or family owner to know about: the relevant ownership fact for a UK candidate is simply that decisions on portfolio, pricing and structure are made in Michigan and land in Newbury.

The UK operating entity is Stryker UK Limited, company number 03669454, incorporated 12 November 1998, confirmed active at Companies House with accounts made up to 31 December 2025. A separate holding entity, Stryker UK Technologies Holdings Ltd (company number 14772563), also exists on the register; the trading entity NHS customers contract with is Stryker UK Limited.

press.text: Stryker completes the sale of its US spinal implants business to Viscogliosi Brothers, LLC, forming VB Spine, LLC. VB Spine gets exclusive access to Mako Spine and Copilot for use with its implants. Certain international markets were stated as transferring later. Stryker's own release.
Kevin Lobo, Stryker's Chair and CEO, joins GE HealthCare's board of directors, effective this date, per GE HealthCare's own announcement.

Cyber attack causes a global disruption to Stryker's internal Microsoft environment, halting order processing, manufacturing and shipping. Stryker states its products, connected and otherwise, were not affected and remain safe to use.

NHS England issues an EPRR publication (PRN02438) to trust COOs, medical directors, heads of procurement, EPRR and nursing directors: UK stock estimated at around two weeks at normal ordering volumes, orders placed 11 to 16 March cancelled, an interim ordering route stood up via NHS Supply Chain and Stryker's logistics partner DHL, six NHS Supply Chain stocked lines put under Control Demand Management, and a mandatory national SitRep from every acute, community, mental health and ambulance trust by 4pm on 19 March. Trusts told to organise mutual aid and to engage independent-sector providers.

Stryker confirms some patient-specific implant cases scheduled for the week of 16 March were rescheduled because of shipping delays, and thanks the White House National Cyber Director, FBI, CISA, DHA, HHS and H-ISAC for support.

Stryker states the incident is contained. Its investigation with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 identified a malicious file used to run commands and hide activity, revising the company's earlier position that there was no indication of malware. Unit 42 issued a general assurance letter finding no evidence the threat actor reached customer, supplier, vendor or partner systems.

Stryker completes the acquisition of Amplitude Vascular Systems, adding a CO2-generated pressure wave intravascular lithotripsy platform for complex peripheral arterial disease. Terms undisclosed, closed under a month after announcement.
Q2 2026 results: net sales $6.6bn, up 9.4% reported and 9.0% organic; reported net earnings up 44.3%. Lobo describes 'significant progress in our recovery from the cyber incident'.

hiring: Stryker recruits UK field sales through its own careers site (careers.stryker.com) rather than through a job board feed this pipeline can read, so a live UK vacancy count was not captured in this session and is not asserted. What is verifiable is that Stryker's own guidance during the March 2026 disruption leaned heavily on the field force: customers were told repeatedly to direct all product questions to their local sales representative, that reps would arrange manual ordering where electronic ordering was down, and that it was safe for reps to be on site in hospitals. That is a company whose UK commercial model runs through people in theatres, which is worth knowing before an interview for one of those roles.
marketPosition: Stryker describes itself as 'a global leader in medical technologies' and says it impacts more than 150 million patients annually; those are the company's own words and its own figure, not an independently audited claim, and no verified market-share percentage was found in this session, so none is stated. The clearest UK-specific evidence of scale is its NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 14 separate live frameworks confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, spanning total orthopaedic solutions, operating theatre equipment, surgical navigation, rigid endoscopy, minimally invasive surgery, electrosurgical consumables, wound closure, external defibrillation, pulse oximetry and capnography, pressure area care and patient handling, medical healthcare furniture, CT scanners, electrodes and ultrasound gels, and medical chart paper.

NHS England's own March 2026 letter is a second, blunter measure of position: it lists trust dependency on Stryker across trauma and orthopaedics, neuroradiology including microwires, other surgical technology and consumables, connected devices, rehabilitation and community, diagnostics and equipment services, and facilities and office solutions, and judged the national exposure serious enough to require a return from every acute, community, mental health and ambulance trust. Few suppliers reach that far into an NHS trust.
