glassdoor.scale: /5 on Glassdoor UK, from 49 reviews by employees based in London, England
glassdoor.summary: 79% of London-based employees would recommend Stryker to a friend. Sub-scores for the London sample: compensation and benefits 3.9, work-life balance 3.6, diversity and inclusion 4.2, culture and values 4.1, career opportunities 4.0, each of which sits below the company-wide equivalent. The company-wide review base is large, over 7,200 reviews, but the company-wide star rating was not captured in this session and is not stated here. Treat a 49-review London sample as indicative, not definitive, and note it is not the same population as the Newbury commercial team.

deepDive.interview: Bring the cyber incident up yourself, carefully. Do not use it as a gotcha; use it to show you understand what a supplier owes an NHS customer. A good question sounds like: what changed in UK order management and business continuity after March, and what would a rep do differently if it happened again? Know the shape of the portfolio too: Stryker sold its US spinal implants business to VB Spine on 1 April 2025 and stayed in spine only through Interventional Spine, Neurotechnology and Enabling Technologies, so do not walk in describing Stryker as a spinal implants company. Know which segment the role sits in, because MedSurg and Neurotechnology grew 15.7% in FY2025 while Orthopaedics grew 4.3% on a reported basis, and the two have very different momentum stories. Mako, Triathlon, LIFEPAK and ProCuity are the names most NHS clinicians will recognise. If the role touches trauma and orthopaedics, expect procurement to remember March 2026 clearly.

alerts.title: Self-Retaining (Foley) 2-Way PTFE Coated Latex catheters, 12Ch to 22Ch (12 product codes)
alerts.detail: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3267, opened 24/02/2026 and last updated 09/07/2026, now marked Resolved and closed. Teleflex Medical UK has discontinued the range and NHS Supply Chain has requested all 12 codes be delisted from the catalogue. FSS137 is delisted and unavailable to order. Six codes remain available while remaining stocks last and will then be delisted: FSS134, FSS136, FSS138, FSS141, FSS142 and FSS143. Five were delisted at the 29/05/2026 update: FSS10089, FSS10090, FSS1028, FSS1029 and FSS144. Indirect alternatives are mapped on the online catalogue and a product matrix is available; NHS Supply Chain advises consulting clinical experts on suitability.
alerts.use: Every trust still ordering these PTFE-coated latex Foley codes has to convert as stock runs out, so this is a live switching conversation for any indwelling-catheter supplier. Ask which of the six remaining codes they still order and whether an alternative has actually been agreed with their clinical team, or only mapped.

background.heading: Divestment and spin-off
background.text: Teleflex announced (09/12/2025) the sale of its Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses to Intersurgical Ltd (private UK company, Wokingham) for $530m, and its OEM business to Montagu and Kohlberg for ~$1.5bn -- combined $2.03bn, expected to close H2 2026. Per the business-unit allocation confirmed at primary-source level, most of what currently sits under this record's Anaesthesia tag (Rüsch/LMA airway) and all of Urology (UroLift, Barrigel, Rüsch Foley/ureteral) is expected to move to Intersurgical -- Vascular Access (Arrow), Interventional and Surgical (Weck/Deknatel) are expected to remain with Teleflex. Brand-level detail is from an earlier, now-superseded separation plan (Feb 2025) and hasn't been independently re-confirmed in the December sale documents -- treat as likely but not certified. Revisit this record once the sale closes rather than pre-emptively splitting products now.

deepDive.tagline: Basildon anaesthesia, general medical and surgical instrument maker, family-owned and trading since 1964 on its own account, named on 8 NHS Supply Chain frameworks · turnover fell from £12.8m to £9.0m as PPE income vanished, and £15m left the company as dividends in the same year
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Timesco had one extraordinary pandemic year, distributed the proceeds, and has been a smaller company ever since. Its own audited accounts for the year to 28 February 2023 record turnover of £8,965,149 against £12,787,629 the year before, and the directors say why in their own strategic report: "2022 was a bumper year mainly due to PPE related revenue." The class-of-business note makes that literal. PPE turnover was £3,929,193 in FY2022 and £2,366 in FY2023. In the same year the company paid an interim dividend of £75,000 per share, £15,000,000 in total, and net assets fell from £23,299,686 to £8,828,814. Since then it has taken audit exemption and filed abridged accounts, which by law deliver no income statement, so no turnover figure after February 2023 exists on the public record and none is invented here. What the balance sheets do show is a steady contraction: retained earnings £8,828,812, then £7,094,675, then £6,480,524; average headcount 45, then 41, then 38; cash £5.73m, then £4.61m, then £4.52m. Set that against eight NHS Supply Chain frameworks, two of which started in 2026, and the question in the room writes itself: this is a business whose NHS category access is holding up better than its published financial trajectory, and whoever joins the commercial team is being hired to close that gap.

prose: Two turnover figures are on the public record and no more. Timesco Healthcare Limited turned over £12,787,629 in the year to 28 February 2022 and £8,965,149 in the year to 28 February 2023, both read from the tagged accounts. The company's own strategic report describes FY2022 as "a bumper year mainly due to PPE related revenue" and reports gross margin easing from 44.12% to 39.42%, EBITDA of £778,662 against £2,484,769, debtor days lengthening from 48 to 60 and creditor days shortening from 38 to 35. Profit before tax was £552,608 against £2,394,982; profit after tax £529,128 against £2,053,039.

The class-of-business note is where the shape of the fall shows. On the company's own segment names, FY2023 against FY2022: PPE £2,366 against £3,929,193; GenMed £4,240,620 against £5,741,163; Anaesthetic £2,860,737 against £2,291,258; Services £891,328 against nil; Electro £583,515 against £458,703; Surgical £161,212 against £245,035; Chiropractic £152,140 against £122,277; Despatch £73,231 against nil. So the whole of the decline is PPE and GenMed, while anaesthesia, the range the company is best known for, grew by £569,479 in the worst year it has published. By geography, United Kingdom sales were £7,600,997 of the FY2023 total and £11,431,811 of FY2022, with the rest of the world almost flat at £1,364,152 against £1,355,818.

After that the record goes quiet, and the reason is a filing choice rather than a gap in this pipeline. The FY2023 accounts were audited by Raffingers LLP. For FY2024 and FY2025 the company took audit exemption under section 477 of the Companies Act 2006 and filed abridged accounts under section 444(2A), which deliver a balance sheet and notes but no profit and loss account. What can be read from those balance sheets is that retained earnings fell from £8,828,812 at 28 February 2023 to £7,094,675 and then to £6,480,524; stocks fell to £1,670,787; debtors to £1,168,061; cash held broadly flat at £4,519,536. That movement in retained earnings is NOT reported here as a loss. Retained earnings move by profit or loss less distributions, the abridged filings disclose neither, and attributing the change to trading would be a guess dressed as a figure.

ownership: TIMESCO HEALTHCARE LIMITED, company number 03346938, was incorporated on 8 April 1997 and is active. It has carried three names: Timesco of London Limited and Timesco of London (2005) Limited before becoming TIMESCO HEALTHCARE LIMITED on 31 August 2012. Its registered SIC codes are 26600, manufacture of irradiation, electromedical and electrotherapeutic equipment, and 47749, retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods in specialised stores. The registered office moved on 18 April 2023 from 19-20 Bourne Court, Southend Road, Woodford Green, Essex IG8 8HD to Timesco House, 3 Carnival Park, Carnival Close, Basildon, Essex SS14 3WN. The Woodford Green address is the office of its accountants, Raffingers.

There is no parent company on the register. The only active person with significant control is Mrs Nabila Naseem Fayyaz, notified on 2 February 2022, holding more than 25% but not more than 50% of the shares and of the voting rights. Three earlier PSC entries have ceased: Mr Sohail Fayyaz and Mrs Andeleeb Fayyaz, both notified 6 April 2016 and 11 April 2019 respectively and both ceased in April 2019, and Mr Shahjehan Fayyaz, notified 6 April 2016 and ceased 5 November 2021. Read that register carefully before repeating it: no one is recorded as holding a majority of this company, and the single active entry is a 25 to 50% holding. This is a British family business with decisions taken in Basildon, not a subsidiary of an overseas manufacturer.

Three charges are registered and all three are outstanding: a debenture in favour of HSBC Bank PLC created 6 February 2003, a fixed charge on purchased debts which fail to vest in favour of HSBC Invoice Finance (UK) Ltd created 23 January 2006, and a general pledge in favour of HSBC Bank PLC created 6 October 2015. The related party notes name a second structure a rep should know about: the company pays rent to Timesco Property Partnership, a partnership in which Mr Sohail Fayyaz and Mrs Nabila Fayyaz are members, £285,000 in FY2023, £299,400 in FY2024 and £306,600 in FY2025. Remuneration paid to close family members of the directors and key management personnel was £337,638 in FY2023, £224,157 in FY2024 and £163,689 in FY2025. A separate company, TIMESCO OF LONDON LIMITED, number 08182773, registered at the same Basildon address, was dissolved on 14 October 2025.

hiring: Timesco's own careers page carried no live vacancies on 19/08/2026: the Current Vacancies section reads only "Thank you for your interest in Timesco." The page is worth reading anyway, because it says something specific about how the company staffs itself: "we're proud to say that 8 out of the 9 managers within our Senior Team have been recruited from within", and "We do not recruit people to do a job, we actively recruit people to have a career with us; and our average length of service demonstrates that we do this very well." Taken with an average headcount that has fallen from 45 to 38 in three years, that is a small, long-tenured company that promotes internally, so an external commercial hire here is likely to be a specific gap rather than a growth requisition. There is no applicant tracking system on the site and no salary information; roles are advertised through recruiters this check did not cover.
marketPosition: The verifiable measure of this company's NHS position is its framework footprint: named supplier on 8 separate NHS Supply Chain frameworks, each confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief. They are Airway Management Products and Associated Equipment (2023/S 000-005729, 22 July 2024 to 21 July 2028), Central Venous Catheters and Associated Products (2025/S 000-001530, 23 March 2026 to 22 March 2028), Electrosurgical Consumables and Related Accessories (2024/S 000-001161, 20 October 2025 to 19 October 2028), Maternity, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Sexual Health Products (2019/S 214-525123, 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2027), Pulse Oximetry, Capnography and Related Monitoring Technologies (2023/S 000-011885, 4 March 2024 to 4 March 2028), Respiratory Solutions (1 August 2022 to 15 June 2027), Surgical Instruments (2020/S 170-412524, 6 August 2021 to 12 July 2027) and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions (2025/S 000-032216, 4 August 2026 to 3 August 2028). The Airway Management, Surgical Instruments and Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions briefs were re-read on 19/08/2026 and name the company as "Timesco Healthcare Ltd" on each. Nothing expires within the next ten months; the earliest end date is Respiratory Solutions on 15 June 2027.

What it actually sells is best read from its own filings rather than its website, because the two are shaped differently. The class-of-business note in the FY2023 accounts puts GenMed at £4,240,620 and Anaesthetic at £2,860,737, which is 79% of turnover between them, with Electro £583,515, Surgical £161,212 and Chiropractic £152,140 much smaller. That last point is the one worth carrying into a conversation: Timesco is named on NHS Supply Chain's Surgical Instruments framework, and by its own segmentation surgical instruments were under 2% of the year's revenue. The framework award is category access, not a revenue line. The Hub's own crawl of timesco.com on 15/08/2026 read 224 products from the company's own catalogue, filed as General Medical 106, Anaesthesia 60 and Surgery 56, the largest single category being Airway Management with 54. Named ranges include the Callisto and Sirus XL laryngoscopes, Optima View video laryngoscopy, the Vide chest drainage system, the NeuroLight pupillometer, Wira-Flexi fixation, the Coral sphygmomanometer and Evac-S single use suction.

Two things sit outside that crawl and should not be mistaken for absences. Podiatry is a real Timesco division with its own site at timesco-podiatry.co.uk, selling foot dressers, nail probes, nail files and nail cutters plus a Social Nail Care single patient use range; it is not in the 224 products above because the Hub has only crawled timesco.com, and the accounts show that business, as Chiropractic, at £152,140 in FY2023. And the company's policies page states LSAS Level 3, the Labour Standards Assurance System, "for instrument and laryngoscope portfolios", alongside REACH and WEEE compliance, an ISO certificate referenced GBMD_010037, a Carbon Reduction Plan under PPN 06/21 updated August 2025 and steps toward ISO 14001. That matters commercially because labour standards assurance is exactly what NHS Supply Chain scrutinises in instrument categories: its Surgical Instruments brief states that "Sustainable procurement is embedded into our category management processes to ensure that our suppliers meet requirements for carbon reduction plans, evergreen assessment, modern slavery, social value and NHS England net zero supplier roadmap." The brief does not itself specify a required LSAS level, so the Level 3 claim is published here as the company's own statement about itself, read on its own site on 19/08/2026, and not as an NHS Supply Chain finding.

No market share is given here and none is calculable. The company's own scale claims are its own and are published as such: "3,000+ product lines available", "200+ distributors worldwide" and "8.5m+ medical devices supplied each year", all from timesco.com/about-us, read 19/08/2026. No Timesco product could be confirmed in this Hub's NHS Supply Chain catalogue cache by NPC, so no catalogue code is quoted; that is a gap in the cache rather than evidence the company has no catalogue lines.

deepDive.interview: Read the FY2023 accounts before you go in, because everything interesting is in them and almost nobody applying will have. Three questions come out of the filings and none of them is hostile. First, the PPE cliff: the directors wrote that 2022 was "a bumper year mainly due to PPE related revenue" and the segment note shows PPE going from £3.93m to £2,366 in twelve months, while anaesthesia grew. Asking what the company kept from that year, in customers or in listings, rather than what it lost, is a commercial question that shows you read the report. Second, the reporting gap: FY2024 and FY2025 were filed abridged with no income statement, so a candidate cannot know the current revenue, and asking straightforwardly where turnover sits now is fair and expected. Third, category access against category revenue: they are on the Surgical Instruments framework and surgical was £161,212 in the last published year, so ask which of the eight frameworks the team is actually being measured on. Two pieces of context to carry: the newest framework, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, started on 4 August 2026 and consolidates three older ones, which means live trust-level implementation work right now; and this is a family business with one active PSC holding 25 to 50%, no parent company and a landlord that is a partnership of two of its own directors, so the people you meet are the people who decide. Finally, know the two dates. The business says it has traded since 1964. The company you would be employed by was incorporated in 1997 and has been called Timesco Healthcare Limited since 2012.

deepDive.tagline: Family-run Stafford wholesaler of pharmacy packaging, disposables and dispensers, founded from a 1970s pharmacy sundries business, still fully owned and directed by the Pittock family.

deepDive.lede: Valley Northern is on the incumbent-plus list for NHS Supply Chain's new Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework, which starts 4 August 2026 and merges the old Patient Assessment Devices, Blood Pressure Cuffs and Thermometer Device frameworks into one 40-supplier deal. It is a genuinely family business, not a marketing line: all five current directors and all four people with significant control on the Companies House register share the surname Pittock, and the company's own history page traces the name back to a Valley Road pharmacy sundries business their grandfather David Pittock started in 1972.

prose: No turnover figure can be read for this company. Its Companies House filing history shows only total exemption full accounts each year (most recently to 31 December 2024, filed 25 June 2025), which is the small company exemption that lets a business file a balance sheet without a profit and loss account or a turnover figure. There is no group or subsidiary structure disclosed that would let a parent level number stand in for it, and Valley Northern's own website does not publish a turnover or key figures page.

The company does publish some scale indicators on its own homepage as live counters rather than audited figures: 810,957,000 bags supplied, six countries supplied, 1,414 product lines available online and 26 years industry experience, counting from the 2000 founding of Valley Northern specifically, not the earlier family pharmacy business. These are self-reported marketing statistics, not filed financial data, and are labelled as such here rather than treated as a growth series.

ownership: Valley Northern Limited, company number 09188858, is a private limited company incorporated on 28 August 2014, with its registered office at Valley Northern, Carver Road, Astonfields, Stafford ST16 3BP. Its SIC code is 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods. Status is active. Companies House, read 18/08/2026.

It is not part of any disclosed group structure and there is no parent company or PE or institutional shareholder on the register. The four active persons with significant control, notified 14 September 2020, are Adrian Pittock, Oliver John Pittock, Darren Pittock and Dale Pittock, each recorded with the generic nature of control has significant influence or control rather than a specific shareholding band. An earlier PSC statement, notified 19 August 2016 and ceased 16 December 2016, had recorded Adrian Pittock alone holding more than 25% but not more than 50% of shares and voting rights; that entry was superseded by the current four person notification in 2020, so the precise current shareholding split between the four is not stated on the public register and is marked Not verified here.

The company's own history page describes it as continuously family owned since its 1972 origins as a pharmacy sundries business, Valley Road, hence the name, through a 2000 split off into Valley Northern proper under Oliver Pittock, and incorporation as a limited company in 2014.

Launched a Controlled Drug Destruction Kit specifically designed for liquid medication, described on its own site as an industry first, alongside a Kinder to our planet range of eco-friendly packaging alternatives.
Supplied PPE dispensers to NHS Nightingale during the COVID-19 pandemic, alongside its ongoing supply to pharmacies, chemists and hospitals.

hiring: Valley Northern runs a single generic careers page, with no individually listed live vacancies, inviting applications by department: Sales, Customer Service, Accounts, Marketing, Purchasing, IT, Assistants and Warehouse. It markets itself to candidates as a family business with a friendly working environment, career growth opportunities and employee benefits. No specific current open roles or headcount target could be verified from this page; treat as Not verified beyond the general hiring channel existing.
marketPosition: Valley Northern positions itself as a specialist pharmacy and healthcare packaging, disposables and dispensers wholesaler serving hospital pharmacies, GPs, community pharmacies, wholesalers, dentists, vets, ambulance trusts and care homes across the UK, with next working day delivery as a core differentiator since 2002. Its own customer logo carousel names the NHS, BUPA, HCA Healthcare, Spire Healthcare, Nuffield, Numark, the MOD and the RAF among users of its products, though these are supplier published customer references rather than independently confirmed contracts.

Its verified NHS Supply Chain presence, Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions, starting 4 August 2026, sits alongside larger, better known medical device names on the same 40 supplier framework, such as Philips, GE Medical Systems, Welch Allyn and Draeger; Valley Northern's own product range is weighted toward packaging, dispensers and disposables rather than the diagnostic devices most of that framework covers, so its specific lot or lots on it were not independently confirmed in this session and are Not verified.
It holds ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 accreditation and a Cyber Essentials certificate, evidenced by PDFs linked from its own site footer.
deepDive.interview: Worth knowing before a conversation with this company: it is a genuinely small, closely held family operation, not a group subsidiary, so questions about ownership structure or a head office in another country will not land; decision making authority likely sits with the five Pittock directors rather than a wider corporate hierarchy. Its news is product and framework led rather than financial, so ask about its position on the new Total Patient Assessment Device Solutions framework, live from 4 August 2026, and which of the five lots it actually supplies into, since that could not be confirmed independently here. Also worth probing gently: which Pittock currently holds the top operational role, since the website's own team page anonymises this behind department graphics.

deepDive.lede: Vernacare made two significant moves within weeks of each other in early 2026: on 2 March 2026 it sold its Harm Reduction business, eXchange, to Orion Medical Supplies while striking an exclusive deal for Orion to source all its sharps containers from Vernacare, then on 7 April 2026 it acquired Eakin Surgical Limited from Eakin Healthcare Group, continuing a buy-and-build run that also took in Frontier Medical's Infection Prevention business in 2020, Robinson Healthcare in 2021 and Splice Cast Limited in 2023. Worth knowing before a meeting: the company is reshaping its portfolio in real time, trimming harm reduction while building out surgical solutions.

press.text: Vernacare announced the appointment of Alex Hodges as Chief Executive Officer, bringing prior experience from Owens and Minor, Halyard Health and Kimberly-Clark.

Orion Medical Supplies acquired Vernacare's Harm Reduction business, known as eXchange, with Vernacare and Orion entering an exclusive partnership under which Orion will source all its sharps containers from Vernacare.

H.I.G. Capital-backed Vernacare completed the acquisition of Eakin Surgical Limited from Eakin Healthcare Group, a manufacturer of single-use surgical instruments including suction products and sterile procedure solutions; press coverage frames this as continuing a buy-and-build strategy that previously took in Frontier Medical's Infection Prevention business in 2020, Robinson Healthcare in 2021 and Splice Cast Limited in 2023.

hiring: Vernacare's own careers page describes the company as making a difference in healthcare, with vacancies also mirrored on third-party job boards, Reed, Glassdoor, CV-Library, Indeed, at the time of this check. Specific current vacancy titles, numbers or locations were not read in detail in this session and are not reported here; a rep wanting live openings should check the careers page directly.
marketPosition: Vernacare positions itself around three segments: Infection Prevention, Clinical Waste Management and Surgical Solutions, per its own website navigation and about page. It describes itself as a pioneer of single-use infectious waste disposal systems, manufacturing from two sites in the North West of England plus a Toronto, Canada base, serving more than 65 countries. It is a confirmed NHS Supply Chain framework supplier; the specific frameworks and lots are already captured elsewhere in this supplier's frameworks array and were not re-verified here, per the standing instruction not to duplicate that work.

The March 2026 divestment of its Harm Reduction, eXchange, business to Orion Medical Supplies, alongside the April 2026 acquisition of Eakin Surgical, suggests active portfolio reshaping under H.I.G. Capital ownership: narrowing out of harm reduction, needle and syringe provision, while building depth in surgical instruments and infection prevention. This is a live strategic direction, not a stable long-run position, and should be treated as current state rather than settled.
deepDive.interview: Given the pace of change, a rep meeting Vernacare should ask directly what the Eakin Surgical acquisition of 7 April 2026 means for their surgical solutions range and sales structure, and confirm whether the harm reduction exit to Orion on 2 March 2026 has any bearing on categories relevant to your own conversation, since that product line has left the business. It is also worth probing who currently owns commercial and NHS account relationships following two changes in a matter of weeks, as the four Companies House directors, Hall, Hodges, Morris, Wadhams, may not map neatly onto day-to-day commercial contacts you would actually deal with.

deepDive.tagline: French, family-owned since 1962 and still independent: no private equity, no listing · UK subsidiary at Swindon since 1973, under a new general manager since 1 January 2026
deepDive.lede: The thing worth knowing before this interview: Vygon UK changed hands at the top on 1 January 2026, and the new general manager is the man who was its finance director. Dale Keegan joined in August 2016 and was chief financial officer until the end of 2025; the group's own announcement says he takes over from Les Davies, who had run the subsidiary for twenty years and moves to developing Vygon's principal markets. Companies House shows the same switch as register events six weeks later: Keegan appointed a director on 1 February 2026, Davies resigned the same day. Underneath that, the UK trading position is unusually legible. Vygon is a named supplier on 15 NHS Supply Chain frameworks confirmed against the briefs, four of which started during 2026, and one of which, Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets, expires on 30 September 2026, six weeks from this record being written. A new commercial leader with a retender landing in his first year is the shape of the conversation you are walking into.

prose: No UK turnover figure can be read for this company. Vygon (U.K.) Limited (Companies House 01131530) files full accounts, most recently for the year ended 31 December 2025, filed on 10 June 2026, but they are filed as a 29-page PDF with no tagged figures, so there is nothing to read. Third-party company-data sites do publish a UK turnover for Vygon, derived by picking a line off that PDF. This record does not use it: identifying the turnover line by position is a guess about which number is turnover, and a wrong turnover against a named company is exactly the error this Hub refuses to make. The figures below are the group's, as the group itself publishes them, and they are not a proxy for UK trading.

Vygon's own key-figures page gives group turnover of €423 million for 2025. Its press releases through the first half of 2026 give €417.9 million for 2024, with 81% of that earned outside France. That is growth of roughly 1.2% year on year in euros, which for a private, family-held manufacturer with 11 factories is a holding pattern rather than a story, and it is worth reading alongside where the company is actually spending: the February 2026 Stiletto acquisition was explicitly aimed at the United States, not Europe.

Vygon SA is private and French, so there is no annual report, no investor call and no tagged filing to read. Everything above comes from the company's own published statements, which is a weaker source class than a filing and is labelled as such. Earlier years are not plotted because no Vygon-published figure for them was read in this session.

ownership: Vygon is a family company, founded in 1962 by Pierre Simonet. The group's own history page tells the story: he was a hospital patient, saw what sterilisation was costing staff, and went away to make single-use kit instead. It is still headquartered at 8 rue de Paris, Ecouen, north of Paris. It describes itself in every 2026 press release as "a family company" and "a mid-sized business", and nothing found in this session contradicts that: there is no listing, no private-equity holder and no announced sale process. That independence is the company's own stated position, and "independence, optimism and humanism" is the group's headline about itself. For a rep it is the practical difference between a business that answers to a family board and one that answers to quarterly guidance.

The UK entity is Vygon (U.K.) Limited, company number 01131530, incorporated 28 August 1973 and confirmed active at Companies House on 18/08/2026, registered at The Pierre Simonet Building, V Park, Gateway North, Latham Road, Swindon, Wiltshire SN25 4DL. Its registered activity is SIC 46460, wholesale of pharmaceutical goods: a sales and distribution entity, not a manufacturing one; the group's 11 factories are in Europe, the US and Colombia. The building is named after the founder.

The UK company's sole person with significant control is Vygon SAS of Ecouen, notified on 1 June 2016, holding 75% or more of the shares, registered at the Pontoise register of trade and companies under B325241750. That is the whole ownership chain: French parent, UK subsidiary, no intermediate holding company and no third-party investor on the register.

deepDive.peopleNote: The Companies House entries above are statutory register facts. Where this record says one person took over from another it is quoting Vygon's own announcement of 7 January 2026, not inferring succession from the register. Beyond the general manager, the UK commercial leadership could not be verified: Vygon UK's own page titled "Meet the Senior Leadership Team" (read 18/08/2026) describes the business units and names no individuals at all. Treat sales-director and business-unit-head names as Not verified, and confirm them nearer the interview.

press.text: Vygon announces Dale Keegan as general manager of its UK subsidiary, effective 1 January 2026. Keegan, with the company since August 2016 and CFO until the end of 2025, takes over from Les Davies, who moves to developing Vygon's principal markets. The release sets his brief as "driving growth across the NHS and the private sector".
NHS Supply Chain's Needlefree Connection Systems and Associated Products framework starts, running to 25 January 2028, with Vygon among 16 named suppliers.

Vygon acquires Stiletto® and its patented SlipStream™ insertion system from Avia Vascular of Salt Lake City, its first entry into the extended-dwell catheter segment. Financial details were not disclosed. The stated aim is US growth: the group calls North America "the world's largest and most dynamic market for midline and extended-dwell catheters".

NHS Supply Chain's Central Venous Catheters and Associated Products framework starts, running to 22 March 2028, with Vygon among 18 named suppliers, one of the narrowest supplier fields Vygon sits on.
NHS Supply Chain's Single Use Theatre Protective Wear and Related Consumables framework starts, running to 25 May 2029, with Vygon among 29 named suppliers.

Vygon Corporation receives Health Canada approval to commercialise Stiletto™, and appoints NIPRO Canada as national distributor. Four months after the acquisition, the extended-dwell line is still being rolled out in North America rather than Europe.
NHS Supply Chain's Syringes, Needles and Associated Products framework starts, running to 30 June 2029, with Vygon among 53 named suppliers.

hiring: No open-vacancy count could be verified. Vygon UK's careers page at vygon.co.uk/value-life/careers/ carries a "View our current vacancies" panel that is loaded by script and returned nothing readable in this session, and group roles are advertised through a separate careers portal. So this is Not verified rather than zero. What the careers page does say, and it is worth reading before an interview: "many of our senior team members started their Vygon journey from entry-level roles, and in many cases have been with the company for more than 20 years". The new general manager, a decade in and promoted from CFO, is that claim in practice.
marketPosition: Vygon calls itself "a world leader in the neonatology and vascular management clinical specialties" in its own press releases. That is the company's own description and no independently verified market share exists for it in any source read here, so none is stated. The one thing the group does quantify about itself is volume: 210 million medical devices produced a year, sold in more than 120 countries through 26 subsidiaries and 400 distributors, with 183 patents filed.

The verifiable measure of UK position is the NHS Supply Chain footprint: named supplier on 15 frameworks, confirmed against NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs, and the pattern in them is tight rather than broad. Vygon appears in intravenous cannula, central venous catheters, extension sets and lines, IV accessories and pressure monitoring, needle-free connection systems, infusion pumps and administration sets, syringes and needles, blood collection devices, enteral feeding and bile bags, airway management, procedure packs, single-use theatre protective wear, pulse oximetry and capnography, patient monitoring, and maternity/obstetrics. That is one clinical story, the line into the patient and what runs through it, sold across fifteen buying routes, not a general-consumables catalogue.

Two of those fields are narrow enough to matter in an interview. Central Venous Catheters names 18 suppliers and Needle-free Connection Systems names 16, against 53 on syringes and needles and 57 on maternity. Where the field is small, framework presence is closer to a competitive position; where it is large, it is closer to a licence to quote.

The UK business also runs Vygon Vet, a veterinary consumables division of Vygon (UK) Ltd with over 20 years' trading, at vygonvet.co.uk. It is a genuine second channel out of the same Swindon operation and is easy to miss.
deepDive.interview: Three things are fair game and all three are sourced. First, the framework that runs out: Infusion Pumps and Administration Sets and Associated Products expires on 30 September 2026, six weeks after this record was written, and asking how the team is preparing for the retender shows you have read the award record rather than the website. Second, the leadership change: a general manager who came from the CFO's chair on 1 January 2026, after twenty years of the same predecessor, will have a view on what he wants done differently, so ask it directly rather than dancing round it. Third, the geography of the growth: the Stiletto acquisition and its Health Canada approval both point at North America, so a question about what the UK gets from the group's investment plan is a serious one. And know how this company sells: clinical nurse advisors, in-service training, competency sign-off and the Campus Vygon education platform are the delivery model, so a candidate who talks only about price per unit is answering the wrong question.

background.heading: Ownership and parent
background.text: Össur's listed parent entity was renamed Embla Medical hf in April 2024 (ticker EMBLA, Nasdaq Copenhagen). 'Össur' continues as the operating/product brand and UK subsidiary name (OSSUR UK LTD, confirmed on NHS Supply Chain); College Park and Streifeneder are separate Embla Medical acquisitions, NOT Össur products, and should not be folded into this record. Össur divested its compression-therapy business (Gibaud Group, acquired 2006) to Innothera in September 2020 -- do not add a Compression product family, that segment is no longer Össur's. Exos thermoformable bracing is NOT Össur-owned -- it belongs to Enovis (formerly DJO Global), a direct competitor.
